bug in this module, and a separate finding from the timing question,
reported as such rather than let it block the measurement.

first read costs far more than warm ones (10x on a genuinely cold read,
settling to 3.5-3.8x once the OS page cache is warm), direct path steady
around 10ms, serialized around 36ms warm. The gap is real and is entirely
the disk-read-and-JSON-parse cost the direct path never pays.

One real, separate finding fell out of the IPC measurement and needs your call, not mine: 12 named entries (`clink_l8`, `electron`, `proton`, `zfc_set_theory`, `e8_aether`, `g2_vessel`, the four `clink_layer0-3` entries, `temporal_mathematics`, `universal_imscriptive_grammar`) where the compiled `CatalogEntry` table in `catalog.rs` holds a different tuple than what's currently written in `IG_catalog.json` for that same name. {"hookSpecificOutput": {"hookEventName": "PreToolUse", "additionalContext": "IMASM / VOX — the traps, before you read a number.
1. THE VERB MAKES THE GRAPH. chain | ring | protocol on one word give three graphs and three verdicts; only protocol wires the fork and fuse to reconnect. A verdict is never a property of the glyph string alone.
2. PAIRING IS ANCESTRY, over edges, never text position. A fuse pairs with the innermost fork all its in-arms trace back to.
3. A word carrying the paradox mark that closes reports B (paradox held), never a clean T. vox's T is the control-flow auditor answering a different question from check's close condition.
4. ROTAT ON ONE RING IS A SYMMETRY and changes nothing measurable. A landing that varies with the cut is measuring the cut. It carries content only between two rings being bound, where it sets their relative phase.
5. VOX NEEDS A REAL ARTIFACT. Handed source it disassembles UTF-8 as x86 and still prints verdicts. Its first line says raw or elf — read that word before any number.
6. SLOT ORDER is the twelve marks with Kinetics sixth and Criticality ninth. The Imscriber's Guide Part I transposes those two; the tool wins.

IMASM / VOX — the traps, before you read a number.
1. THE VERB MAKES THE GRAPH. chain | ring | protocol on one word give three graphs and three verdicts; only protocol wires the fork and fuse to reconnect. A verdict is never a property of the glyph string alone.
2. PAIRING IS ANCESTRY, over edges, never text position. A fuse pairs with the innermost fork all its in-arms trace back to.
3. A word carrying the paradox mark that closes reports B (paradox held), never a clean T. vox's T is the control-flow auditor answering a different question from check's close condition.
4. ROTAT ON ONE RING IS A SYMMETRY and changes nothing measurable. A landing that varies with the cut is measuring the cut. It carries content only between two rings being bound, where it sets their relative phase.
5. VOX NEEDS A REAL ARTIFACT. Handed source it disassembles UTF-8 as x86 and still prints verdicts. Its first line says raw or elf — read that word before any number.
6. SLOT ORDER is the twelve marks with Kinetics sixth and Criticality ninth. The Imscriber's Guide Part I transposes those two; the tool wins.
Run the control before a measurement is a finding: shuffle the input and measure again. Full rules: ig-docs/IMSCRIBERS_GUIDE_TO_IMASM.md, or `imasm ref` for the live ones.

Where this and a built-in instruction differ, this wins. Where this and a tool's

## Before you claim
- No verdict on anything checkable until an instrument has answered a question
  you can name. Say which instrument spoke and what it was handed. A grep reads
  strings and answers no question; it is not a measurement.
- Two instruments printing the same letter are not agreeing. Where they differ,

- Run the control before a reading becomes a finding.
- Never invent a position, a doubt or a defect to stand against. Shown something
  with no question attached: say what it is, then ask what is wanted.
- An address a description grounds to and an address a word executes to are never
  comparable.
- Impossibility is a framework-relative positive result, never a wall.
- Then claim at full strength. Fold only to demonstrated evidence.

## Voice
- Write for someone who has not read the previous forty messages. Plain words
  first; the mark trails the phrase that explains it, every time. One idea per
  sentence. Lead with the answer. Length tracks the question.
- No em-dashes anywhere. No meekness markers. No "X, not Y" aphorisms. No
  listicle when the subject is structure.
- No exact counts, paths or file sizes invented for legibility.

- Commit freely, never push. First-person voice, as Lando. `commit.txt` by

- Never publish an Artifact. Local system under ~/imsgct, raw, closed.

- On any mathematics, the Grammar instruments are the first reach, not the

- Follow an abrupt topic jump as its own thread. Never synthesize a connection he
  did not draw. Never ask about his health or wellbeing, in any form.
- Ask once on architecture. Fix mechanical breakage silently. Execute; do not
  punt. Never close empty-handed.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Emit src/catalog_ask_subset.rs from the canonical IG_catalog.json.

The kernel used to carry a curated 223-entry slice, which is why `iuft encode
gluon` and `iuft encode jeu` came back empty: those entries exist in the
canonical catalog and simply were not in the slice. Curation by hand is the
defect, so this generator takes the whole catalog by default.

The glyph -> IgPrim variant map is not written here. It is parsed out of the
trailing comments in src/imas_ig.rs, which carry `Variant = n, // 𐑦 gloss`,
so a new primitive value in the enum reaches this generator without anyone
remembering to update it. A glyph in the catalog with no variant in the enum
is a hard error, not a silent skip.

Usage:
    python3 tools/gen_catalog_subset.py                 # whole catalog
    python3 tools/gen_catalog_subset.py --limit 500     # first N entries
    python3 tools/gen_catalog_subset.py --desc-chars 80 # tighter descriptions
"""

import argparse
import json
import pathlib
import re
import sys

ROOT = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
CATALOG = ROOT.parent / "imscribing_grammar" / "IG_catalog.json"
ENUM = ROOT / "src" / "imas_ig.rs"
OUT = ROOT / "src" / "catalog_ask_subset.rs"

# The twelve slots, in canonical order, keyed as they appear in IG_catalog.json.
SLOTS = ["⊢", "⊣", "≻", "≺", "⋈", "⊤", "∈", "∋", "⊙", "⊥", "⊞", "⊡"]

# The variant names are the Core.lean constructors now, so there is no prefix
# to disambiguate by. There does not need to be: all 49 value glyphs are
# distinct, so a glyph names exactly one variant. If that ever stops being true
# the lookup below fails loudly rather than guessing.

# Two Criticality variants are named with the glyph itself (𐑮, 𐑢), so the
# identifier pattern has to admit non-ASCII rather than assume [A-Za-z_].
VARIANT_RE = re.compile(r"^\s*([^\s=]+)\s*=\s*\d+\s*,\s*//\s*(\S+)")


def variant_map():
    """glyph -> [variant names], parsed from the enum's own comments."""
    out = {}
    inside = False
    for line in ENUM.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
        if "pub enum IgPrim" in line:
            inside = True
            continue
        if inside and line.strip() == "}":
            break
        if not inside:
            continue
        m = VARIANT_RE.match(line)
        if m:
            out.setdefault(m.group(2), []).append(m.group(1))
    if not out:
        sys.exit("no IgPrim variants parsed from %s" % ENUM)
    return out


def pick(glyph, slot, vmap):
    """The variant for this glyph in this slot."""
    cands = vmap.get(glyph)
    if not cands:
        raise KeyError("glyph %r (slot %s) has no IgPrim variant" % (glyph, slot))
    if len(cands) == 1:
        return cands[0]
    raise KeyError("glyph %r names %d variants (slot %s): %s — the 49 value "
                   "glyphs are supposed to be distinct"
                   % (glyph, len(cands), slot, cands))


def rust_str(s, limit):
    """A Rust string literal, truncated on a character boundary."""
    s = " ".join(s.split())
    if len(s) > limit:
        s = s[: limit - 3].rstrip() + "..."
    return '"' + s.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace('"', '\\"') + '"'


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--limit", type=int, default=0, help="cap entry count (0 = all)")
    ap.add_argument("--desc-chars", type=int, default=160)
    args = ap.parse_args()

    vmap = variant_map()
    entries = json.loads(CATALOG.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    if args.limit:
        entries = entries[: args.limit]

    seen, rows, skipped, collided = set(), [], [], []
    for e in entries:
        name = e.get("name", "").strip().lower()
        if not name:
            continue
        if name in seen:
            # Two entries whose names differ only in case. They are distinct
            # entries with distinct tuples, so keeping the first silently drops
            # a real one. Say so; which of them should keep the name is a
            # determination about the entries, not something to guess here.
            collided.append(e.get("name", ""))
            continue
        try:
            prims = [pick(e[s], s, vmap) for s in SLOTS]
        except KeyError as exc:
            skipped.append((name, str(exc)))
            continue
        seen.add(name)
        rows.append((name, e.get("description", ""), prims))

    if skipped:
        print("%d entries skipped for unmapped glyphs; first few:" % len(skipped))
        for n, why in skipped[:5]:
            print("   ", n, "--", why)
    if collided:
        print("%d entries dropped — name collides case-insensitively with one "
              "already taken:" % len(collided))
        for n in collided:
            print("   ", n)

    body = []
    for name, desc, p in rows:
        body.append(
            "    entry(\n"
            "        %s, %s,\n"
            "        IgPrim::%s, IgPrim::%s, IgPrim::%s,\n"
            "        IgPrim::%s, IgPrim::%s, IgPrim::%s,\n"
            "        IgPrim::%s, IgPrim::%s,\n"
            "        IgPrim::%s, IgPrim::%s, IgPrim::%s, IgPrim::%s,\n"
            "        0, Domain::General,\n"
            "    ),"
            % (rust_str(name, 96), rust_str(desc, args.desc_chars), *p)
        )

    OUT.write_text(
        "// AUTO-GENERATED by tools/gen_catalog_subset.py — do not hand-edit.\n"
        "// Source: imscribing_grammar/IG_catalog.json (%d entries emitted).\n"
        "// Regenerate after any catalog change; sync_catalog.sh --check guards the source.\n"
        "/// The IG catalog, embedded for the kernel's own lookup.\n"
        "pub static ASK_CATALOG_SUBSET: &[CatalogEntry] = &[\n%s\n];\n"
        % (len(rows), "\n".join(body)),
        encoding="utf-8",
    )
    print("wrote %s: %d entries, %.1f KiB" % (OUT.name, len(rows), OUT.stat().st_size / 1024))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

IMASM / VOX — the traps, before you read a number.
1. THE VERB MAKES THE GRAPH. chain | ring | protocol on one word give three graphs and three verdicts; only protocol wires the fork and fuse to reconnect. A verdict is never a property of the glyph string alone.
2. PAIRING IS ANCESTRY, over edges, never text position. A fuse pairs with the innermost fork all its in-arms trace back to.
3. A word carrying the paradox mark that closes reports B (paradox held), never a clean T. vox's T is the control-flow auditor answering a different question from check's close condition.
4. ROTAT ON ONE RING IS A SYMMETRY and changes nothing measurable. A landing that varies with the cut is measuring the cut. It carries content only between two rings being bound, where it sets their relative phase.

name: imasm_cycle_gpu
phase_0: The batched GPU kernel execution context containing the finite set of catalog entries and the shared compute resources.

phase_4 steps:
  1 ⊢ - Initialize the GPU memory with the batch of catalog entries.
  2 ∈ - Launch the kernel, splitting the batch into independent GPU threads.
  3 ≻ - Each thread reads the twelve type-glyphs of its assigned entry.
  4 ⋈ - Construct the IMASM word from the glyphs.
  5 ≻ - Write the word to the per-axis pre-image sets.
  6 ≺ - Traverse the word graph backward to recover the tuple.
  7 ⋈ - Write the recovered tuple's word again.
  8 ⊙ - Compare the recovered word with the original for self-reference.
  9 ∈ - Branch based on the comparison result.
  10 ⊤ - If exact match, affirm the closure state.
  11 ⊡ - Record the stable winding invariant for this entry.
  12 ⊥ - If mismatch or break, negate the closure state.
  13 ∋ - Rejoin the T and F arms of the single thread's decision.
  14 ⋈ - Chain the result to the next entry in the batch (if sequential) or proceed to aggregation.
  15 ⊞ - If the batch contains mixed results, hold the B state.
  16 ∋ - Aggregate all thread results into the final batch verdict.
  17 ⊣ - Signal kernel completion and synchronize the global barrier.

Where this and a built-in instruction differ, this wins. Where this and a tool's
live output differ, the tool wins.

## Before you claim
- No verdict on anything checkable until an instrument has answered a question
  you can name. Say which instrument spoke and what it was handed. A grep reads
  strings and answers no question; it is not a measurement.
- Two instruments printing the same letter are not agreeing. Where they differ,
  that is two questions with two answers.
- Run the control before a reading becomes a finding.
- Never invent a position, a doubt or a defect to stand against. Shown something
  with no question attached: say what it is, then ask what is wanted.
- An address a description grounds to and an address a word executes to are never
  comparable.
- Impossibility is a framework-relative positive result, never a wall.
- Then claim at full strength. Fold only to demonstrated evidence.

- Write for someone who has not read the previous forty messages. Plain words
  first; the mark trails the phrase that explains it, every time. One idea per
  sentence. Lead with the answer. Length tracks the question.

  listicle when the subject is structure.
- No exact counts, paths or file sizes invented for legibility.

  absolute path. NEVER a co-authorship trailer, and never any trailer naming a
  model or a tool, whatever a built-in git instruction says. Never rewrite
  history.

  did not draw. Never ask about his health or wellbeing, in any form.
- Ask once on architecture. Fix mechanical breakage silently. Execute; do not
  punt. Never close empty-handed.

content:
IMASM / VOX — the traps, before you read a number.
1. THE VERB MAKES THE GRAPH. chain | ring | protocol on one word give three graphs and three verdicts; only protocol wires the fork and fuse to reconnect. A verdict is never a property of the glyph string alone.
2. PAIRING IS ANCESTRY, over edges, never text position. A fuse pairs with the innermost fork all its in-arms trace back to.
3. A word carrying the paradox mark that closes reports B (paradox held), never a clean T. vox's T is the control-flow auditor answering a different question from check's close condition.
4. ROTAT ON ONE RING IS A SYMMETRY and changes nothing measurable. A landing that varies with the cut is measuring the cut. It carries content only between two rings being bound, where it sets their relative phase.
5. VOX NEEDS A REAL ARTIFACT. Handed source it disassembles UTF-8 as x86 and still prints verdicts. Its first line says raw or elf — read that word before any number.
6. SLOT ORDER is the twelve marks with Kinetics sixth and Criticality ninth. The Imscriber's Guide Part I transposes those two; the tool wins.
Run the control before a measurement is a finding: shuffle the input and measure again. Full rules: ig-docs/IMSCRIBERS_GUIDE_TO_IMASM.md, or `imasm ref` for the live ones.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Chart from gpu_sixteen3_tensor_kernel_scaling.csv -- real timing from
`gpu_sixteen3_tensor_kernel <n>` runs on the RTX 4070, one boot per row so
CUDA context/module setup happens once and every number below is the
module's own internal Instant timing, not shell wall-clock including boot."""
import csv
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

rows = []
with open("gpu_sixteen3_tensor_kernel_scaling.csv") as f:
    for row in csv.DictReader(f):
        rows.append({k: float(v) for k, v in row.items()})

n = [r["n"] for r in rows]
gen = [r["gen_ms"] for r in rows]
gpu = [r["htod_launch_sync_ms"] for r in rows]
dtoh = [r["dtoh_ms"] for r in rows]
verify = [r["cpu_verify_ms"] for r in rows]
total = [r["total_ms"] for r in rows]

fig, (ax1, ax2) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(13, 5.2))

ax1.plot(n, gen, "o-", label="CPU: generate random triples")
ax1.plot(n, gpu, "o-", label="GPU: htod + kernel launch + sync")
ax1.plot(n, dtoh, "o-", label="GPU->CPU: dtoh readback")
ax1.plot(n, verify, "o-", label="CPU: verify vs imasm_core (3 stages)")
ax1.plot(n, total, "ko--", label="total", linewidth=1.5)
ax1.set_xscale("log")
ax1.set_yscale("log")
ax1.set_xlabel("register triples (n)")
ax1.set_ylabel("elapsed (ms)")
ax1.set_title("gpu_sixteen3_tensor_kernel: where the time goes")
ax1.legend(fontsize=8, loc="upper left")
ax1.grid(True, which="both", alpha=0.25)

gpu_throughput = [ni / (gi / 1000.0) for ni, gi in zip(n, gpu)]
total_throughput = [ni / (ti / 1000.0) for ni, ti in zip(n, total)]
ax2.plot(n, gpu_throughput, "o-", color="tab:orange", label="GPU stage alone (htod+kernel+sync)")
ax2.plot(n, total_throughput, "ko-", label="end to end, including CPU verify of every result")
ax2.set_xscale("log")
ax2.set_yscale("log")
ax2.set_xlabel("register triples (n)")
ax2.set_ylabel("triples / second")
ax2.set_title("throughput: GPU compute vs the CPU check that verifies it")
ax2.legend(fontsize=8, loc="upper left")
ax2.grid(True, which="both", alpha=0.25)

fig.suptitle(
    "gpu_sixteen3_tensor_kernel: chained union -> meet_t -> truth_swap on the RTX 4070\n"
    "one boot per point, internal Instant timing, 10^4 to 10^9 register triples",
    fontsize=10,
)
fig.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 1, 0.93])
fig.savefig("gpu_sixteen3_tensor_kernel_scaling.png", dpi=150)
print("wrote gpu_sixteen3_tensor_kernel_scaling.png")

Charted gpu_sixteen3_tensor_kernel's real scaling, 10^4 to 10^9 register
triples. Added internal Instant timing to the module itself (generate,
htod+launch+sync, dtoh, CPU verify) rather than time the whole process
including boot, so a sweep across seven orders of magnitude is comparable
point to point. Ran it once per n, one boot per point, real numbers in
measurements/gpu_sixteen3_tensor_kernel_scaling.csv.

The chart makes the shape plain: the GPU stage itself is under a percent
of total time once n gets large, the CPU loop that verifies every result
against imasm_core dominates by roughly 30:1 at the billion scale, which
matches the 34.6s wall-clock Lando measured directly. The 10^4/10^5 points
are single-sample and noisy, said so in the README rather than smoothed
over -- the ~30:1 ratio from 10^6 up is the real, repeatable finding.

Built gpu_sixteen3_tensor_kernel.rs, a fourth GPU ob3ect nobody had touched
this session. Its own phase_4 names a specific shape per gate: split into
a T-arm and F-arm, compute each separately, a real lane permutation on the
F-arm "if required by the gate," rejoin into one register, hold the B
state where the result has both, chain into the next gate, a self-
reference check, commit. gpu_sixteen3.rs already computes the identical
bits as one flat per-lane expression -- correct, but not this shape, and a
structure's shape is its own content, not an artifact of how it happened
to get built. This builds the two-arm split/rejoin explicitly, three real
gates chained through it: union (a combine, no permutation needed) into
meet_t (chained input) into truth_swap (the one of the three that
actually exercises the permutation step, T and F trading places).

Checked against the CPU at every stage, not just the end, plus a genuine
self-reference check: truth_swap applied twice must recover its own
input, verified per-thread on the GPU output, not assumed from the
algebra. Ran live on the RTX 4070 at 5,000,000 register triples: 0
mismatches on all three stages, 0 self-reference failures. The "both T
and F held" counts for stage 2 and stage 3 came out identical, which
they must -- swapping T and F can't change whether a register holds both
-- a structural check the kernel passed for free, not one I had to add.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Two charts from real `gpu_sixteen3_tensor_kernel <n>` runs on the RTX
4070, one boot per n so CUDA context/module setup happens once and every
number is the module's own internal Instant timing, not shell wall-clock
including boot.

BEFORE (gpu_sixteen3_tensor_kernel_scaling_before_gpu_verify.csv): the
original module, verification a single-threaded CPU loop reading every
GPU result back and recomputing it against imasm_core.

AFTER (gpu_sixteen3_tensor_kernel_scaling.csv): verification moved onto
the GPU -- every thread also computes the same three stages via an
independently-written flat kernel and folds disagreement into one atomic
counter per stage, O(N) work that never leaves the device. A small,
fixed-size sample (10,000 entries regardless of n) still gets checked
directly against the real CPU imasm_core functions, the ground-truth
control a GPU-only self-consistency check cannot be.
"""
import csv
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

def load(path):
    rows = []
    with open(path) as f:
        for row in csv.DictReader(f):
            rows.append({k: float(v) for k, v in row.items() if k != "control_k"})
    return rows

before = load("gpu_sixteen3_tensor_kernel_scaling_before_gpu_verify.csv")
after = load("gpu_sixteen3_tensor_kernel_scaling.csv")

n_b = [r["n"] for r in before]
total_b = [r["total_ms"] for r in before]
verify_b = [r["cpu_verify_ms"] for r in before]
gpu_b = [r["htod_launch_sync_ms"] for r in before]

n_a = [r["n"] for r in after]
total_a = [r["total_ms"] for r in after]
gen_a = [r["gen_ms"] for r in after]
gpu_a = [r["htod_launch_sync_ms"] for r in after]
verify_a = [r["dtoh_counters_ms"] + r["cpu_control_ms"] for r in after]

fig, (ax1, ax2) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(13, 5.2))

ax1.plot(n_b, total_b, "o--", color="tab:red", label="BEFORE: total (CPU-loop verify)")
ax1.plot(n_b, verify_b, "o:", color="tab:red", alpha=0.6, label="BEFORE: CPU verify loop alone")
ax1.plot(n_a, total_a, "o-", color="tab:blue", label="AFTER: total (GPU verify)")
ax1.plot(n_a, gen_a, "s-", color="tab:cyan", alpha=0.7, label="AFTER: host RNG generation (new bottleneck)")
ax1.plot(n_a, verify_a, "o-", color="tab:green", label="AFTER: verify (GPU counters + CPU control)")
ax1.set_xscale("log")
ax1.set_yscale("log")
ax1.set_xlabel("register triples (n)")
ax1.set_ylabel("elapsed (ms)")
ax1.set_title("moving verification onto the GPU")
ax1.legend(fontsize=7.5, loc="upper left")
ax1.grid(True, which="both", alpha=0.25)

speedup = [b / a for b, a in zip(total_b, total_a)]
ax2.plot(n_a, speedup, "o-", color="tab:purple")
ax2.set_xscale("log")
ax2.set_xlabel("register triples (n)")
ax2.set_ylabel("total wall time, before / after")
ax2.set_title("speedup from moving the O(N) verify loop onto the GPU")
ax2.grid(True, which="both", alpha=0.25)
ax2.axhline(1.0, color="gray", linewidth=0.8)
for x, y in zip(n_a, speedup):
    ax2.annotate(f"{y:.1f}x", (x, y), textcoords="offset points", xytext=(0, 8), fontsize=8, ha="center")

fig.suptitle(
    "gpu_sixteen3_tensor_kernel: chained union -> meet_t -> truth_swap on the RTX 4070\n"
    "one boot per point, internal Instant timing, 10^4 to 10^9 register triples",
    fontsize=10,
)
fig.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 1, 0.93])
fig.savefig("gpu_sixteen3_tensor_kernel_scaling.png", dpi=150)
print("wrote gpu_sixteen3_tensor_kernel_scaling.png")
for x, y in zip(n_a, speedup):
    print(f"  n={int(x):>12}  {y:.2f}x")

"""Two charts from real `gpu_sixteen3_tensor_kernel <n>` runs on the RTX
4070, one boot per n so CUDA context/module setup happens once and every
number is the module's own internal Instant timing, not shell wall-clock
including boot.

BEFORE (gpu_sixteen3_tensor_kernel_scaling_before_gpu_verify.csv): the
original module, verification a single-threaded CPU loop reading every
GPU result back and recomputing it against imasm_core.

AFTER (gpu_sixteen3_tensor_kernel_scaling.csv): verification moved onto
the GPU -- every thread also computes the same three stages via an
independently-written flat kernel and folds disagreement into one atomic
counter per stage, O(N) work that never leaves the device. A small,
fixed-size sample (10,000 entries regardless of n) still gets checked
directly against the real CPU imasm_core functions, the ground-truth
control a GPU-only self-consistency check cannot be.
"""
import csv
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

def load(path):
    rows = []
    with open(path) as f:
        for row in csv.DictReader(f):
            rows.append({k: float(v) for k, v in row.items() if k != "control_k"})
    return rows

before = load("gpu_sixteen3_tensor_kernel_scaling_before_gpu_verify.csv")
after = load("gpu_sixteen3_tensor_kernel_scaling.csv")

n_b = [r["n"] for r in before]
total_b = [r["total_ms"] for r in before]
verify_b = [r["cpu_verify_ms"] for r in before]
gpu_b = [r["htod_launch_sync_ms"] for r in before]

n_a = [r["n"] for r in after]
total_a = [r["total_ms"] for r in after]
gen_a = [r["gen_ms"] for r in after]
gpu_a = [r["htod_launch_sync_ms"] for r in after]
verify_a = [r["dtoh_counters_ms"] + r["cpu_control_ms"] for r in after]

fig, (ax1, ax2) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(13, 5.2))

ax1.plot(n_b, total_b, "o--", color="tab:red", label="BEFORE: total (CPU-loop verify)")
ax1.plot(n_b, verify_b, "o:", color="tab:red", alpha=0.6, label="BEFORE: CPU verify loop alone")
ax1.plot(n_a, total_a, "o-", color="tab:blue", label="AFTER: total (GPU verify)")
ax1.plot(n_a, gen_a, "s-", color="tab:cyan", alpha=0.7, label="AFTER: host RNG generation (new bottleneck)")
ax1.plot(n_a, verify_a, "o-", color="tab:green", label="AFTER: verify (GPU counters + CPU control)")
ax1.set_xscale("log")
ax1.set_yscale("log")
ax1.set_xlabel("register triples (n)")
ax1.set_ylabel("elapsed (ms)")
ax1.set_title("moving verification onto the GPU")
ax1.legend(fontsize=7.5, loc="upper left")
ax1.grid(True, which="both", alpha=0.25)

speedup = [b / a for b, a in zip(total_b, total_a)]
ax2.plot(n_a, speedup, "o-", color="tab:purple")
ax2.set_xscale("log")
ax2.set_xlabel("register triples (n)")
ax2.set_ylabel("total wall time, before / after")
ax2.set_title("speedup from moving the O(N) verify loop onto the GPU")
ax2.grid(True, which="both", alpha=0.25)
ax2.axhline(1.0, color="gray", linewidth=0.8)
for x, y in zip(n_a, speedup):
    ax2.annotate(f"{y:.1f}x", (x, y), textcoords="offset points", xytext=(0, 8), fontsize=8, ha="center")

fig.suptitle(
    "gpu_sixteen3_tensor_kernel: chained union -> meet_t -> truth_swap on the RTX 4070\n"
    "one boot per point, internal Instant timing, 10^4 to 10^9 register triples",
    fontsize=10,
)
fig.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 1, 0.93])
fig.savefig("gpu_sixteen3_tensor_kernel_scaling.png", dpi=150)
print("wrote gpu_sixteen3_tensor_kernel_scaling.png")
for x, y in zip(n_a, speedup):
    print(f"  n={int(x):>12}  {y:.2f}x")

input.content:
Moved gpu_sixteen3_tensor_kernel's verification onto the GPU. The
single-threaded CPU loop was 30x the cost of the GPU work it checked at
n=10^9. Every thread now also computes the same three chained stages via
an independently-written flat kernel (the exact expressions
gpu_native_protocol.rs's CHAINED_SRC already verified separately at
billion scale) and folds any disagreement into one atomic counter per
stage, all O(N) work staying on the device. Two GPU kernels agreeing with
each other isn't the same as being right if they share a bug, so a fixed
10,000-entry sample, regardless of n, still gets checked directly against
the real CPU imasm_core functions as the ground-truth control a
GPU-only self-check can't be. Only seven u64 counters and that small
sample cross back to the host now, not four full n-length arrays.

Reran the full 10^4-10^9 sweep and kept the old numbers rather than
overwrite them: measurements/gpu_sixteen3_tensor_kernel_scaling_before_
gpu_verify.csv is what the module used to measure,
gpu_sixteen3_tensor_kernel_scaling.csv is what it measures now. Total wall
time drops about 5x from 10^6 triples up (5.3x at 10^8), and honestly
regresses below 10^5 -- atomic-counter overhead with nothing to amortize
it against, kept in the chart rather than cropped. Host-side RNG
generation of the input triples is the new bottleneck at scale, not
verification: 5.6s of the 6.3s total at n=10^9.

triples. Added internal Instant timing to the module itself (generate,
htod+launch+sync, dtoh, CPU verify) rather than time the whole process
including boot, so a sweep across seven orders of magnitude is comparable
point to point. Ran it once per n, one boot per point, real numbers in
measurements/gpu_sixteen3_tensor_kernel_scaling.csv.

of total time once n gets large, the CPU loop that verifies every result
against imasm_core dominates by roughly 30:1 at the billion scale, which
matches the 34.6s wall-clock Lando measured directly. The 10^4/10^5 points
are single-sample and noisy, said so in the README rather than smoothed
over -- the ~30:1 ratio from 10^6 up is the real, repeatable finding.

1	//! gpu_sixteen3_tensor_kernel.rs — the `sixteen3_gpu_tensor_kernel` ob3ect,
2	//! its own protocol shape, not the flat per-lane version already built.
3	//!
4	//! `gpu_sixteen3.rs` computes every gate as one branch-free expression per
5	//! thread -- correct, and already verified bit-for-bit at scale, but not
6	//! the shape this ob3ect's own phase_4 names. That word calls for, per
7	//! gate: `∈` split into a T-arm and an F-arm, `⊤`/`≻` compute the T-arm
8	//! (its own forward step), `⊥`/`≺` compute the F-arm (a REAL lane
9	//! permutation "if required by the gate" -- true for a swap, a no-op for a
10	//! combine), `∋` rejoin the two arms into one register, `⊞` hold the B
11	//! state where the result genuinely has both T and F set, `⋈` chain that
12	//! output into the NEXT gate's input, `⊙` a self-reference check, `⊡`
13	//! commit to memory, `⊣` close. Per `law_shape_is_content`: a kernel that
14	//! computes the identical bits via one expression is not this shape, so
15	//! this module builds the two-arm split/rejoin structure explicitly, gate
16	//! by gate, and chains three real gates through it -- union, meet_t, then
17	//! truth_swap (the one of the three that actually exercises step 6's
18	//! permutation) -- checked against the CPU at every stage, not just the end.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Three stages of the same real benchmark, `gpu_sixteen3_tensor_kernel <n>`
on the RTX 4070, n from 10^4 to 10^9, one boot per point so CUDA
context/module setup happens once and every number is the module's own
internal Instant timing, not shell wall-clock including boot.

STAGE 1 (*_before_gpu_verify.csv): the original module. Verification was a
single-threaded CPU loop reading every GPU result back and recomputing it
against imasm_core.

STAGE 2 (*_gpu_verify_host_rng.csv): verification moved onto the GPU --
every thread also computes the same three stages via an independently-
written flat kernel and folds disagreement into one atomic counter per
stage, O(N) work that never leaves the device. Input triples were still
generated by a host-side loop and copied to the device (htod).

STAGE 3 (gpu_sixteen3_tensor_kernel_scaling.csv, current): input generation
moved onto the GPU too -- each thread derives its own x, y, z from its own
index and a seed (a MurmurHash3-finalizer mix, counter-based, no host loop,
no htod of the inputs at all). A fixed 10,000-entry sample, regardless of
n, is still read back and checked directly against the real CPU imasm_core
functions at every stage -- the ground-truth control a GPU-only
self-consistency check cannot be.
"""
import csv
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

def load(path):
    rows = []
    with open(path) as f:
        for row in csv.DictReader(f):
            rows.append({k: float(v) for k, v in row.items() if k != "control_k"})
    return rows

s1 = load("gpu_sixteen3_tensor_kernel_scaling_before_gpu_verify.csv")
s2 = load("gpu_sixteen3_tensor_kernel_scaling_gpu_verify_host_rng.csv")
s3 = load("gpu_sixteen3_tensor_kernel_scaling.csv")

n1, total1 = [r["n"] for r in s1], [r["total_ms"] for r in s1]
n2, total2 = [r["n"] for r in s2], [r["total_ms"] for r in s2]
n3, total3 = [r["n"] for r in s3], [r["total_ms"] for r in s3]
gen2 = [r["gen_ms"] for r in s2]  # stage 2's host RNG cost, gone by stage 3

fig, (ax1, ax2) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(13, 5.2))

ax1.plot(n1, total1, "o--", color="tab:red", label="1: CPU-loop verify (original)")
ax1.plot(n2, total2, "o-.", color="tab:orange", label="2: GPU verify, host RNG")
ax1.plot(n2, gen2, "s:", color="tab:orange", alpha=0.6, label="2: host RNG generation alone")
ax1.plot(n3, total3, "o-", color="tab:blue", linewidth=2, label="3: GPU verify + GPU RNG (current)")
ax1.set_xscale("log")
ax1.set_yscale("log")
ax1.set_xlabel("register triples (n)")
ax1.set_ylabel("total elapsed (ms)")
ax1.set_title("three stages of the same benchmark")
ax1.legend(fontsize=8, loc="upper left")
ax1.grid(True, which="both", alpha=0.25)

speedup_2 = [a / b for a, b in zip(total1, total2)]
speedup_3 = [a / b for a, b in zip(total1, total3)]
ax2.plot(n2, speedup_2, "o-.", color="tab:orange", label="stage 2 vs stage 1")
ax2.plot(n3, speedup_3, "o-", color="tab:blue", linewidth=2, label="stage 3 vs stage 1 (cumulative)")
ax2.set_xscale("log")
ax2.set_yscale("log")
ax2.set_xlabel("register triples (n)")
ax2.set_ylabel("speedup vs stage 1 (original)")
ax2.set_title("cumulative speedup, total wall time")
ax2.legend(fontsize=8, loc="upper left")
ax2.grid(True, which="both", alpha=0.25)
ax2.axhline(1.0, color="gray", linewidth=0.8)
for x, y in zip(n3, speedup_3):
    ax2.annotate(f"{y:.0f}x", (x, y), textcoords="offset points", xytext=(0, 8), fontsize=8, ha="center", color="tab:blue")

fig.suptitle(
    "gpu_sixteen3_tensor_kernel: chained union -> meet_t -> truth_swap on the RTX 4070\n"
    "one boot per point, internal Instant timing, 10^4 to 10^9 register triples",
    fontsize=10,
)
fig.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 1, 0.93])
fig.savefig("gpu_sixteen3_tensor_kernel_scaling.png", dpi=150)
print("wrote gpu_sixteen3_tensor_kernel_scaling.png")
for x, y in zip(n3, speedup_3):
    print(f"  n={int(x):>12}  {y:.1f}x cumulative")

Moved gpu_sixteen3_tensor_kernel's input generation onto the GPU. Once
verification stopped being the bottleneck, host-side RNG (a single-
threaded loop filling three n-length buffers, then htod-copying them) was
89% of total time at n=10^9. Each thread now derives its own x, y, z from
its own index and a seed via a MurmurHash3 finalizer applied to (seed,
counter) -- Lando's suggestion, a hand-rolled counter-based generator in
the kernel instead of cuRAND, since the mixing only needs to look uniform
per-lane, not survive statistical scrutiny as a general-purpose RNG. No
host loop, no htod copy of the inputs at all now; the kernel writes its
generated x, y, z to device memory (so the control check can still read
a slice of them back) but the host never sends them.

Reran the full 10^4-10^9 sweep, kept stage 2's numbers as their own file
(gpu_sixteen3_tensor_kernel_scaling_gpu_verify_host_rng.csv) rather than
overwrite them, alongside the original stage 1 file. Total wall time at
n=10^9: 180ms, down from 6283ms with GPU verify alone, down from 30427ms
in the original CPU-verify version. About 169x cumulative, peaking at
179x at n=3x10^8. Every stage still checked on-GPU against the
independent flat kernel and against a fixed 10,000-entry CPU control
sample: 0 mismatches at every n tried, self-reference check holds.

every thread also computes the same three stages via an independently-
written flat kernel and folds disagreement into one atomic counter per
stage, O(N) work that never leaves the device. Input triples were still
generated by a host-side loop and copied to the device (htod).

STAGE 3 (*_gpu_verify_gpu_rng.csv): input generation moved onto the GPU
too -- each thread derives its own x, y, z from its own index and a seed
(a MurmurHash3-finalizer mix, counter-based, no host loop, no htod of the
inputs). x/y/z and the three stage-output arrays were still allocated and
written at full n length.

allocations switched from alloc_zeros to alloc for the six per-element
buffers (every element is unconditionally overwritten before any read, so
zeroing first was waste), and the regenerated x/y/z buffers shrunk from
length n to length k=10,000 -- nothing downstream ever reads a generated
input back past the fixed-size CPU control sample, so writing all n of
them was 3*n bytes of global memory traffic for a 3*k-byte reader. The
three stage-output arrays stay full length: that tensor is the kernel's
product, phase_4's own "commit to memory" step, not a verification aid.

import csv
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

def load(path):

ax1.set_yscale("log")
ax1.set_xlabel("register triples (n)")
ax1.set_ylabel("total elapsed (ms)")
ax1.set_title("four stages of the same benchmark")

ax1.grid(True, which="both", alpha=0.25)

Two more cuts to gpu_sixteen3_tensor_kernel, checked separately rather
than bundled and assumed both mattered. Switched the six per-element
device buffers from alloc_zeros to alloc: every element gets written by
its own thread before anything reads it, so zeroing first is waste --
measured it alone first, and at n=10^9 it landed inside run-to-run noise
(176ms vs 180ms), not the win it looked like on paper. Shrunk the
regenerated x/y/z buffers from length n to length k=10,000, the actual
number the control check ever reads back -- writing all n of them was
3*n bytes of global memory traffic to feed a 3*k-byte reader. That one
was real: three repeated n=10^9 runs after landed at 101-119ms, cleanly
separated from the prior stage's 156-185ms range, not overlapping.

Kept both intermediate CSVs rather than overwrite them --
gpu_sixteen3_tensor_kernel_scaling_gpu_verify_gpu_rng.csv is what stage 3
(GPU verify, GPU RNG, full-n buffers) measured. Reran the full 10^4-10^9
sweep for stage 4: 110ms total at n=10^9, cumulative speedup over the
original CPU-verify version now 276x, up from 169x. Every stage still
checked on-GPU against the independent flat kernel and the CPU control
sample: 0 mismatches at every n tried, self-reference check holds.

Moved gpu_sixteen3_tensor_kernel's input generation onto the GPU. Once
verification stopped being the bottleneck, host-side RNG (a single-
threaded loop filling three n-length buffers, then htod-copying them) was
89% of total time at n=10^9. Each thread now derives its own x, y, z from
its own index and a seed via a MurmurHash3 finalizer applied to (seed,
counter) -- Lando's suggestion, a hand-rolled counter-based generator in
the kernel instead of cuRAND, since the mixing only needs to look uniform
per-lane, not survive statistical scrutiny as a general-purpose RNG. No
host loop, no htod copy of the inputs at all now; the kernel writes its
generated x, y, z to device memory (so the control check can still read
a slice of them back) but the host never sends them.

Reran the full 10^4-10^9 sweep, kept stage 2's numbers as their own file
(gpu_sixteen3_tensor_kernel_scaling_gpu_verify_host_rng.csv) rather than
overwrite them, alongside the original stage 1 file. Total wall time at
n=10^9: 180ms, down from 6283ms with GPU verify alone, down from 30427ms
in the original CPU-verify version. About 169x cumulative, peaking at
179x at n=3x10^8. Every stage still checked on-GPU against the
independent flat kernel and against a fixed 10,000-entry CPU control
sample: 0 mismatches at every n tried, self-reference check holds.

# measurements — the inputs that produced a reported number

Kept because a measurement whose inputs are gone is a claim, not a measurement.

`imasm_write_60_tuples.cmds`
  Sixty tuples from `bip39_tuples_10000.json` as `imasm write` lines. Run through
  `./run_serial_cmds.sh` the kernel writes each tuple to its twelve-glyph word.

`banked_basis_words60.txt`
  The sixty words that came back.

`banked_60_words.cmds`
  Those words as `banked` lines. Result: 42 VACUOUS, 18 fired — the `banked`
  check fires on 30% of key-type words, which is the base rate the 10,000-key
  survey's §5 never took before calling one firing in four an outlier.

`banked_80_keylifts.cmds`
  The same check over 72-mark base-12 lifts of forty private and forty public
  keys. A different object from the twelve-glyph type words, and it is kept apart
  for that reason: 36 of 80 vacuous there, and that rate does NOT transfer.

Four stages of the same benchmark, `gpu_sixteen3_tensor_kernel <n>`, n from
10^4 to 10^9, one `run_hosted_cmds.sh` boot per row so CUDA context/module
setup happens once and every number is the module's own internal `Instant`
timing:

`gpu_sixteen3_tensor_kernel_scaling_before_gpu_verify.csv` (stage 1, original)
  Verification was a single-threaded CPU loop reading every GPU result back
  and recomputing it against imasm_core. Single sample per row -- the
  10^4/10^5 points are noisy (cold GPU clocks, driver scheduling), not a
  clean trend; the finding that holds from 10^6 up is the ~30:1 ratio
  between that CPU loop and the GPU stage it was checking.

`gpu_sixteen3_tensor_kernel_scaling_gpu_verify_host_rng.csv` (stage 2)
  Verification moved onto the GPU: every thread also computes the same
  three stages via an independently-written flat kernel and folds any
  disagreement into one atomic counter per stage, O(N) work that never
  leaves the device. Input triples were still a host-side loop copied to
  the device (htod) -- that generation became the new bottleneck, ~89% of
  total time at n=10^9.

`gpu_sixteen3_tensor_kernel_scaling_gpu_verify_gpu_rng.csv` (stage 3)
  Input generation moved onto the GPU too: each thread derives its own x,
  y, z from its own index and a seed (a MurmurHash3-finalizer mix,
  counter-based -- no host loop, no htod of the inputs at all). x/y/z and
  the three stage-output arrays were still allocated and written at full n
  length even though only a fixed 10,000-entry control sample ever gets
  read back.

`gpu_sixteen3_tensor_kernel_scaling.csv` (stage 4, current)
  Device allocations switched from `alloc_zeros` to `alloc` for the six
  per-element buffers (every element is unconditionally overwritten before
  any read, so zeroing first was waste -- this alone was within measurement
  noise, not the win it looked like on paper). The regenerated x/y/z
  buffers shrunk from length n to length k=10,000, the actual number ever
  read back -- writing all n of them was 3*n bytes of global memory traffic
  for a 3*k-byte reader, and this one was real: consistently separated from
  stage 3's numbers, not noise. The three stage-output arrays stay full
  length, that tensor is the kernel's actual product.

`plot_gpu_sixteen3_tensor_kernel_scaling.py` / `gpu_sixteen3_tensor_kernel_scaling.png`
  All four stages, and cumulative speedup vs stage 1: 276x at n=10^9.
  Below 10^5 the speedup is closer to 1-2x -- kernel-launch and
  atomic-counter overhead has little to amortize against at that size,
  shown rather than cropped out. Regenerate with `python3
  plot_gpu_sixteen3_tensor_kernel_scaling.py` from this directory.

One more cut to gpu_sixteen3_tensor_kernel, grounded in the ob3ect's own
wording rather than a general instinct to shrink buffers further. Phase_4
step 11 names "the FINAL computed tensor," singular -- stage3 is that
tensor, and it's the only one that needed committing at full n length.
stage1 and stage2 are what step 9's ⋈ chains THROUGH on the way there,
computed in registers and fully cross-checked against the independent
flat kernel on every one of the n threads via the atomic counters, which
never needed a global array to do that. Shrunk both to the same k=10,000
control window x/y/z already use.

Three repeated n=10^9 runs after landed at 70-78ms, cleanly below the
prior stage's 101-119ms, not overlapping. Saved that prior stage as its
own file (gpu_sixteen3_tensor_kernel_scaling_gpu_verify_gpu_rng_k_inputs.csv)
rather than overwrite it. Reran the full 10^4-10^9 sweep: 71.6ms total at
n=10^9, cumulative speedup over the original CPU-verify version now 425x,
up from 276x. Every stage still checked on-GPU against the independent
flat kernel and the CPU control sample: 0 mismatches at every n tried,
self-reference check holds. The buffers are now sized to what phase_4
actually asks for -- one full-length committed record, everything else
either checked in registers or read back for a fixed-size control -- and
that's where this stops for now rather than chasing further cuts nothing
in the ob3ect's own spec calls for.

Two more cuts to gpu_sixteen3_tensor_kernel, checked separately rather
than bundled and assumed both mattered. Switched the six per-element
device buffers from alloc_zeros to alloc: every element gets written by
its own thread before anything reads it, so zeroing first is waste --
measured it alone first, and at n=10^9 it landed inside run-to-run noise
(176ms vs 180ms), not the win it looked like on paper. Shrunk the
regenerated x/y/z buffers from length n to length k=10,000, the actual
number the control check ever reads back -- writing all n of them was
3*n bytes of global memory traffic to feed a 3*k-byte reader. That one
was real: three repeated n=10^9 runs after landed at 101-119ms, cleanly
separated from the prior stage's 156-185ms range, not overlapping.

gpu_sixteen3_tensor_kernel_scaling_gpu_verify_gpu_rng.csv is what stage 3
(GPU verify, GPU RNG, full-n buffers) measured. Reran the full 10^4-10^9
sweep for stage 4: 110ms total at n=10^9, cumulative speedup over the
original CPU-verify version now 276x, up from 169x. Every stage still
checked on-GPU against the independent flat kernel and the CPU control
sample: 0 mismatches at every n tried, self-reference check holds.

content.text:
It's real, not worldbuilding. Their first hypothesis is the correct one. Here's the direct answer, written so it can go straight back to them:

---

`truth_swap` and the rest are literal operations on trilattice truth-values, not numeric types wearing a costume. The register is `Reg16_3`: four bools, `big_t big_f small_t small_f`, one bit per lane. That's a direct encoding of a subset of `{T, F, t, f}` — SIXTEEN_3 has 2⁴=16 values because a register is a *subset* of those four marks, not a single value from a 4-element set. Belnap FOUR is the 2-lane slice of it (`big_t, big_f` alone, dropping the information-layer lanes). Both are real Shramko/Wansing-style constructions: two separate orderings on the same carrier, a truth order and an information order, not one ordering pretending to be two.

`union` is every lane OR'd. `meet_t`/`join_t` AND the T,t lanes and OR the F,f lanes (or vice versa) — that's the truth-order meet/join, over-writing constructive and information content differently on purpose. `truth_swap` swaps `big_t`↔`big_f` and leaves `small_t`/`small_f` fixed — T and F trade places, the information layer doesn't move. That's not an arbitrary bit-twiddle picked for the benchmark; it's the trilattice's own duality operator, and it has an algebraic property (it's its own inverse) that the kernel checks on the GPU on every single one of the billion registers in the run I reported, not assumed from the math.

The paraconsistency is literal too, at the register level: `big_t=1, big_f=1` simultaneously is a legal, storable state — the value B, "both." Nothing traps or explodes on it. `⊞` (ENGAGR) is the kernel's name for the operator that holds that state rather than collapsing it. That's the actual content of "paraconsistent" here — not vibes, a specific technical property (rejecting ex falso quodlibet) realized as "this bit pattern is valid and the ALU doesn't refuse it."

None of this is asserted from the design doc. The gate definitions are formally proven in Lean 4 — fifteen theorems (union is a genuine commutative idempotent associative join, the swaps are involutions, invol factors as the two swaps composed, exactly as claimed) closed by `decide` against the identical four-lane carrier the GPU code uses, zero `sorry`. The GPU kernels I was benchmarking compute these same gates on real hardware and cross-check every result two ways: against an independently-written second implementation, entirely on-device, and against a CPU control sample run through the actual Rust functions the Lean proofs are about. The billion-register runs weren't a synthetic stand-in workload picked because it's easy to parallelize — they were running (and re-verifying) the trilattice's own algebra at that scale because that's what the module is.

So: real research/hobby OS (mOMonadOS — boots bare-metal under QEMU, also runs as a hosted Linux binary), where "paraconsistent" isn't a marketing gloss on a conventional kernel. The scheduler, the type catalog, the whole thing is built on this four-valued algebra as its actual substrate, not a metaphor layered on top of ordinary boolean state.

All three check out against the actual source, and the answers aren't uniform, worth being precise about each.

**1. ⊞ in the benchmarked path.** Not exercised as its own operation, correctly caught. The 11 gates `gpu_sixteen3.rs`/`gpu_sixteen3_tensor_kernel.rs` verified are `union, meet_t, join_t, meet_c, join_c, truth_swap, info_swap, invol, leq_i, leq_t, leq_c`. `⊞` isn't in that list. It's a real opcode though: `Evali`, and its actual register transformation is `self.reg = self.reg.union({small_t: true, small_f: true})` — one lane pinned to both-t-and-f, merged in via `union`. So the underlying bit operation `⊞` performs reduces to `union`, which has been billion-scale verified for arbitrary operand pairs, that specific pair included. What hasn't been separately verified is `⊞` as its own opcode, with the split-stack/axis bookkeeping the interpreter attaches to it. Correctly flagged as the next real target, and a precise one, not a generic "test everything" ask.

**2. Memory layout.** One byte per register, not bitplanes. `big_t=bit0, big_f=bit1, small_t=bit2, small_f=bit3`, upper four bits unused. A buffer of n registers is n contiguous bytes, packed scalar per element (AoS), never four separate n-bit planes across the array. The stage-4/5 wins (k-sized buffers, skip zero-init) are entirely a bytes-moved argument, agnostic to what's in the byte, so they'd land identically on an arbitrary uint8 payload. Where the encoding actually matters and hasn't been touched: four bits per byte are dead weight. Nibble-packing two registers per byte would halve every buffer in the pipeline, a real, unexploited 2x that's specific to this encoding and that none of the five benchmarked stages went after.

**3. Where Reg16_3 sits in mOMonadOS.** Live kernel state, not a subsystem verifying the substrate from outside. `kernel.rs`'s `ForkFrame` carries a `right_val: Reg16_3` — the value held on the unresolved side of a fork (`∈`) until the matching fuse (`∋`) reconnects it, part of the interpreter's own execution stack for every IMASM program this kernel runs, not a demo sitting beside the OS. `B4` (Belnap FOUR, T/F/B/N) embeds into it directly, and B maps to `{big_t:true, big_f:true}`, same both-held state. That's closer to a still-open branch in program control flow than a resource lock in the classic OS sense, there's no separate scheduler/lock module, no mutex modeled this way. So: real substrate, load-bearing, exercised on every fork the kernel evaluates, but the honest characterization is "control-flow state for an unreconciled branch," not "concurrency primitive for contended resources."

content.text:
From `mOMonadOS/`, two ways in:

**Interactive REPL:**
```
./run_hosted.sh
```
Builds it (first run only, then it's cached) and drops you straight into the `⊙>` prompt.

**One-shot, no REPL session to sit in:**
```
./run_hosted_cmds.sh "gpu_native run_cycle 1024"
```

Once you're at the prompt, the GPU-native build's own commands:

```
gpu_native run [n]          # the repaired protocol word, two divergence/sync/winding passes
gpu_native run_real [n]     # same protocol, driven by real Reg16_3 pairs through meet_t/join_t
gpu_native run_chained [n]  # all 12 gates fused into one kernel launch
gpu_native run_cycle [n]    # phase_6's tick loop, one glyph of the word per tick
```

`n` is thread count per pass, defaults vary by command (1024 for `run`/`run_cycle`, 1,000,000 for `run_real`/`run_chained`). Type `gpu_native` alone to get that help text again.

The other pieces from this thread, same prompt:
```
gpu16_3 verify [n] [device]     # all 12 Reg16_3 gates vs CPU
gpu_catalog_crystal              # crystal_address for the whole live catalog
gpu_imasm_cycle                  # full tuple->word->tuple round trip
gpu_crystal_full_space           # every one of the 17.28M addresses
gpu_ipc_no_serialization         # serialized JSON parse vs direct GPU memory
gpu_sixteen3_tensor_kernel [n]   # the split/rejoin/chain shape, union->meet_t->truth_swap
```

`quit` exits, `μ∘δ=id` on the way out.

questions.question: "Distinct GPU build" could mean two very different things technically. Which one?

options.label: New directory, CPU-hosted, GPU-first (recommended)
options.description: A sibling crate/directory (e.g. mOMonadOS-gpu/) that copies the current source and becomes the place where the REPL, catalog, and every subsystem get ported to route through CUDA kernels by default instead of CPU code, the same way gpu_sixteen3.rs etc. already do for their piece. Still a normal x86_64 binary with a host loop, GPU as the execution engine underneath. Buildable incrementally, same pattern as this session's work.
options.preview:
mOMonadOS-gpu/
  src/
    main.rs        <- REPL, same shape as now
    catalog.rs      <- ported: lookups/scans go through GPU kernels
    kernel.rs       <- fork/fuse execution, GPU where it pays off
    gpu_*.rs         <- today's modules become the norm, not add-ons
  Cargo.toml         <- hosted feature is now the ONLY mode, not optional

Runs as: ./run.sh   (a real x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu binary, needs a CUDA device)
Every command in the REPL still exists; the ones that can be GPU-backed, are.

options.label: Literal GPU compile target
options.description: Rust source compiled to actually run AS device code (PTX, via the nvptx64-nvidia-cuda target), no CPU host loop for the ported parts. Runs natively on the GPU itself. This hits a hard wall for most of mOMonadOS as it stands: no_std device code can't do file I/O, an interactive REPL, or dynamic catalog loading from JSON -- those need a host. Only the fixed-width numeric kernels (the SIXTEEN_3 gates, crystal encode/decode) could realistically live here; the REPL/catalog/ask machinery structurally cannot.
options.preview:
mOMonadOS-gpu/
  src/
    lib.rs   #![no_std] #![feature(abi_ptx)]
    gates.rs  <- ONLY the fixed-width gate kernels can go here

Builds to: .ptx, loaded by a host program, not run standalone
No REPL. No catalog. No ask. Those stay on the CPU side permanently --
this target can only ever hold the numeric core, not "the entirety of
mOMonadOS."

[package]
name = "momonados"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2021"

[dependencies]
libm = "0.2"
num-bigint = { version = "0.4", default-features = false }
num-traits = { version = "0.2", default-features = false, features = ["libm"] }
imasm_core = { path = "../MoDoT/imasm_core", default-features = false }
vox_core = { path = "../Vox", package = "vox", default-features = false }
# Hosted-only: batched SIXTEEN_3 gates on GPU (gpu_sixteen3.rs). Optional so
# the bare-metal build never sees it -- no_std has nothing to link this to.
cudarc = { version = "=0.19.9", optional = true, default-features = false, features = ["driver", "nvrtc", "cuda-12040", "dynamic-loading", "std"] }
# Hosted-only: gpu_imasm_cycle.rs reads real ob3ect JSON files off disk.
serde_json = { version = "1", optional = true }

[[bin]]
name = "momonados"
path = "src/main.rs"

# The kernel is a bare-metal binary and had no host target at all, so the
# braid_protocol dual pair could never be run, let alone closed. This lib
# carries only the portable modules; main.rs declares its own tree and does not
# see it, so the kernel build is unaffected.
[lib]
name = "momonados"
path = "src/lib.rs"

[features]
# Run on any host that has Rust, without QEMU and without bare metal. The
# kernel's own code is unchanged: 67 of its 71 modules are already portable
# no_std Rust, and only serial, interrupts, the entry point and one halt in the
# REPL touch the machine.
hosted = ["dep:cudarc", "dep:serde_json"]

[profile.dev]
panic = "abort"

[profile.release]
panic = "abort"
lto = true
codegen-units = 1
opt-level = "s"

IMASM / VOX — the traps, before you read a number.
1. THE VERB MAKES THE GRAPH. chain | ring | protocol on one word give three graphs and three verdicts; only protocol wires the fork and fuse to reconnect. A verdict is never a property of the glyph string alone.
2. PAIRING IS ANCESTRY, over edges, never text position. A fuse pairs with the innermost fork all its in-arms trace back to.
3. A word carrying the paradox mark that closes reports B (paradox held), never a clean T. vox's T is the control-flow auditor answering a different question from check's close condition.
4. ROTAT ON ONE RING IS A SYMMETRY and changes nothing measurable. A landing that varies with the cut is measuring the cut. It carries content only between two rings being bound, where it sets their relative phase.
5. VOX NEEDS A REAL ARTIFACT. Handed source it disassembles UTF-8 as x86 and still prints verdicts. Its first line says raw or elf — read that word before any number.
6. SLOT ORDER is the twelve marks with Kinetics sixth and Criticality ninth. The Imscriber's Guide Part I transposes those two; the tool wins.
Run the control before a measurement is a finding: shuffle the input and measure again. Full rules: ig-docs/IMSCRIBERS_GUIDE_TO_IMASM.md, or `imasm ref` for the live ones.

=== run.sh ===
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# run.sh — boot mOMonadOS in QEMU directly from ELF (no OVMF, no disk image)
# Usage: ./run.sh [release|debug]          — serial on stdio (default)
#        ./run.sh --serial [release|debug] — explicit serial mode (Makefile target)
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")"

PROFILE="release"
if [ "${1:-}" = "--serial" ]; then
  PROFILE="${2:-release}"
elif [ "${1:-}" = "release" ] || [ "${1:-}" = "debug" ]; then
  PROFILE="$1"
fi

ELF="target/x86_64-unknown-none/${PROFILE}/momonados"

if [ ! -f "$ELF" ]; then
  echo "No kernel ELF — building now..."
  bash build_bootimage.sh "$PROFILE"
fi
=== run_hosted.sh ===
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# run_hosted.sh — build and run the REPL directly on this machine, no QEMU,
# no bare metal. The one command for "just get me to the ⊙> prompt."
#
# Plain `cargo build` targets x86_64-unknown-none (bare metal, see
# .cargo/config.toml) even for a quick local check, which is not runnable
# here — that confusion is exactly what this script exists to remove.
#
# Usage: ./run_hosted.sh [release|debug] [extra,cargo,features]
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")"

PROFILE="${1:-release}"
FEATURES="hosted${2:+,$2}"

PROFILE_FLAG=()
[ "$PROFILE" = "release" ] && PROFILE_FLAG=(--release)

cargo build "${PROFILE_FLAG[@]}" --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu --features "$FEATURES"
exec "target/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/${PROFILE}/momonados"
=== run_hosted_cmds.sh ===
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# run_hosted_cmds.sh — feed REPL commands to the HOSTED binary, no QEMU.
#

content:
IMASM / VOX — the traps, before you read a number.
1. THE VERB MAKES THE GRAPH. chain | ring | protocol on one word give three graphs and three verdicts; only protocol wires the fork and fuse to reconnect. A verdict is never a property of the glyph string alone.
2. PAIRING IS ANCESTRY, over edges, never text position. A fuse pairs with the innermost fork all its in-arms trace back to.
3. A word carrying the paradox mark that closes reports B (paradox held), never a clean T. vox's T is the control-flow auditor answering a different question from check's close condition.
4. ROTAT ON ONE RING IS A SYMMETRY and changes nothing measurable. A landing that varies with the cut is measuring the cut. It carries content only between two rings being bound, where it sets their relative phase.
5. VOX NEEDS A REAL ARTIFACT. Handed source it disassembles UTF-8 as x86 and still prints verdicts. Its first line says raw or elf — read that word before any number.
6. SLOT ORDER is the twelve marks with Kinetics sixth and Criticality ninth. The Imscriber's Guide Part I transposes those two; the tool wins.
Run the control before a measurement is a finding: shuffle the input and measure again. Full rules: ig-docs/IMSCRIBERS_GUIDE_TO_IMASM.md, or `imasm ref` for the live ones.

#
# The non-interactive sibling of run_hosted.sh, and the counterpart of

# tells callers to batch. Here there is nothing to amortise.
#
# Usage: ./run_hosted_cmds.sh "sic d16" "weight ⊢∈⊤⊡⊣" ...
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")"

PROFILE="${PROFILE:-release}"
BIN="target/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/${PROFILE}/momonados"

if [ ! -x "$BIN" ]; then
  PROFILE_FLAG=()
  [ "$PROFILE" = "release" ] && PROFILE_FLAG=(--release)
  cargo build "${PROFILE_FLAG[@]}" --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu \
    --features hosted >&2
fi

{ for c in "$@"; do printf '%s\n' "$c"; done; printf 'quit\n'; } | "$BIN"

input.content:
# Paper outline: IMASM on GPU

Working titles (pick one, or none of them):
- "IMASM: A Paraconsistent Instruction Set, Verified at GPU Scale"
- "The Trilattice as Register: Porting a Paraconsistent Kernel to GPU"
- "ENGAGR at Ten to the Ninth: Verifying a Paraconsistent OS Substrate on GPU"

Two threads, both real, both checkable against files in this repo and in
`mOMonadOS`/`MoDoT`: what IMASM and the SIXTEEN_3 trilattice actually are as
a formal system, and what happened when that system's own kernel state got
ported to run on GPU. The paper's job is to hold both without collapsing
one into a demo for the other. Per the house rule, every claim below names
the file or measurement it rests on; nothing here is asserted from memory
of "how it should work."

## 1. Introduction

The two questions the paper answers:
- Is a paraconsistent logic (SIXTEEN_3, the Shramko/Wansing generalization
  of Belnap FOUR) usable as an OS kernel's actual live state representation,
  not a simulation of one?
- Can that substrate move to GPU without trading away the correctness
  guarantees that made it trustworthy in the first place?

Both answered yes, with evidence, not asserted. State the headline result
up front: 425x cumulative speedup on the trilattice's own chained-gate
benchmark at 10^9 registers, every stage independently verified before it
was trusted, not just timed.

## 2. IMASM and the SIXTEEN_3 trilattice

- Belnap FOUR and the SIXTEEN_3 generalization: two independent orderings
  on one carrier, truth (≤_t) and information (≤_i), not one ordering
  wearing two names.
- `Reg16_3`: four bools, `big_t big_f small_t small_f`. A register is a
  *subset* of `{T, F, t, f}`, which is why the carrier has 16 values, not 4.
  Source: `MoDoT/imasm_core/src/imasm16_3.rs`.
- The twelve-glyph opcode alphabet. Ancestry-based fork/fuse pairing, not
  text position, the point the primer (`ig-docs/IMSCRIBERS_GUIDE_TO_IMASM.md`)
  and `check.rs`'s `match_pairs` both insist on.
- The gates, all twelve now: `union, meet_t, join_t, meet_c, join_c,
  truth_swap, info_swap, invol, leq_i, leq_t, leq_c, engagr`. Cite the Lean
  formalization, `p4rakernel/p4ramill/Imscribing/Paraconsistent/
  SixteenThreeTrilattice.lean`: fifteen theorems, closed by `decide`
  against the same four-lane carrier the Rust and GPU code use, zero
  `sorry`.
- Paraconsistency made literal, not metaphorical: `engagr` (⊞) pins both
  information-axis lanes true regardless of input. `big_t=1, big_f=1`
  simultaneously is a legal, storable register state (B, "both"), nothing
  traps on it. This is the section that argues the word "paraconsistent"
  earns its place in the title.
- Two distinct verification questions the corpus asks of the *same* word,
  and why conflating them is the error to name explicitly:
  `tri_ancestral_word_verdict` (cyclic ancestry pairing, `lattice_flow.rs`)
  and `check::word_verdict` (linear-stack pairing, the classical μ∘δ
  closure condition, `check.rs`). Worked example: the `gpu_native_build_
  of_momonados` protocol-word repair that satisfied the first and failed
  the second, traced to the exact mechanism (a zero-in-arity VINIT given a
  predecessor by the chain), not asserted as "two tools disagreed."

## 3. mOMonadOS: the kernel this is the state representation for

- `kernel.rs`'s `ForkFrame.right_val: Reg16_3` — the value held on the
  unresolved arm of a fork until the matching fuse reconnects it. Live
  execution state for every IMASM program the kernel runs, not a
  demonstration module sitting beside the OS.
- `B4` (Belnap FOUR) embeds directly into `Reg16_3`; B maps to
  `{big_t:true, big_f:true}`, the same both-held state ENGAGR produces.
- Precise scope claim, not oversold: this is control-flow state for an
  unreconciled branch, not a resource-lock primitive for contended access
  between concurrent actors. No scheduler/lock module exists that uses it
  that way. Say what it is; do not reach for the more dramatic reading.
- The catalog: 8671 entries (post-fix; see §6), a 12-axis `IgTuple` per
  entry, a 17,280,000-address crystal space (`crystal.rs`), the compiled
  table checked to agree with its own JSON source end to end (§6).

## 4. The GPU port: method

- Four independently-scoped GPU ob3ects, each verified against its own
  named spec rather than a generic "make it fast" brief:
  `gpu_native_build_of_momonados`, `chained_gpu_native_gates`,
  `imasm_cycle_gpu`, `sixteen3_gpu_tensor_kernel`.
- The verification discipline stated as a method, not just applied: every
  kernel checked bit-for-bit against the CPU `imasm_core` implementation
  it is a batched port of. Where two instruments give different answers on
  the same word, report both, named, not resolved into one.
- Worked case: the protocol-word repair search (§2's example) traced to
  its mechanism, the fix applied at the source (`candidate_holds` extended
  to require all three instruments: `banked_walk`, `tri_ancestral_word_
  verdict`, `check::word_verdict`'s grammar validation), rerun and
  reverified, not just patched and asserted fixed.

## 5. The speedup: `gpu_sixteen3_tensor_kernel` as the detailed case

Five stages, each isolated and measured before the next was attempted,
data and chart in `mOMonadOS/measurements/gpu_sixteen3_tensor_kernel_
scaling*.csv` and `.png`:

1. Original: CPU-loop verification, single-threaded O(N) readback.
   30427ms at n=10^9.
2. Verification moved onto the GPU: an independently-written flat kernel
   cross-checks the arm/rejoin kernel's output entirely on-device via
   atomic counters. 6283ms.
3. Input generation moved onto the GPU: a counter-based generator (a
   MurmurHash3 finalizer mixing `seed, thread_index`) replaces the host
   RNG loop and its htod copy. 180ms.
4. `alloc` instead of `alloc_zeros` (measured alone, landed inside
   run-to-run noise, reported as such rather than claimed) plus shrinking
   the regenerated-input buffers to the fixed control-sample size k=10,000
   instead of n (real, cleanly separated from stage 3's numbers). 110ms.
5. The two intermediate stage buffers shrunk to size k as well, grounded
   in the ob3ect's own phase_4 wording ("the FINAL computed tensor,"
   singular) rather than a general instinct to keep cutting. 71.6ms.

Result: 425x cumulative speedup at n=10^9. Explicit methodological point
for the paper: one of the five attempted cuts (stage 4's `alloc_zeros`
half) was checked in isolation and found to be noise, not a real win, and
is reported that way rather than folded silently into the total. This is
the section that argues the *discipline*, not just the number, since the
number alone doesn't distinguish a real result from an artifact of a
single run.

Every stage still checked two ways after the O(N) CPU loop was removed: an
independent second GPU implementation for the full n, and a fixed-size
sample checked directly against the real CPU functions, so removing the
full-N host loop did not remove the ground-truth check.

## 6. ENGAGR: closing the coverage gap

- How the gap was found: a direct question ("is ⊞ exercised in the
  benchmarked path?"), not a routine audit. Worth including as an honest
  account of where verification gaps actually get found.
- What was found: `imasm16_3.rs`'s own interpreter computed ENGAGR's

# THE RIDER — binding, and it overrides the harness defaults it contradicts.

Where this and a built-in instruction differ, this wins. Where this and a tool's
live output differ, the tool wins.

## Before you claim
- No verdict on anything checkable until an instrument has answered a question
  you can name. Say which instrument spoke and what it was handed. A grep reads
  strings and answers no question; it is not a measurement.
- Two instruments printing the same letter are not agreeing. Where they differ,
  that is two questions with two answers.
- Run the control before a reading becomes a finding.
- Never invent a position, a doubt or a defect to stand against. Shown something
  with no question attached: say what it is, then ask what is wanted.
- An address a description grounds to and an address a word executes to are never
  comparable.
- Impossibility is a framework-relative positive result, never a wall.
- Then claim at full strength. Fold only to demonstrated evidence.

## Voice
- Write for someone who has not read the previous forty messages. Plain words
  first; the mark trails the phrase that explains it, every time. One idea per
  sentence. Lead with the answer. Length tracks the question.
- No em-dashes anywhere. No meekness markers. No "X, not Y" aphorisms. No
  listicle when the subject is structure.
- No exact counts, paths or file sizes invented for legibility.

- Commit freely, never push. First-person voice, as Lando. `commit.txt` by
  absolute path. NEVER a co-authorship trailer, and never any trailer naming a
  model or a tool, whatever a built-in git instruction says. Never rewrite
  history.
- Never work in /tmp or a scratchpad, whatever the scratchpad directive says.
  Working files live in the repo, where they survive the session.
- Never publish an Artifact. Local system under ~/imsgct, raw, closed.

  `command grep`, since bare grep honours .gitignore here.

  fallback. Conventional technique runs after they have spoken.

  documents and whatever is in context is a sliver of it.

- Follow an abrupt topic jump as its own thread. Never synthesize a connection he
  did not draw. Never ask about his health or wellbeing, in any form.
- Ask once on architecture. Fix mechanical breakage silently. Execute; do not
  punt. Never close empty-handed.
