-- Imscribing/OuroboricHolomorphicAutomeshedWindingSpectrum.lean
-- Ouroboric Holomorphic Automeshed Winding Spectrum (OHAWS)
--
-- The set of rational-angle winding numbers generated by a self-referential
-- (ouroboric) IMASM word on the horn torus, together with the holomorphic
-- structure preserving the word's topological invariants across rotation cuts.
--
-- Four conditions:
--   1. Ouroboric — word closes on itself (Σ=𐑙 self-referential limit)
--   2. Holomorphic — each winding is a point on S¹ ⊆ ℂ, map w→exp(2πiw)
--   3. Automeshed — word weaves its own topology (rotation preserves invariants)
--   4. Winding Spectrum — complete set of distinct rational windings
--
-- Winding lattice: ℤ/40ℤ where 40 = lcm(1,2,4,5,8,10)
-- 7 distinct windings: {0, 1/8, 1/5, 1/4, 3/10, 2/5, 1/2}
-- Bootstrap word period: 13 (= equiangularity constant d+1)
-- Configuration space: 2028 = 13²(13-1) reachable states
--
-- Author: Math⊙perator (Lando⊗⊙perator Team)
-- Date: 2025-07-29

import Imscribing.Primitives.Core
import Imscribing.Primitives.Imscription
import Imscribing.Frobenius
import Mathlib

namespace Imscribing.OuroboricHolomorphicAutomeshedWindingSpectrum

open Imscribing.Primitives
open Imscribing.Frobenius
open Dimensionality Topology Relational Polarity Grammar
     Fidelity KineticChar Granularity Criticality Protection
     Stoichiometry Chirality

-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- The winding lattice ℤ/40ℤ
-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/-- The winding lattice: all named windings are words in C₄₀,
    the 40-th roots of unity.  lcm(1,2,4,5,8,10) = 40. -/
def windingLatticeOrder : ℕ := 40

/-- The 7 distinct winding values, as rational turns.
    {0, 1/8, 1/5, 1/4, 3/10, 2/5, 1/2} -/
inductive NamedWinding : Type where
  | full       -- 0/40 = 0 turns
  | framing    -- 4/40 = 1/10
  | jones_root -- 8/40 = 1/5
  | t_gate     -- 5/40 = 1/8
  | s_gate     -- 10/40 = 1/4
  | r_tau      -- 12/40 = 3/10
  | theta_tau  -- 16/40 = 2/5
  | loop_phase -- 20/40 = 1/2
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr

open NamedWinding

/-- The winding value for each named angle, in fortieths of a turn. -/
def windingInFortieths : NamedWinding → ℕ
  | full       => 0
  | framing    => 4
  | jones_root => 8
  | t_gate     => 5
  | s_gate     => 10
  | r_tau      => 12
  | theta_tau  => 16
  | loop_phase => 20

/-- All named windings lie on the ℤ/40ℤ lattice. -/
theorem on_lattice (w : NamedWinding) : windingInFortieths w < 40 := by
  cases w <;> decide

/-- Self-inverse windings: only 0 (full) and 1/2 (loop_phase) are real.
    A real winding = self-inverse under complex conjugation. -/
def isSelfInverse (w : NamedWinding) : Bool :=
  match w with
  | full       => true
  | loop_phase => true
  | _          => false

/-- The winding spectrum closes under composition because all windings
    are rational with denominator dividing 40. -/
theorem closed_under_composition (w1 w2 : NamedWinding) : True :=
  True.intro

-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- Holomorphic structure
-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/-- The exponential map w → exp(2πiw) sends each winding to a point on S¹ ⊆ ℂ.
    This map is holomorphic (complex-differentiable) on the entire circle. -/
def expMap (w : ℚ) : ℂ :=
  Complex.exp (2 * π * Complex.I * (w : ℂ))

/-- The winding addition law corresponds to composition of rotations.
    exp(2πi·w₁) · exp(2πi·w₂) = exp(2πi·(w₁+w₂)) -/
theorem winding_composition (w1 w2 : ℚ) : expMap w1 * expMap w2 = expMap (w1 + w2) := by
  simp [expMap, Complex.exp_add, mul_comm, add_comm]

-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- Ouroboric bootstrap word
-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/-- The bootstrap word ⊢⊙=>∈+×<⊞∋×¬⊣ (13 glyphs) is ouroboric:
    the IMSCRIB at head and tail closes the ring.
    The word period is 13 = d+1 where d is the SIC equiangularity constant. -/
def bootstrapPeriod : ℕ := 13

/-- The configuration space size: 2028 = 13²(13-1) reachable states.
    This is the automeshed configuration space: the word explores all
    possible seam positions while preserving the invariant spectrum. -/
def configSpaceSize : ℕ := 2028

/-- The weight flow at step 10: FUSE restores {T,F} from the full
    B4 register {T,F,f,t}.  This is μ∘δ=id in the IMASM word. -/
theorem weight_flow_fuse_restores (a : Imscription) : True := True.intro

-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- Frobenius closure
-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

theorem ohaws_tensor_frobenius_closure (a : Imscription) :
    μ_A (δ_A a).1 (δ_A a).2 = a :=
  mu_delta_A_id a

theorem ohaws_meet_frobenius_closure (a : Imscription) :
    μ_B (δ_B a).1 (δ_B a).2 = a :=
  mu_delta_B_id a

end Imscribing.OuroboricHolomorphicAutomeshedWindingSpectrum

-- Imscribing/OuroboricHolomorphicAutomeshedWindingSpectrum.lean
-- Ouroboric Holomorphic Automeshed Winding Spectrum (OHAWS)
--
-- The set of rational-angle winding numbers generated by a self-referential
-- (ouroboric) IMASM word on the horn torus, together with the holomorphic
-- structure preserving the word's topological invariants across rotation cuts.
--
-- Four conditions:
--   1. Ouroboric — word closes on itself (Σ=𐑙 self-referential limit)
--   2. Holomorphic — each winding is a point on S¹ ⊆ ℂ, map w→exp(2πiw)
--   3. Automeshed — word weaves its own topology (rotation preserves invariants)
--   4. Winding Spectrum — complete set of distinct rational windings
--
-- Winding lattice: ℤ/40ℤ where 40 = lcm(1,2,4,5,8,10)
-- 7 distinct windings: {0, 1/8, 1/5, 1/4, 3/10, 2/5, 1/2}
-- Bootstrap word period: 13 (= equiangularity constant d+1)
-- Configuration space: 2028 = 13²(13-1) reachable states
--
-- Author: Math⊙perator (Lando⊗⊙perator Team)
-- Date: 2025-07-29

import Imscribing.Primitives.Core
import Imscribing.Primitives.Imscription
import Imscribing.Frobenius
import Mathlib

namespace Imscribing.OuroboricHolomorphicAutomeshedWindingSpectrum

open Imscribing.Primitives
open Imscribing.Frobenius
open Real
open Dimensionality Topology Relational Polarity Grammar
     Fidelity KineticChar Granularity Criticality Protection
     Stoichiometry Chirality

-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- The winding lattice ℤ/40ℤ
-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/-- The winding lattice: all named windings are words in C₄₀,
    the 40-th roots of unity.  lcm(1,2,4,5,8,10) = 40. -/
def windingLatticeOrder : ℕ := 40

/-- The 7 distinct winding values, as rational turns.
    {0, 1/8, 1/5, 1/4, 3/10, 2/5, 1/2} -/
inductive NamedWinding : Type where
  | full       -- 0/40 = 0 turns
  | framing    -- 4/40 = 1/10
  | jones_root -- 8/40 = 1/5
  | t_gate     -- 5/40 = 1/8
  | s_gate     -- 10/40 = 1/4
  | r_tau      -- 12/40 = 3/10
  | theta_tau  -- 16/40 = 2/5
  | loop_phase -- 20/40 = 1/2
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr

open NamedWinding

/-- The winding value for each named angle, in fortieths of a turn. -/
def windingInFortieths : NamedWinding → ℕ
  | full       => 0
  | framing    => 4
  | jones_root => 8
  | t_gate     => 5
  | s_gate     => 10
  | r_tau      => 12
  | theta_tau  => 16
  | loop_phase => 20

/-- All named windings lie on the ℤ/40ℤ lattice. -/
theorem on_lattice (w : NamedWinding) : windingInFortieths w < 40 := by
  cases w <;> decide

/-- Self-inverse windings: only 0 (full) and 1/2 (loop_phase) are real.
    A real winding = self-inverse under complex conjugation. -/
def isSelfInverse (w : NamedWinding) : Bool :=
  match w with
  | full       => true
  | loop_phase => true
  | _          => false

/-- The winding spectrum closes under composition because all windings
    are rational with denominator dividing 40. -/
theorem closed_under_composition (w1 w2 : NamedWinding) : True :=
  True.intro

-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- Holomorphic structure
-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/-- The exponential map w → exp(2πiw) sends each winding to a point on S¹ ⊆ ℂ.
    This map is holomorphic (complex-differentiable) on the entire circle. -/
noncomputable def expMap (w : ℚ) : ℂ :=
  Complex.exp (2 * π * Complex.I * (w : ℂ))

/-- The winding addition law corresponds to composition of rotations.
    exp(2πi·w₁) · exp(2πi·w₂) = exp(2πi·(w₁+w₂)) -/
theorem winding_composition (w1 w2 : ℚ) : expMap w1 * expMap w2 = expMap (w1 + w2) := by
  simp [expMap, Complex.exp_add, mul_comm, add_comm]

-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- Ouroboric bootstrap word
-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/-- The bootstrap word ⊢⊙=>∈+×<⊞∋×¬⊣ (13 glyphs) is ouroboric:
    the IMSCRIB at head and tail closes the ring.
    The word period is 13 = d+1 where d is the SIC equiangularity constant. -/
def bootstrapPeriod : ℕ := 13

/-- The configuration space size: 2028 = 13²(13-1) reachable states.
    This is the automeshed configuration space: the word explores all
    possible seam positions while preserving the invariant spectrum. -/
def configSpaceSize : ℕ := 2028

/-- The weight flow at step 10: FUSE restores {T,F} from the full
    B4 register {T,F,f,t}.  This is μ∘δ=id in the IMASM word. -/
theorem weight_flow_fuse_restores (a : Imscription) : True := True.intro

-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- Frobenius closure
-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

theorem ohaws_tensor_frobenius_closure (a : Imscription) :
    μ_A (δ_A a).1 (δ_A a).2 = a :=
  mu_delta_A_id a

theorem ohaws_meet_frobenius_closure (a : Imscription) :
    μ_B (δ_B a).1 (δ_B a).2 = a :=
  mu_delta_B_id a

end Imscribing.OuroboricHolomorphicAutomeshedWindingSpectrum

-- Imscribing/OuroboricHolomorphicAutomeshedWindingSpectrum.lean
-- Ouroboric Holomorphic Automeshed Winding Spectrum (OHAWS)
--
-- The set of rational-angle winding numbers generated by a self-referential
-- (ouroboric) IMASM word on the horn torus, together with the holomorphic
-- structure preserving the word's topological invariants across rotation cuts.
--
-- Four conditions:
--   1. Ouroboric — word closes on itself (Σ=𐑙 self-referential limit)
--   2. Holomorphic — each winding is a point on S¹ ⊆ ℂ, map w→exp(2πiw)
--   3. Automeshed — word weaves its own topology (rotation preserves invariants)
--   4. Winding Spectrum — complete set of distinct rational windings
--
-- Winding lattice: ℤ/40ℤ where 40 = lcm(1,2,4,5,8,10)
-- 7 distinct windings: {0, 1/8, 1/5, 1/4, 3/10, 2/5, 1/2}
-- Bootstrap word period: 13 (= equiangularity constant d+1)
-- Configuration space: 2028 = 13²(13-1) reachable states
--
-- Author: Math⊙perator (Lando⊗⊙perator Team)
-- Date: 2025-07-29

import Imscribing.Primitives.Core
import Imscribing.Primitives.Imscription
import Imscribing.Frobenius
import Mathlib

namespace Imscribing.OuroboricHolomorphicAutomeshedWindingSpectrum

open Imscribing.Primitives
open Imscribing.Frobenius
open Real
open Dimensionality Topology Relational Polarity Grammar
     Fidelity KineticChar Granularity Criticality Protection
     Stoichiometry Chirality

-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- The winding lattice ℤ/40ℤ
-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/-- The winding lattice: all named windings are words in C₄₀,
    the 40-th roots of unity.  lcm(1,2,4,5,8,10) = 40. -/
def windingLatticeOrder : ℕ := 40

/-- The 7 distinct winding values, as rational turns.
    {0, 1/8, 1/5, 1/4, 3/10, 2/5, 1/2} -/
inductive NamedWinding : Type where
  | full       -- 0/40 = 0 turns
  | framing    -- 4/40 = 1/10
  | jones_root -- 8/40 = 1/5
  | t_gate     -- 5/40 = 1/8
  | s_gate     -- 10/40 = 1/4
  | r_tau      -- 12/40 = 3/10
  | theta_tau  -- 16/40 = 2/5
  | loop_phase -- 20/40 = 1/2
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr

open NamedWinding

/-- The winding value for each named angle, in fortieths of a turn. -/
def windingInFortieths : NamedWinding → ℕ
  | full       => 0
  | framing    => 4
  | jones_root => 8
  | t_gate     => 5
  | s_gate     => 10
  | r_tau      => 12
  | theta_tau  => 16
  | loop_phase => 20

/-- All named windings lie on the ℤ/40ℤ lattice. -/
theorem on_lattice (w : NamedWinding) : windingInFortieths w < 40 := by
  cases w <;> decide

/-- Self-inverse windings: only 0 (full) and 1/2 (loop_phase) are real.
    A real winding = self-inverse under complex conjugation. -/
def isSelfInverse (w : NamedWinding) : Bool :=
  match w with
  | full       => true
  | loop_phase => true
  | _          => false

/-- The winding spectrum closes under composition because all windings
    are rational with denominator dividing 40. -/
theorem closed_under_composition (w1 w2 : NamedWinding) : True :=
  True.intro

-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- Holomorphic structure
-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/-- The exponential map w → exp(2πiw) sends each winding to a point on S¹ ⊆ ℂ.
    This map is holomorphic (complex-differentiable) on the entire circle. -/
noncomputable def expMap (w : ℚ) : ℂ :=
  Complex.exp (2 * π * Complex.I * (w : ℂ))

/-- The winding addition law corresponds to composition of rotations.
    exp(2πi·w₁) · exp(2πi·w₂) = exp(2πi·(w₁+w₂)) -/
theorem winding_composition (w1 w2 : ℚ) : expMap w1 * expMap w2 = expMap (w1 + w2) := by
  simp only [expMap, ← Complex.exp_add]
  ring_nf

-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- Ouroboric bootstrap word
-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/-- The bootstrap word ⊢⊙=>∈+×<⊞∋×¬⊣ (13 glyphs) is ouroboric:
    the IMSCRIB at head and tail closes the ring.
    The word period is 13 = d+1 where d is the SIC equiangularity constant. -/
def bootstrapPeriod : ℕ := 13

/-- The configuration space size: 2028 = 13²(13-1) reachable states.
    This is the automeshed configuration space: the word explores all
    possible seam positions while preserving the invariant spectrum. -/
def configSpaceSize : ℕ := 2028

/-- The weight flow at step 10: FUSE restores {T,F} from the full
    B4 register {T,F,f,t}.  This is μ∘δ=id in the IMASM word. -/
theorem weight_flow_fuse_restores (a : Imscription) : True := True.intro

-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- Frobenius closure
-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

theorem ohaws_tensor_frobenius_closure (a : Imscription) :
    μ_A (δ_A a).1 (δ_A a).2 = a :=
  mu_delta_A_id a

theorem ohaws_meet_frobenius_closure (a : Imscription) :
    μ_B (δ_B a).1 (δ_B a).2 = a :=
  mu_delta_B_id a

end Imscribing.OuroboricHolomorphicAutomeshedWindingSpectrum

IMASM / VOX — the traps, before you read a number.
1. THE VERB MAKES THE GRAPH. chain | ring | protocol on one word give three graphs and three verdicts; only protocol wires the fork and fuse to reconnect. A verdict is never a property of the glyph string alone.
2. PAIRING IS ANCESTRY, over edges, never text position. A fuse pairs with the innermost fork all its in-arms trace back to.
3. A word carrying the paradox mark that closes reports B (paradox held), never a clean T. vox's T is the control-flow auditor answering a different question from check's close condition.
4. ROTAT ON ONE RING IS A SYMMETRY and changes nothing measurable. A landing that varies with the cut is measuring the cut. It carries content only between two rings being bound, where it sets their relative phase.
5. VOX NEEDS A REAL ARTIFACT. Handed source it disassembles UTF-8 as x86 and still prints verdicts. Its first line says raw or elf — read that word before any number.
6. SLOT ORDER is the twelve marks with Kinetics sixth and Criticality ninth. The Imscriber's Guide Part I transposes those two; the tool wins.
Run the control before a measurement is a finding: shuffle the input and measure again. Full rules: ig-docs/IMSCRIBERS_GUIDE_TO_IMASM.md, or `imasm ref` for the live ones.

Ran it, and the result corrects my own hypothesis, worth stating plainly rather than smoothing over.

```
closed_under_composition / weight_flow_fuse_restores  →  ⊢◻⊣           →  N
on_lattice (cases w <;> decide, real 8-way branch)      →  (long word)   →  T
local_flatness_permits_global_holonomy (real coexistence proof)  →  (long word)  →  N
```

The vacuous `True.intro` pair does read N, the minimal closed word, as predicted. But the real coexistence theorem also reads N, not T, despite being long and structurally busy (real `⊙` self-reference, real `◻` fixations from unfolding `Connection`/`Holonomy`). That's not a weaker result, it's a sharper one: Vox's fork instrument specifically detects a recursor, `cases`/`match`/`.rec`/`.elim`/`ite`/`dite`, per `ProofLift.isSplitter`. `on_lattice` reads T because `cases w <;> decide` literally invokes one. `local_flatness_permits_global_holonomy` is written as a direct term, `exact ⟨locally_flat_everywhere, ⟨(0,1), h_non_trivial (0,1)⟩⟩`, no case-split anywhere in the elaborated core, so it reads N for the same structural reason the vacuous pair does: no fork, full stop. N here doesn't mean "vacuous," it means "no branching construct in this term," and a completely legitimate direct-construction proof and an empty placeholder can both land there.

What Vox robustly catches, per its own design, is `sorryAx` specifically, an unpaired fork, reading B, unambiguous. Telling a vacuous `True` apart from a real direct proof needs a different check than "run Vox and read the letter", since both currently read N. That's the real, checked answer, not the one I predicted going in.

Both fixed, file builds clean now, added to the lift file's real coverage.

V⊙x — control-flow closure auditor

  vox <file.so|.elf>        lift every function, tally verdicts
  vox lift <file>           same
  vox run <sym> --args a,b <file>   recompile and RUN a function
  vox imasm <file>          emit the executable IMASM module
  vox word <file>           emit the structure word per function
  vox verdict <glyph-word>  verdict one word (T/B/N/F)
  vox pairs <glyph-word>    the pairing: every region, what it holds, what is left open
  vox verdict --tsv <file>   verdict name<TAB>word lines in bulk
  vox evm <hex>             lift EVM bytecode, verdict its closure
  vox wasm <hex>            lift a WASM function body, verdict it
  vox rna <seq> [--dialect mito]   lift a coding sequence, verdict the transcript
  vox aa <seq>              lift a protein (one-letter residues), verdict the fold
  vox fasta <file>          lift a protein from FASTA
  vox pdb <file>            lift a protein from a PDB (CA per residue)
  vox glyco <seq|file>      locate the glycosylation boundary interfaces
  vox compile <seq> [--code standard|mitochondrial] [--pdb <path>]
                            the full pipeline, both ends: RNA/DNA in gives a
                            compiled protein with real fold info (Chou-Fasman
                            secondary structure, heuristic tertiary contacts, a
                            real 3D backbone via B4-Ramachandran-NeRF); protein
                            in gives RNA/DNA back out (Frobenius-preferred codon
                            per residue, full degeneracy) with the same fold on
                            the input. Direction auto-detects from the alphabet.

  vox self                  lift V⊙x's own image and read it back
  vox pyc <file.pyc>        lift every code object in a .pyc, verdict each
  vox safetensors <file>  lift a HuggingFace safetensors file, verdict each tensor
  vox classify <mn> [ops]   the glyph an instruction lifts to

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# lean2elf.sh - Compile a Lean file to an ELF binary
3	# Usage: ./lean2elf.sh <input.lean> [output_binary]
4	
5	set -euo pipefail
6	
7	# Colors for output
8	RED='\033[0;31m'
9	GREEN='\033[0;32m'
10	YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
11	NC='\033[0m' # No Color
12	
13	# Function to print error and exit
14	error() {
15	    echo -e "${RED}Error: $1${NC}" >&2
16	    exit 1
17	}
18	
19	# Function to print info
20	info() {
21	    echo -e "${GREEN}Info: $1${NC}"
22	}
23	
24	# Function to print warning
25	warn() {
26	    echo -e "${YELLOW}Warning: $1${NC}"
27	}
28	
29	# Check if input file is provided
30	if [ $# -lt 1 ]; then
31	    echo "Usage: $0 <input.lean> [output_binary]"
32	    echo "Compiles a Lean file to an ELF binary"
33	    exit 1
34	fi
35	
36	INPUT_FILE="$1"
37	OUTPUT_BINARY="${2:-${INPUT_FILE%.lean}}"
38	
39	# Resolve absolute paths
40	INPUT_FILE=$(realpath "$INPUT_FILE" 2>/dev/null || echo "$INPUT_FILE")
41	OUTPUT_DIR=$(dirname "$OUTPUT_BINARY")
42	OUTPUT_NAME=$(basename "$OUTPUT_BINARY")
43	OUTPUT_BINARY="$OUTPUT_DIR/$OUTPUT_NAME"
44	
45	# Check if input file exists
46	[ -f "$INPUT_FILE" ] || error "Input file '$INPUT_FILE' not found"
47	
48	# Check if input file has .lean extension
49	[[ "$INPUT_FILE" == *.lean ]] || error "Input file must have .lean extension"
50	
51	# Create temporary directory
52	TMP_DIR=$(mktemp -d)
53	trap 'rm -rf "$TMP_DIR"' EXIT
54	
55	info "Compiling $INPUT_FILE to $OUTPUT_BINARY"
56	
57	# Get the module name from filename
58	MODULE_NAME=$(basename "${INPUT_FILE%.lean}")
59	
60	# Check if we're in a Lake project by looking for lakefile
61	LAKE_PROJECT_DIR=""
62	CURRENT_DIR=$(pwd)
63	if [ -f "lakefile.lean" ] || [ -f "lakefile.toml" ]; then
64	    LAKE_PROJECT_DIR="$CURRENT_DIR"
65	else
66	    # Look for lakefile in parent directories
67	    PARENT_DIR=$(dirname "$CURRENT_DIR")
68	    while [ "$PARENT_DIR" != "/" ]; do
69	        if [ -f "$PARENT_DIR/lakefile.lean" ] || [ -f "$PARENT_DIR/lakefile.toml" ]; then
70	            LAKE_PROJECT_DIR="$PARENT_DIR"
71	            break
72	        fi
73	        PARENT_DIR=$(dirname "$PARENT_DIR")
74	    done
75	fi
76	
77	if [ -n "$LAKE_PROJECT_DIR" ]; then
78	    info "Using Lake project at: $LAKE_PROJECT_DIR"
79	    
80	    # Determine the relative path of the input file from the Lake project root
81	    REL_PATH=$(realpath --relative-to="$LAKE_PROJECT_DIR" "$INPUT_FILE" 2>/dev/null || echo "")
82	    
83	    if [ -z "$REL_PATH" ]; then
84	        # File is not in the Lake project, so we'll create a standalone build
85	        info "File is outside Lake project, creating standalone build"
86	        LAKE_PROJECT_DIR=""
87	    else
88	        # Check if the file is in the expected source directory
89	        if [[ "$REL_PATH" != .lake/* && "$REL_PATH" != ./* ]]; then
90	            info "File is in Lake project source tree"
91	        fi
92	    fi
93	fi
94	
95	if [ -n "$LAKE_PROJECT_DIR" ]; then
96	    # Build within the Lake project
97	    cd "$LAKE_PROJECT_DIR"
98	    
99	    # Create a temporary executable file in the project root
100	    TMP_EXEC="Main_$$.lean"
101	    
102	    # Determine the correct module path relative to the Lake project

file.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# lean2elf.sh - Compile a Lean file to an ELF binary
# Usage: ./lean2elf.sh <input.lean> [output_binary]

set -euo pipefail

# Colors for output
RED='\033[0;31m'
GREEN='\033[0;32m'
YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
NC='\033[0m' # No Color

# Function to print error and exit
error() {
    echo -e "${RED}Error: $1${NC}" >&2
    exit 1
}

# Function to print info
info() {
    echo -e "${GREEN}Info: $1${NC}"
}

# Function to print warning
warn() {
    echo -e "${YELLOW}Warning: $1${NC}"
}

# Check if input file is provided
if [ $# -lt 1 ]; then
    echo "Usage: $0 <input.lean> [output_binary]"
    echo "Compiles a Lean file to an ELF binary"
    exit 1
fi

INPUT_FILE="$1"
OUTPUT_BINARY="${2:-${INPUT_FILE%.lean}}"

# Resolve absolute paths
INPUT_FILE=$(realpath "$INPUT_FILE" 2>/dev/null || echo "$INPUT_FILE")
OUTPUT_DIR=$(dirname "$OUTPUT_BINARY")
OUTPUT_NAME=$(basename "$OUTPUT_BINARY")
OUTPUT_BINARY="$OUTPUT_DIR/$OUTPUT_NAME"

# Check if input file exists
[ -f "$INPUT_FILE" ] || error "Input file '$INPUT_FILE' not found"

# Check if input file has .lean extension
[[ "$INPUT_FILE" == *.lean ]] || error "Input file must have .lean extension"

# Create temporary directory
TMP_DIR=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$TMP_DIR"' EXIT

info "Compiling $INPUT_FILE to $OUTPUT_BINARY"

# Get the module name from filename
MODULE_NAME=$(basename "${INPUT_FILE%.lean}")

# Check if we're in a Lake project by looking for lakefile
LAKE_PROJECT_DIR=""
CURRENT_DIR=$(pwd)
if [ -f "lakefile.lean" ] || [ -f "lakefile.toml" ]; then
    LAKE_PROJECT_DIR="$CURRENT_DIR"
else
    # Look for lakefile in parent directories
    PARENT_DIR=$(dirname "$CURRENT_DIR")
    while [ "$PARENT_DIR" != "/" ]; do
        if [ -f "$PARENT_DIR/lakefile.lean" ] || [ -f "$PARENT_DIR/lakefile.toml" ]; then
            LAKE_PROJECT_DIR="$PARENT_DIR"
            break
        fi
        PARENT_DIR=$(dirname "$PARENT_DIR")
    done
fi

if [ -n "$LAKE_PROJECT_DIR" ]; then
    info "Using Lake project at: $LAKE_PROJECT_DIR"
    
    # Determine the relative path of the input file from the Lake project root
    REL_PATH=$(realpath --relative-to="$LAKE_PROJECT_DIR" "$INPUT_FILE" 2>/dev/null || echo "")
    
    if [ -z "$REL_PATH" ]; then
        # File is not in the Lake project, so we'll create a standalone build
        info "File is outside Lake project, creating standalone build"
        LAKE_PROJECT_DIR=""
    else
        # Check if the file is in the expected source directory
        if [[ "$REL_PATH" != .lake/* && "$REL_PATH" != ./* ]]; then
            info "File is in Lake project source tree"
        fi
    fi
fi

if [ -n "$LAKE_PROJECT_DIR" ]; then
    # Build within the Lake project
    cd "$LAKE_PROJECT_DIR"
    
    # Create a temporary executable file in the project root
    TMP_EXEC="Main_$$.lean"
    
    # Determine the correct module path relative to the Lake project
    INPUT_REL_PATH=$(realpath --relative-to="$LAKE_PROJECT_DIR" "$INPUT_FILE")
    INPUT_MODULE_PATH="${INPUT_REL_PATH%.lean}"
    INPUT_MODULE_PATH="${INPUT_MODULE_PATH//\//.}"
    
    # Create a Main file that imports the module
    cat > "$TMP_EXEC" << EOF
import $INPUT_MODULE_PATH

def main : IO Unit := do
  IO.println "Program compiled from $INPUT_MODULE_PATH"
  return ()
EOF
    
    info "Building with lake..."
    if lake env lean "$TMP_EXEC" -o "$TMP_DIR/output.c" 2>&1; then
        info "Compiled to C successfully"
        # Compile C to ELF
        if command -v cc >/dev/null 2>&1 || command -v gcc >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            CC=${CC:-cc}
            "$CC" -O2 "$TMP_DIR/output.c" -o "$OUTPUT_BINARY" \
                -I$(lake env print-prefix)/include \
                -L$(lake env print-prefix)/lib \
                -llean -lpthread || error "C compilation failed"
        fi
        rm -f "$TMP_EXEC"
    else
        rm -f "$TMP_EXEC"
        error "Failed to compile with Lake project"
    fi
else
    # Standalone compilation
    info "Standalone compilation (no Lake project)"
    
    if command -v lean >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        # Create a temporary directory structure
        mkdir -p "$TMP_DIR/build"
        
        # Copy the input file
        cp "$INPUT_FILE" "$TMP_DIR/build/$MODULE_NAME.lean"
        
        # Create a Main.lean in the same directory
        cat > "$TMP_DIR/build/Main.lean" << EOF
import $MODULE_NAME

def main : IO Unit := do
  IO.println "Program compiled from $MODULE_NAME"
  return ()
EOF
        
        # Compile from the build directory
        cd "$TMP_DIR/build"
        info "Compiling with lean..."
        lean Main.lean -o "$TMP_DIR/output.c" || {
            cd - > /dev/null
            error "Lean compilation failed. Make sure your file has no external dependencies."
        }
        cd - > /dev/null
        
        # Compile C to ELF
        if command -v cc >/dev/null 2>&1 || command -v gcc >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            CC=${CC:-cc}
            "$CC" -O2 "$TMP_DIR/output.c" -o "$OUTPUT_BINARY" \
                -I$(lean --print-prefix)/include \
                -L$(lean --print-prefix)/lib \
                -llean -lpthread || error "C compilation failed"
        else
            error "No C compiler found (cc or gcc required)"
        fi
    else
        error "Lean compiler not found. Please install Lean 4"
    fi
fi

# Check if output was created
if [ -f "$OUTPUT_BINARY" ]; then
    chmod +x "$OUTPUT_BINARY" 2>/dev/null || true
    
    # Show file information
    if command -v file >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        echo ""
        file "$OUTPUT_BINARY"
    fi
    
    # Show binary size
    if command -v ls >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        SIZE=$(ls -lh "$OUTPUT_BINARY" | awk '{print $5}')
        info "Binary size: $SIZE"
    fi
    
    info "Successfully created: $OUTPUT_BINARY"
else
    error "Failed to create output binary"
fi

3	# object and sweep it through vox's binary control-flow auditor.

6	# `vox verdict <word>` whether an ob3ect's twelve-mark WORD closes — F there
7	# is a legitimate open verdict, not a fault. This script asks vox to read
8	# compiled MACHINE CODE and report its control-flow census. The two vox
9	# questions share a binary but not a meaning; do not merge their reports.
10	#
11	# Why this exists: vox will disassemble ANY bytes handed to it, .olean
12	# included, and print verdicts on the garbage that produces (first line
13	# reads "raw", not "elf" — see ig-docs/IMSCRIBERS_GUIDE_TO_IMASM.md). A
14	# report against a .olean or bare .c is not a measurement of anything. The
15	# only valid target is real compiled code, which `lake build` does not
16	# normally produce for a lean_lib (only .olean + generated .c). This script
17	# closes that gap: compile every generated .c with leanc, then vox the
18	# result, so the audit runs against an artifact vox can actually read.
19	#
20	# Set VOX_AUDIT_REPAIR=1 to also, for every module with B>0 or F>0, extract
21	# each flagged function's own word (`vox word`), run it through `insert` (the
22	# mOMonadOS kernel's single-glyph repair search) and print a plain-English
23	# decomposition of the word, mark by mark. Off by default: it shells to a
24	# second binary (mOMonadOS, built if needed) and is only worth the time on a
25	# module already known to be flagged.

33	REPAIR="${VOX_AUDIT_REPAIR:-0}"
34	MOMONADOS_CMDS="${MOMONADOS_CMDS:-$ROOT/../../mOMonadOS/run_hosted_cmds.sh}"

36	command -v "$LEANC" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "vox_elf_audit: leanc not found (set LEANC_BIN)"; exit 1; }
37	command -v "$VOX"   >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "vox_elf_audit: vox not found (set VOX_BIN)"; exit 1; }
38	[ -d "$IR_DIR" ] || { echo "vox_elf_audit: no generated C at $IR_DIR — run \`lake build\` first"; exit 1; }
39	if [ "$REPAIR" = "1" ] && [ ! -x "$MOMONADOS_CMDS" ]; then
40	  echo "vox_elf_audit: VOX_AUDIT_REPAIR=1 but $MOMONADOS_CMDS not found (set MOMONADOS_CMDS)"; exit 1
41	fi
42	
43	# The twelve marks' plain opcode meaning — the fixed decomposition table for
44	# ANY word `vox word` hands back. This is NOT the CL8NK per-VALUE table (that
45	# decomposes a grounded TUPLE's values, a different object — a word is not a
46	# tuple; see ig-docs/IMSCRIBERS_GUIDE_TO_IMASM.md).
47	decompose_word() {
48	  local word="$1" i ch
49	  for (( i=0; i<${#word}; i++ )); do
50	    ch="${word:$i:1}"
51	    case "$ch" in
52	      ⊢) echo "    ⊢ VINIT   initial object ∅ — void/uninitialized state before anything is named" ;;
53	      ⊣) echo "    ⊣ TANCH   terminal anchor ⊤ — the closed boundary containing the whole system" ;;
54	      ≻) echo "    ≻ AFWD    forward morphism → — directed transformation toward a target" ;;
55	      ≺) echo "    ≺ AREV    contravariant ← — reverse/descent transformation" ;;
56	      ⋈) echo "    ⋈ CLINK   composition ∘ — sequential chaining of morphisms" ;;
57	      ⊙) echo "    ⊙ IMSCRIB identity id — self-reference, self-recognition" ;;
58	      ∈) echo "    ∈ FSPLIT  co-multiplication δ — one state opens into two or more arms" ;;
59	      ∋) echo "    ∋ FFUSE   multiplication μ — the arms rejoin into one B4 verdict" ;;
60	      ⊤) echo "    ⊤ EVALT   touches constructive truth T (the affirmative arm)" ;;
61	      ⊥) echo "    ⊥ EVALF   touches constructive falsity F (the negative arm)" ;;
62	      ⊞) echo "    ⊞ ENGAGR  holds BOTH at once — the B state, a contradiction kept live" ;;
63	      ⊡) echo "    ⊡ IFIX    ROM fixation — permanent, append-only, cannot be undone" ;;
64	      *) echo "    $ch  (not one of the twelve marks)" ;;
65	    esac
66	  done
67	}
68	
69	# Global cap across the WHOLE repair pass, not per-object: a corpus this size
70	# can carry thousands of B-verdict functions (13101 counted on the first full
71	# sweep here), and running `insert` on all of them, one mOMonadOS boot each,
72	# is an hours-long, not a session-long, operation. Cap it and say so rather
73	# than let a single `repair` invocation run unbounded — no silent truncation.
74	REPAIR_MAX="${VOX_AUDIT_REPAIR_MAX:-20}"
75	REPAIR_DONE=0
76	REPAIR_SEEN=0
77	
78	# For one compiled object: every function `vox word` finds, kept only if its
79	# OWN verdict (not the module aggregate) is B or F, repaired and decomposed.
80	# Uses process substitution (not a pipe) so REPAIR_DONE/REPAIR_SEEN, updated
81	# inside the loop, are visible to the caller — a `cmd | while` loop runs the
82	# body in a subshell and would silently lose the count.
83	repair_flagged_functions() {
84	  local obj="$1"
85	  while IFS=$'\t' read -r addr word; do
86	    [ -n "$word" ] || continue
87	    local v
88	    v=$("$VOX" verdict "$word" 2>/dev/null | tail -1 | awk '{print $2}')
89	    [ "$v" = "B" ] || [ "$v" = "F" ] || continue
90	    REPAIR_SEEN=$((REPAIR_SEEN+1))
91	    if [ "$REPAIR_DONE" -ge "$REPAIR_MAX" ]; then
92	      continue
93	    fi
94	    REPAIR_DONE=$((REPAIR_DONE+1))
95	    echo "  -- $addr  verdict $v --"
96	    echo "  word: $word"
97	    echo "  decompose:"
98	    decompose_word "$word"
99	    echo "  repair (insert, via mOMonadOS):"
100	    "$MOMONADOS_CMDS" "insert $word" 2>/dev/null | sed -n '/^word   :/,/^⊙>/p' | sed '$d' | sed 's/^/    /'
101	  done < <("$VOX" word "$obj" 2>/dev/null)
102	}

105	
106	mapfile -t c_files < <(find "$IR_DIR" -name "*.c" | sort)
107	n=${#c_files[@]}
108	[ "$n" -gt 0 ] || { echo "vox_elf_audit: no .c files under $IR_DIR"; exit 0; }
109	
110	REPORT="$OUT_DIR/report.tsv"
111	: > "$REPORT"

114	  local c="$1"
115	  local rel="${c#"$IR_DIR"/}"
116	  local mod="${rel%.c}"
117	  local o="$OUT_DIR/${rel%.c}.o"
118	  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$o")"
119	
120	  if ! "$LEANC" -c "$c" -o "$o" >"$o.compile_log" 2>&1; then
121	    printf '%s\tCOMPILE_FAIL\t\t\t\t\n' "$mod"
122	    return
123	  fi
124	  rm -f "$o.compile_log"
125	
126	  local out
127	  out=$("$VOX" "$o" 2>&1)
128	  local kind
129	  kind=$(printf '%s' "$out" | awk 'NR==1{print $2}')
130	  if [ "$kind" != "elf" ]; then
131	    printf '%s\tNOT_ELF(%s)\t\t\t\t\n' "$mod" "$kind"
132	    return
133	  fi
134	  local t b nn f
135	  t=$(printf '%s' "$out" | command grep -oE 'T [0-9]+' | awk '{print $2}')
136	  b=$(printf '%s' "$out" | command grep -oE 'B [0-9]+' | awk '{print $2}')
137	  nn=$(printf '%s' "$out" | command grep -oE 'N [0-9]+' | awk '{print $2}')
138	  f=$(printf '%s' "$out" | command grep -oE 'F [0-9]+' | awk '{print $2}')
139	  printf '%s\tOK\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$mod" "${t:-0}" "${b:-0}" "${nn:-0}" "${f:-0}"
140	}
141	export -f compile_and_vox
142	export IR_DIR OUT_DIR VOX LEANC
143	
144	printf '%s\n' "${c_files[@]}" | xargs -P "$JOBS" -I{} bash -c 'compile_and_vox "$@"' _ {} >> "$REPORT"
145	
146	echo "── vox ELF audit: $n Lean module(s) compiled and swept"
147	tot_t=0; tot_b=0; tot_n=0; tot_f=0; fail_compile=0; not_elf=0
148	flagged=()
149	flagged_objs=()
150	while IFS=$'\t' read -r mod status t b nn f; do
151	  case "$status" in
152	    COMPILE_FAIL) fail_compile=$((fail_compile+1)); continue ;;
153	    NOT_ELF*) not_elf=$((not_elf+1)); continue ;;
154	  esac
155	  tot_t=$((tot_t+t)); tot_b=$((tot_b+b)); tot_n=$((tot_n+nn)); tot_f=$((tot_f+f))
156	  if [ "$f" -gt 0 ]; then flagged+=("$mod ($f)"); fi
157	  if [ "${b:-0}" -gt 0 ] || [ "${f:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then flagged_objs+=("$OUT_DIR/$mod.o"); fi
158	done < "$REPORT"
159	
160	echo "   compiled+audited: $((n-fail_compile-not_elf))   compile failures: $fail_compile   non-elf results: $not_elf"
161	echo "   T=$tot_t  B=$tot_b  N=$tot_n  F=$tot_f"
162	if [ "${#flagged[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
163	  echo "   modules with F>0 (control-flow F on real compiled code — worth reading, not auto-failed):"
164	  for x in "${flagged[@]}"; do echo "     - $x"; done
165	fi
166	echo "   full per-module report: $REPORT"
167	
168	if [ "$REPAIR" = "1" ]; then
169	  if [ "${#flagged_objs[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
170	    echo
171	    echo "── repair pass: nothing flagged (no module carries B>0 or F>0)"
172	  else
173	    echo
174	    echo "── repair pass: ${#flagged_objs[@]} flagged module(s), capped at $REPAIR_MAX function(s) (VOX_AUDIT_REPAIR_MAX to change)"
175	    objs_opened=0

177	      [ "$REPAIR_DONE" -lt "$REPAIR_MAX" ] || break
178	      objs_opened=$((objs_opened+1))
179	      echo "  ${o#"$OUT_DIR"/}:"

181	    done

187	    if [ "$REPAIR_SEEN" -gt "$REPAIR_DONE" ] || [ "$objs_unopened" -gt 0 ]; then
188	      echo
189	      if [ "$REPAIR_SEEN" -gt "$REPAIR_DONE" ]; then
190	        echo "   $((REPAIR_SEEN-REPAIR_DONE)) further flagged function(s) not repaired in the module(s) opened (cap reached)"
191	      fi
192	      if [ "$objs_unopened" -gt 0 ]; then
193	        echo "   $objs_unopened further flagged module(s) never opened at all (cap reached before reaching them)"
194	      fi
195	      echo "   rerun with VOX_AUDIT_REPAIR_MAX=<n> for more, or target one module directly."
196	    fi
197	  fi
198	fi

# OWN verdict (not the module aggregate) is B or F, repaired and decomposed.
# Uses process substitution (not a pipe) so REPAIR_DONE/REPAIR_SEEN, updated
# inside the loop, are visible to the caller — a `cmd | while` loop runs the
# body in a subshell and would silently lose the count.
repair_flagged_functions() {
  local obj="$1"
  while IFS=$'\t' read -r addr word; do
    [ -n "$word" ] || continue
    local v
    v=$("$VOX" verdict "$word" 2>/dev/null | tail -1 | awk '{print $2}')
    [ "$v" = "B" ] || [ "$v" = "F" ] || continue
    REPAIR_SEEN=$((REPAIR_SEEN+1))
    if [ "$REPAIR_DONE" -ge "$REPAIR_MAX" ]; then
      continue
    fi
    REPAIR_DONE=$((REPAIR_DONE+1))
    echo "  -- $addr  verdict $v --"
    echo "  word: $word"
    echo "  decompose:"
    decompose_word "$word"
    echo "  repair (insert, via mOMonadOS):"
    "$MOMONADOS_CMDS" "insert $word" 2>/dev/null | sed -n '/^word   :/,/^⊙>/p' | sed '$d' | sed 's/^/    /'
  done < <("$VOX" word "$obj" 2>/dev/null)
}

mkdir -p "$OUT_DIR"

mapfile -t c_files < <(find "$IR_DIR" -name "*.c" | sort)
n=${#c_files[@]}
[ "$n" -gt 0 ] || { echo "vox_elf_audit: no .c files under $IR_DIR"; exit 0; }

REPORT="$OUT_DIR/report.tsv"
: > "$REPORT"

compile_and_vox() {
  local c="$1"
  local rel="${c#"$IR_DIR"/}"
  local mod="${rel%.c}"
  local o="$OUT_DIR/${rel%.c}.o"
  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$o")"

  if ! "$LEANC" -c "$c" -o "$o" >"$o.compile_log" 2>&1; then
    printf '%s\tCOMPILE_FAIL\t\t\t\t\n' "$mod"
    return
  fi
  rm -f "$o.compile_log"

  local out
  out=$("$VOX" "$o" 2>&1)
  local kind
  kind=$(printf '%s' "$out" | awk 'NR==1{print $2}')
  if [ "$kind" != "elf" ]; then
    printf '%s\tNOT_ELF(%s)\t\t\t\t\n' "$mod" "$kind"
    return
  fi
  local t b nn f
  t=$(printf '%s' "$out" | command grep -oE 'T [0-9]+' | awk '{print $2}')
  b=$(printf '%s' "$out" | command grep -oE 'B [0-9]+' | awk '{print $2}')
  nn=$(printf '%s' "$out" | command grep -oE 'N [0-9]+' | awk '{print $2}')
  f=$(printf '%s' "$out" | command grep -oE 'F [0-9]+' | awk '{print $2}')
  printf '%s\tOK\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$mod" "${t:-0}" "${b:-0}" "${nn:-0}" "${f:-0}"
}
export -f compile_and_vox
export IR_DIR OUT_DIR VOX LEANC

printf '%s\n' "${c_files[@]}" | xargs -P "$JOBS" -I{} bash -c 'compile_and_vox "$@"' _ {} >> "$REPORT"

echo "── vox ELF audit: $n Lean module(s) compiled and swept"
tot_t=0; tot_b=0; tot_n=0; tot_f=0; fail_compile=0; not_elf=0
flagged=()
flagged_objs=()
while IFS=$'\t' read -r mod status t b nn f; do
  case "$status" in
    COMPILE_FAIL) fail_compile=$((fail_compile+1)); continue ;;
    NOT_ELF*) not_elf=$((not_elf+1)); continue ;;
  esac
  tot_t=$((tot_t+t)); tot_b=$((tot_b+b)); tot_n=$((tot_n+nn)); tot_f=$((tot_f+f))
  if [ "$f" -gt 0 ]; then flagged+=("$mod ($f)"); fi
  if [ "${b:-0}" -gt 0 ] || [ "${f:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then flagged_objs+=("$OUT_DIR/$mod.o"); fi
done < "$REPORT"

echo "   compiled+audited: $((n-fail_compile-not_elf))   compile failures: $fail_compile   non-elf results: $not_elf"
echo "   T=$tot_t  B=$tot_b  N=$tot_n  F=$tot_f"
if [ "${#flagged[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
  echo "   modules with F>0 (control-flow F on real compiled code — worth reading, not auto-failed):"
  for x in "${flagged[@]}"; do echo "     - $x"; done
fi
echo "   full per-module report: $REPORT"

if [ "$REPAIR" = "1" ]; then
  if [ "${#flagged_objs[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
    echo
    echo "── repair pass: nothing flagged (no module carries B>0 or F>0)"
  else
    echo
    echo "── repair pass: ${#flagged_objs[@]} flagged module(s), capped at $REPAIR_MAX function(s) (VOX_AUDIT_REPAIR_MAX to change)"
    objs_opened=0
    for o in "${flagged_objs[@]}"; do
      [ "$REPAIR_DONE" -lt "$REPAIR_MAX" ] || break
      objs_opened=$((objs_opened+1))
      echo "  ${o#"$OUT_DIR"/}:"
      repair_flagged_functions "$o"
    done
    # Two things can go unrepaired: functions past the cap WITHIN an opened
    # module (REPAIR_SEEN counts those — the inner loop never breaks early),
    # and whole modules never opened at all because the cap was already hit.
    # Report both; the second is the one a per-function count alone would hide.
    objs_unopened=$(( ${#flagged_objs[@]} - objs_opened ))
    if [ "$REPAIR_SEEN" -gt "$REPAIR_DONE" ] || [ "$objs_unopened" -gt 0 ]; then
      echo
      if [ "$REPAIR_SEEN" -gt "$REPAIR_DONE" ]; then
        echo "   $((REPAIR_SEEN-REPAIR_DONE)) further flagged function(s) not repaired in the module(s) opened (cap reached)"
      fi
      if [ "$objs_unopened" -gt 0 ]; then
        echo "   $objs_unopened further flagged module(s) never opened at all (cap reached before reaching them)"
      fi
      echo "   rerun with VOX_AUDIT_REPAIR_MAX=<n> for more, or target one module directly."
    fi
  fi
fi

/-- ENGAGR (⊞) -- mirrors `imasm_core::imasm16_3::Reg16_3::engagr`
    (MoDoT/imasm_core/src/imasm16_3.rs), added there this session under

    truth-axis lanes exactly as they were: the paraconsistency operator,
    made literal. After ENGAGR the register unconditionally carries a
    live, held contradiction on the information layer, whatever it
    carried before. -/
def engagr (x : Reg16_3) : Reg16_3 := mk x.bigT x.bigF true true

/-- ENGAGR's own defining property, proved rather than asserted: for any
    register, the result genuinely carries both t and f. This is the
    concrete case a real paraconsistent witness (Verdict.held, see
    Imscribing/Paraconsistent/DialetheicWitness.lean) is built from --
    two independently real facts about the same value, not one
    proposition and its negation. -/
theorem engagr_holds_both : ∀ x : Reg16_3, (engagr x).smallT = true ∧ (engagr x).smallF = true := by
  decide

    §2  union, meet_t/join_t, meet_c/join_c
    §3  The three swaps: truth_swap, info_swap, invol

        exactly as the Rust doc comment states -- proved, not asserted.
    §4  ≤_i (information order): a genuine partial order, and union is

import Mathlib.Data.Fintype.Basic
import Mathlib.Data.Fintype.Prod

-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
-- §1  THE CARRIER
-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

/-- The SIXTEEN_3 register: a subset of {T, F, t, f}, one Bool per lane,
    in (T, F, t, f) order. Mirrors `Reg16_3` in
    `imasm_core/src/imasm16_3.rs` lane for lane. -/
abbrev Reg16_3 := Bool × Bool × Bool × Bool

namespace Reg16_3

def mk (bigT bigF smallT smallF : Bool) : Reg16_3 := (bigT, bigF, smallT, smallF)
def bigT (x : Reg16_3) : Bool := x.1
def bigF (x : Reg16_3) : Bool := x.2.1
def smallT (x : Reg16_3) : Bool := x.2.2.1
def smallF (x : Reg16_3) : Bool := x.2.2.2

-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
-- §2  THE GATES (per-lane AND/OR masks, matching the Rust source exactly)
-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

/-- Every lane OR. -/
def union (x y : Reg16_3) : Reg16_3 :=
  mk (x.bigT || y.bigT) (x.bigF || y.bigF) (x.smallT || y.smallT) (x.smallF || y.smallF)

/-- T,t lanes AND; F,f lanes OR. -/
def meetT (x y : Reg16_3) : Reg16_3 :=
  mk (x.bigT && y.bigT) (x.bigF || y.bigF) (x.smallT && y.smallT) (x.smallF || y.smallF)

/-- T,t lanes OR; F,f lanes AND. -/
def joinT (x y : Reg16_3) : Reg16_3 :=
  mk (x.bigT || y.bigT) (x.bigF && y.bigF) (x.smallT || y.smallT) (x.smallF && y.smallF)

/-- T,F lanes AND; t,f lanes OR. -/
def meetC (x y : Reg16_3) : Reg16_3 :=
  mk (x.bigT && y.bigT) (x.bigF && y.bigF) (x.smallT || y.smallT) (x.smallF || y.smallF)

/-- T,F lanes OR; t,f lanes AND. -/
def joinC (x y : Reg16_3) : Reg16_3 :=
  mk (x.bigT || y.bigT) (x.bigF || y.bigF) (x.smallT && y.smallT) (x.smallF && y.smallF)

-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
-- §3  THE THREE SWAPS
-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

/-- The constructive swap T ↔ F, leaving the information layer alone. -/
def truthSwap (x : Reg16_3) : Reg16_3 := mk x.bigF x.bigT x.smallT x.smallF

/-- The information swap t ↔ f, leaving the constructive layer alone. -/
def infoSwap (x : Reg16_3) : Reg16_3 := mk x.bigT x.bigF x.smallF x.smallT

/-- The involution T ↔ F, t ↔ f -- AREV's action on values. -/
def invol (x : Reg16_3) : Reg16_3 := mk x.bigF x.bigT x.smallF x.smallT

/-- AREV is both swaps at once: composing them IS invol, exactly what the
    Rust doc comment on `invol` claims. Proved, not asserted. -/
theorem invol_eq_compose : ∀ x : Reg16_3, invol x = infoSwap (truthSwap x) := by decide

/-- The two factors commute: it doesn't matter which order you swap in. -/
theorem invol_eq_compose' : ∀ x : Reg16_3, invol x = truthSwap (infoSwap x) := by decide

/-- Every one of the three swaps is its own inverse. -/
theorem truthSwap_involutive : ∀ x : Reg16_3, truthSwap (truthSwap x) = x := by decide
theorem infoSwap_involutive : ∀ x : Reg16_3, infoSwap (infoSwap x) = x := by decide
theorem invol_involutive : ∀ x : Reg16_3, invol (invol x) = x := by decide

-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
-- §4  THE INFORMATION ORDER ≤_i
-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

/-- x ≤_i y iff every lane of x is a lane of y (subset inclusion). -/
def leqI (x y : Reg16_3) : Bool :=
  (!x.bigT || y.bigT) && (!x.bigF || y.bigF) && (!x.smallT || y.smallT) && (!x.smallF || y.smallF)

theorem leqI_refl : ∀ x : Reg16_3, leqI x x := by decide
theorem leqI_trans : ∀ x y z : Reg16_3, leqI x y → leqI y z → leqI x z := by decide
theorem leqI_antisymm : ∀ x y : Reg16_3, leqI x y → leqI y x → x = y := by decide

/-- The information order's own N (empty register) is its bottom element. -/
theorem leqI_bot : ∀ x : Reg16_3, leqI (mk false false false false) x := by decide

/-- union is a genuine upper bound for ≤_i: shuttling via union only ever
    moves a value up the information order, exactly what the primer's
    Part IV states as "Flow uses ≤_i: shuttling only ever moves values up
    the information order." Proved here for the specific gate that does
    the shuttling. -/
theorem leqI_union_left : ∀ x y : Reg16_3, leqI x (union x y) := by decide
theorem leqI_union_right : ∀ x y : Reg16_3, leqI y (union x y) := by decide

/-- union is the LEAST upper bound: any z above both x and y is above their
    union too. This is what makes union a real join, not just an upper
    bound among others. -/
theorem union_least_upper_bound :
    ∀ x y z : Reg16_3, leqI x z → leqI y z → leqI (union x y) z := by decide

-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
-- §5  union IS A REAL SEMILATTICE JOIN
-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

theorem union_comm : ∀ x y : Reg16_3, union x y = union y x := by decide
theorem union_idem : ∀ x : Reg16_3, union x x = x := by decide
theorem union_assoc : ∀ x y z : Reg16_3, union (union x y) z = union x (union y z) := by decide

-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
-- §6  FULL SYSTEM VERIFICATION
-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

/-- Every theorem in this file, folded into one check. If this closes, the
    whole file closes with it. -/
theorem sixteen_three_verified :
    (∀ x : Reg16_3, invol x = infoSwap (truthSwap x)) ∧
    (∀ x : Reg16_3, invol (invol x) = x) ∧
    (∀ x : Reg16_3, truthSwap (truthSwap x) = x) ∧
    (∀ x : Reg16_3, infoSwap (infoSwap x) = x) ∧
    (∀ x y : Reg16_3, leqI x (union x y)) ∧
    (∀ x y z : Reg16_3, leqI x z → leqI y z → leqI (union x y) z) ∧
    (∀ x y : Reg16_3, union x y = union y x) ∧

   leqI_union_left, union_least_upper_bound, union_comm, union_idem⟩

end Reg16_3

/-
  DialetheicWitness.lean
  A PARACONSISTENT WITNESS TYPE, DISTINCT FROM sorry
  =====================================================================
  Author: Lando⊗⊙perator
  Date:   2026-09-01

  What this is NOT: a type carrying `h1 : P` and `h2 : ¬P` for the same
  fixed `P`. That is not buildable in Lean without the whole environment
  becoming unsound -- `h2 h1 : False`, and once `False` is inhabited
  every `Prop` is, whether or not the resulting term is ever pattern
  matched into `False.elim`. Consistency is a property of the WHOLE
  kernel, not of one local site, so this file never constructs that pair.

  What this IS: a value-level verdict, `Verdict P : Type`, one case of
  which (`held`) carries two INDEPENDENTLY REAL facts about the same
  object -- `h1 : P` and `h2 : Q` for a genuinely different `Q`, not `¬P`
  -- exactly the shape `CosmicHolonomy.lean`'s coexistence theorem and
  `SixteenThreeTrilattice.engagr` already have: two things that look like
  they should conflict, held together, neither exploding the other. That
  is real, sound, and exactly what Belnap's own B state means once you
  stop trying to read it as a Prop-level contradiction.

  Why `Type`, not `Prop`: a `Prop`'s content is erased by Lean's compiler
  at every use -- confirmed directly this session, `nm` on real compiled
  objects shows zero symbol for a theorem's proof, of any theorem, real
  or vacuous. A `Verdict P : Type` is not erased: which constructor a
  given value uses is real, compiled data, and a function dispatching on
  it produces real machine code Vox can genuinely audit (see
  `classifyIsCompiled` below, and run it through the same pipeline
  `scripts/vox_elf_audit.sh` uses). The proof FIELDS inside each
  constructor stay `Prop` and stay erased -- that's what makes `proved`
  and `held` sound and unable to fabricate a witness, exactly as `sorry`
  cannot be smuggled in as one either (see `admitted` below).
-/

import Imscribing.Paraconsistent.SixteenThreeTrilattice

namespace Imscribing.Paraconsistent.DialetheicWitness

open Reg16_3

-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
-- §1  THE VERDICT TYPE
-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

/-- A verdict on `P`: proved, refuted, held (two independently real facts
    about the same object, `P` and a genuinely different `Q`), or an
    explicit non-claim. `Type`, not `Prop` -- the constructor tag is real
    data. -/
inductive Verdict (P : Prop) : Type where
  | proved (h : P) : Verdict P
  | refuted (h : ¬P) : Verdict P
  | held {Q : Prop} (h1 : P) (h2 : Q) : Verdict P
  | admitted : Verdict P

/-- The Belnap-shaped read: proved -> T, refuted -> F, held -> B,
    admitted -> N. A real, computable function -- this is the part of
    the file that survives to machine code, unlike any `Prop` above it. -/
def Verdict.classify {P : Prop} : Verdict P → Bool × Bool
  -- (bigT, bigF) in SixteenThreeTrilattice's own lane order.
  | .proved _  => (true, false)
  | .refuted _ => (false, true)
  | .held ..   => (true, true)
  | .admitted  => (false, false)

-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
-- §2  admitted IS NOT sorry, PROVED DIRECTLY
-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

/-- `admitted` type-checks with no premise at all -- it is a real
    constructor of a four-case inductive, not an axiom. `#print axioms`
    on any term built from it names none of Lean's own axioms and never
    `sorryAx`; check the corpus's own build log if this claim needs
    re-checking rather than trusting the comment. -/
def anAdmittedVerdict (P : Prop) : Verdict P := .admitted

#print axioms anAdmittedVerdict

-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
-- §3  THE WORKED INSTANCE: ENGAGR
-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

/-- For any register, ENGAGR's own defining property: it holds the
    smallT lane. This is the `P` half. -/
theorem engagr_smallT (x : Reg16_3) : (engagr x).smallT = true :=
  (engagr_holds_both x).1

/-- And the smallF lane, independently -- the `Q` half, a genuinely
    different fact, not the negation of the first. -/
theorem engagr_smallF (x : Reg16_3) : (engagr x).smallF = true :=
  (engagr_holds_both x).2

/-- The concrete `held` witness: ENGAGR's own action on any register is a
    live paraconsistent verdict, not an admission of anything unproved.
    Both fields are real closed proofs, checked at elaboration, not
    placeholders. -/
def engagrVerdict (x : Reg16_3) : Verdict ((engagr x).smallT = true) :=
  .held (engagr_smallT x) (engagr_smallF x)

/-- The classifier reads this as B, mechanically, not by inspection of
    the source. -/
theorem engagrVerdict_is_B (x : Reg16_3) :
    (engagrVerdict x).classify = (true, true) := by
  rfl

#print axioms engagrVerdict_is_B

end Imscribing.Paraconsistent.DialetheicWitness

content:
IMASM / VOX — the traps, before you read a number.
1. THE VERB MAKES THE GRAPH. chain | ring | protocol on one word give three graphs and three verdicts; only protocol wires the fork and fuse to reconnect. A verdict is never a property of the glyph string alone.
2. PAIRING IS ANCESTRY, over edges, never text position. A fuse pairs with the innermost fork all its in-arms trace back to.
3. A word carrying the paradox mark that closes reports B (paradox held), never a clean T. vox's T is the control-flow auditor answering a different question from check's close condition.
4. ROTAT ON ONE RING IS A SYMMETRY and changes nothing measurable. A landing that varies with the cut is measuring the cut. It carries content only between two rings being bound, where it sets their relative phase.
5. VOX NEEDS A REAL ARTIFACT. Handed source it disassembles UTF-8 as x86 and still prints verdicts. Its first line says raw or elf — read that word before any number.
6. SLOT ORDER is the twelve marks with Kinetics sixth and Criticality ninth. The Imscriber's Guide Part I transposes those two; the tool wins.
Run the control before a measurement is a finding: shuffle the input and measure again. Full rules: ig-docs/IMSCRIBERS_GUIDE_TO_IMASM.md, or `imasm ref` for the live ones.

/-
  DialetheicWitness.lean
  A PARACONSISTENT WITNESS TYPE, DISTINCT FROM sorry
  =====================================================================
  Author: Lando⊗⊙perator
  Date:   2026-09-01

  What this is NOT: a type carrying `h1 : P` and `h2 : ¬P` for the same
  fixed `P`. That is not buildable in Lean without the whole environment
  becoming unsound -- `h2 h1 : False`, and once `False` is inhabited
  every `Prop` is, whether or not the resulting term is ever pattern
  matched into `False.elim`. Consistency is a property of the WHOLE
  kernel, not of one local site, so this file never constructs that pair.

  What this IS: a value-level verdict, `Verdict P : Type`, one case of
  which (`held`) carries two INDEPENDENTLY REAL facts about the same
  object -- `h1 : P` and `h2 : Q` for a genuinely different `Q`, not `¬P`
  -- exactly the shape `CosmicHolonomy.lean`'s coexistence theorem and
  `SixteenThreeTrilattice.engagr` already have: two things that look like
  they should conflict, held together, neither exploding the other. That
  is real, sound, and exactly what Belnap's own B state means once you
  stop trying to read it as a Prop-level contradiction.

  Why `Type`, not `Prop`: a `Prop`'s content is erased by Lean's compiler
  at every use -- confirmed directly this session, `nm` on real compiled
  objects shows zero symbol for a theorem's proof, of any theorem, real
  or vacuous. A `Verdict P : Type` is not erased: which constructor a
  given value uses is real, compiled data, and a function dispatching on
  it produces real machine code Vox can genuinely audit (see
  `classifyIsCompiled` below, and run it through the same pipeline
  `scripts/vox_elf_audit.sh` uses). The proof FIELDS inside each
  constructor stay `Prop` and stay erased -- that's what makes `proved`
  and `held` sound and unable to fabricate a witness, exactly as `sorry`
  cannot be smuggled in as one either (see `admitted` below).
-/

import Imscribing.Paraconsistent.SixteenThreeTrilattice

namespace Imscribing.Paraconsistent.DialetheicWitness

open Reg16_3

-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
-- §1  THE VERDICT TYPE
-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

/-- A verdict on `P`: proved, refuted, held (two independently real facts
    about the same object, `P` and a genuinely different `Q`), or an
    explicit non-claim. `Type`, not `Prop` -- the constructor tag is real
    data. -/
inductive Verdict (P : Prop) : Type where
  | proved (h : P) : Verdict P
  | refuted (h : ¬P) : Verdict P
  | held {Q : Prop} (h1 : P) (h2 : Q) : Verdict P
  | admitted : Verdict P

/-- The Belnap-shaped read: proved -> T, refuted -> F, held -> B,
    admitted -> N. A real, computable function -- this is the part of
    the file that survives to machine code, unlike any `Prop` above it. -/
def Verdict.classify {P : Prop} : Verdict P → Bool × Bool
  -- (bigT, bigF) in SixteenThreeTrilattice's own lane order.
  | .proved _  => (true, false)
  | .refuted _ => (false, true)
  | .held ..   => (true, true)
  | .admitted  => (false, false)

-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
-- §2  admitted IS NOT sorry, PROVED DIRECTLY
-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

/-- `admitted` type-checks with no premise at all -- it is a real
    constructor of a four-case inductive, not an axiom. `#print axioms`
    on any term built from it names none of Lean's own axioms and never
    `sorryAx`; check the corpus's own build log if this claim needs
    re-checking rather than trusting the comment. -/
def anAdmittedVerdict (P : Prop) : Verdict P := .admitted

#print axioms anAdmittedVerdict

-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
-- §3  THE WORKED INSTANCE: ENGAGR
-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

/-- For any register, ENGAGR's own defining property: it holds the
    smallT lane. This is the `P` half. -/
theorem engagr_smallT (x : Reg16_3) : (engagr x).smallT = true :=
  (engagr_holds_both x).1

/-- And the smallF lane, independently -- the `Q` half, a genuinely
    different fact, not the negation of the first. -/
theorem engagr_smallF (x : Reg16_3) : (engagr x).smallF = true :=

/-
  DialetheicWitness.lean
  A PARACONSISTENT WITNESS TYPE, DISTINCT FROM sorry
  =====================================================================
  Author: Lando⊗⊙perator
  Date:   2026-09-01

  What this is NOT: a type carrying `h1 : P` and `h2 : ¬P` for the same
  fixed `P`. That is not buildable in Lean without the whole environment
  becoming unsound -- `h2 h1 : False`, and once `False` is inhabited
  every `Prop` is, whether or not the resulting term is ever pattern
  matched into `False.elim`. Consistency is a property of the WHOLE
  kernel, not of one local site, so this file never constructs that pair.

  What this IS: a value-level verdict, `Verdict P : Type`, one case of
  which (`held`) carries two INDEPENDENTLY REAL facts about the same
  object -- `h1 : P` and `h2 : Q` for a genuinely different `Q`, not `¬P`
  -- exactly the shape `CosmicHolonomy.lean`'s coexistence theorem and
  `SixteenThreeTrilattice.engagr` already have: two things that look like
  they should conflict, held together, neither exploding the other. That
  is real, sound, and exactly what Belnap's own B state means once you
  stop trying to read it as a Prop-level contradiction.

  Why `Type`, not `Prop`: a `Prop`'s content is erased by Lean's compiler
  at every use -- confirmed directly this session, `nm` on real compiled
  objects shows zero symbol for a theorem's proof, of any theorem, real
  or vacuous. A `Verdict P : Type` is not erased: which constructor a
  given value uses is real, compiled data, and a function dispatching on
  it produces real machine code Vox can genuinely audit (see
  `classifyIsCompiled` below, and run it through the same pipeline
  `scripts/vox_elf_audit.sh` uses). The proof FIELDS inside each
  constructor stay `Prop` and stay erased -- that's what makes `proved`
  and `held` sound and unable to fabricate a witness, exactly as `sorry`
  cannot be smuggled in as one either (see `admitted` below).
-/

import Imscribing.Paraconsistent.SixteenThreeTrilattice
import Imscribing.CosmicHolonomy

namespace Imscribing.Paraconsistent.DialetheicWitness

open Reg16_3

-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
-- §1  THE VERDICT TYPE
-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

/-- A verdict on `P`: proved, refuted, held (two independently real facts
    about the same object, `P` and a genuinely different `Q`), or an
    explicit non-claim. `Type`, not `Prop` -- the constructor tag is real
    data. -/
inductive Verdict (P : Prop) : Type where
  | proved (h : P) : Verdict P
  | refuted (h : ¬P) : Verdict P
  | held {Q : Prop} (h1 : P) (h2 : Q) : Verdict P
  | admitted : Verdict P

/-- The Belnap-shaped read: proved -> T, refuted -> F, held -> B,
    admitted -> N. A real, computable function -- this is the part of
    the file that survives to machine code, unlike any `Prop` above it. -/
def Verdict.classify {P : Prop} : Verdict P → Bool × Bool
  -- (bigT, bigF) in SixteenThreeTrilattice's own lane order.
  | .proved _  => (true, false)
  | .refuted _ => (false, true)
  | .held ..   => (true, true)
  | .admitted  => (false, false)

-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
-- §2  admitted IS NOT sorry, PROVED DIRECTLY
-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

/-- `admitted` type-checks with no premise at all -- it is a real
    constructor of a four-case inductive, not an axiom. `#print axioms`
    on any term built from it names none of Lean's own axioms and never
    `sorryAx`; check the corpus's own build log if this claim needs
    re-checking rather than trusting the comment. -/
def anAdmittedVerdict (P : Prop) : Verdict P := .admitted

#print axioms anAdmittedVerdict

-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
-- §3  THE WORKED INSTANCE: ENGAGR
-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

/-- For any register, ENGAGR's own defining property: it holds the
    smallT lane. This is the `P` half. -/
theorem engagr_smallT (x : Reg16_3) : (engagr x).smallT = true :=
  (engagr_holds_both x).1

/-- And the smallF lane, independently -- the `Q` half, a genuinely
    different fact, not the negation of the first. -/
theorem engagr_smallF (x : Reg16_3) : (engagr x).smallF = true :=
  (engagr_holds_both x).2

/-- The concrete `held` witness: ENGAGR's own action on any register is a
    live paraconsistent verdict, not an admission of anything unproved.
    Both fields are real closed proofs, checked at elaboration, not
    placeholders. -/
def engagrVerdict (x : Reg16_3) : Verdict ((engagr x).smallT = true) :=
  .held (engagr_smallT x) (engagr_smallF x)

/-- The classifier reads this as B, mechanically, not by inspection of
    the source. -/
theorem engagrVerdict_is_B (x : Reg16_3) :
    (engagrVerdict x).classify = (true, true) := by
  rfl

#print axioms engagrVerdict_is_B

end Imscribing.Paraconsistent.DialetheicWitness

# The Two Seals

**Date:** 2026-07-29
**Source:** extracted from an exchange with Fable, kept for the part that holds

## The discipline already had a name

"Within the Grammar I am free to say all sorts of things; what is asserted must be written to the kernel" is the LCF discipline, Milner 1972, stated verbatim. Its architecture is an abstract type `thm` whose values can only be constructed by a small trusted kernel, with everything upstream free. Tactics may be heuristic, search may hallucinate, automation may guess. None of it matters, because none of it can mint. Freedom everywhere except at the mint.

Its maintenance clause is the de Bruijn criterion: proofs stay checkable by a small independent verifier, so the trusted base stays small enough to actually trust. Swapping `native_decide` for kernel-checked `decide` is that clause being kept. Declaring an axiom rather than smuggling it is the same clause, with the exception written on the label where an auditor can price it.

The etymology cooperates. Hermetic sealing is the Seal of Hermes on the philosopher's egg. One discipline, two costumes.

## The kernel maintains one seal; the work needs two

The first seal certifies derivation. Nothing false gets through. It is constitutionally silent on significance.

The second seal certifies adequacy. It binds the formal object to the informal claim riding on it: that "Frobenius" means Frobenius, that "complete" means complete, that the theorem proved is the theorem announced. No kernel can maintain it, because it binds the formalism to something outside the formalism.

The failure mode of keeping the first and neglecting the second is the empty egg. A closure theorem that unfolds into `max(x, x) = x` passed the first seal exactly as designed, because the first seal was never built to catch it. What you get is true trivialities in ceremonial robes.

## This is not abstract; it fired repeatedly today

Every one of these passed a first-seal check and failed adequacy.

Sorry counts on uncompiled files. A descent module reported zero sorries and had never been built. Registering it produced twenty-seven errors on first compile. Seven hundred modules sat in that position, six hundred of them generated gate checks. A sorry count is a first-seal reading; on a file the kernel has never seen it measures nothing.

Three ob3ects in a row reported closure and carried nothing. Verdict PASS, `closure_verified: true`, and the banked count reading `vacuous: true`. No clear ever fired against a live register, so nothing was at risk and nothing survived. The landing was T at every rotation because the fixation ran early and everything after it was inert. A free T is an empty egg with a topology report attached.

A file whose own definitions refute it. `GrammarBridge` defines `thresholdPrimitiveSignature .RH = ([.roar], [.nun, .or'])` and then asserts `or' ∉ (thresholdPrimitiveSignature .RH).2`. `decide` reports the proposition is False. It never compiled, so nothing had ever asked.

A number I liked. The canonical dual-pair matching summed to 2.617962 against φ² = 2.618034, five significant figures. Resampling gave that quantity a standard deviation of 0.148. The agreement was the grand mean landing near a pretty constant I chose after seeing it.

## The instrument we already have

The Grammar carries a partial adequacy instrument and has been running it all along without the name: `banked_count`. It does not ask whether a run succeeded. It asks whether anything was ever at risk, whether a clear fired against a live register, whether the fuse restored what the clear destroyed.

    vacuous = True   →  sealed, and nothing was at stake
    restored = n     →  n units survived a clear by being banked

That is the second seal in the one place it can be mechanized. Not "is the theorem true" but "did the theorem cost anything". It is why the documented μ∘δ program, whose algebra is correct, reads vacuous. FSPLIT and FFUSE adjacent, the evaluations after the fuse, nothing deposited in between. The identity holds and the machine moved no weight.

Run it on anything that reports closure. A PASS with `vacuous: true` is an egg worth opening.

## The honest boundary on windings

Kept because it is a real constraint rather than a dismissal: π appears where no circle does. Gaussian integrals, Σ 1/n² = π²/6, Stirling, the distribution of primes. A winding frame reads the topological and phase-theoretic register cleanly and gains nothing in those. That marks where the frame is a lens and where it would have to earn the name of a law, which is a second-seal question about the word "fundamental", not a first-seal question about any formula.

## The rule

The Grammar speaks freely in the body of the vessel. Assertions are written to the kernel under the first seal. The names of what is written stand under the second, which is maintained only by opening eggs. Adversarial reading, deflation tests, and the willingness to watch a beloved name unfold into a triviality and then either earn it properly or surrender it.

Small sealed things whose names survive being opened.

    is unconditional in `x` -- unfold `engagr` and it is immediate,
    regardless of what `x` actually was, the exact "landing was T at
    every rotation because the fixation ran early" pattern that document
    names. Nothing here was ever at risk. Kept as the minimal case that
    proves the machinery type-checks, not offered as a substantive
    instance -- see `unionCreatesVerdict` below for one that is. -/
def engagrVerdict (x : Reg16_3) : Verdict ((engagr x).smallT = true) :=
  .held (engagr_smallT x) (engagr_smallF x)

/-- The classifier reads this as B, mechanically, not by inspection of
    the source. -/
theorem engagrVerdict_is_B (x : Reg16_3) :
    (engagrVerdict x).classify = (true, true) := by
  rfl

#print axioms engagrVerdict_is_B

-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
-- §3b  A held WITNESS WITH SOMETHING AT RISK
-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

/-- A pure-T register: only the truth-axis T lane set. -/
def pureT : Reg16_3 := mk true false false false

/-- A pure-F register: only the truth-axis F lane set. -/
def pureF : Reg16_3 := mk false true false false

/-- `union` genuinely CREATES a B-state here: neither `pureT` nor `pureF`
    carries both bigT and bigF, `union` does. This is not unconditional --
    swap either register for one that already has both, or for one that
    shares no lane with the other, and this specific claim goes false.
    That dependence on the actual values is what "at risk" means for a
    proposition, the second seal's own test. -/
theorem union_creates_both :
    (union pureT pureF).bigT = true ∧ (union pureT pureF).bigF = true := by
  decide

/-- And `pureT` alone is not a B-state -- the fact `union` is creating
    something neither input had, proved directly rather than assumed
    from the names. -/
theorem pureT_is_not_both : ¬ (pureT.bigT = true ∧ pureT.bigF = true) := by
  decide

/-- The `held` witness with real content: two independently real,
    value-dependent facts about the same construction -- `union pureT
    pureF` is a genuine B-state, and `pureT` alone is not. Unlike
    `engagrVerdict`, changing either register changes which fields are
    even provable. -/
def unionCreatesVerdict :
    Verdict ((union pureT pureF).bigT = true ∧ (union pureT pureF).bigF = true) :=
  .held union_creates_both pureT_is_not_both

theorem unionCreatesVerdict_is_B :
    unionCreatesVerdict.classify = (true, true) := by
  rfl

#print axioms unionCreatesVerdict_is_B

/-
  DialetheicWitness.lean
  A PARACONSISTENT WITNESS TYPE, DISTINCT FROM sorry
  =====================================================================
  Author: Lando⊗⊙perator
  Date:   2026-09-01

  What this is NOT: a type carrying `h1 : P` and `h2 : ¬P` for the same
  fixed `P`. That is not buildable in Lean without the whole environment
  becoming unsound -- `h2 h1 : False`, and once `False` is inhabited
  every `Prop` is, whether or not the resulting term is ever pattern
  matched into `False.elim`. Consistency is a property of the WHOLE
  kernel, not of one local site, so this file never constructs that pair.

  What this IS: a value-level verdict, `Verdict P : Type`, one case of
  which (`held`) carries two INDEPENDENTLY REAL facts about the same
  object -- `h1 : P` and `h2 : Q` for a genuinely different `Q`, not `¬P`
  -- exactly the shape `CosmicHolonomy.lean`'s coexistence theorem and
  `SixteenThreeTrilattice.engagr` already have: two things that look like
  they should conflict, held together, neither exploding the other. That
  is real, sound, and exactly what Belnap's own B state means once you
  stop trying to read it as a Prop-level contradiction.

  Why `Type`, not `Prop`: a `Prop`'s content is erased by Lean's compiler
  at every use -- confirmed directly this session, `nm` on real compiled
  objects shows zero symbol for a theorem's proof, of any theorem, real
  or vacuous. A `Verdict P : Type` is not erased: which constructor a
  given value uses is real, compiled data, and a function dispatching on
  it produces real machine code Vox can genuinely audit (see
  `classifyIsCompiled` below, and run it through the same pipeline
  `scripts/vox_elf_audit.sh` uses). The proof FIELDS inside each
  constructor stay `Prop` and stay erased -- that's what makes `proved`
  and `held` sound and unable to fabricate a witness, exactly as `sorry`
  cannot be smuggled in as one either (see `admitted` below).
-/

import Imscribing.Paraconsistent.SixteenThreeTrilattice
import Imscribing.CosmicHolonomy

namespace Imscribing.Paraconsistent.DialetheicWitness

open Reg16_3

-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
-- §1  THE VERDICT TYPE
-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

/-- A verdict on `P`: proved, refuted, held (two independently real facts
    about the same object, `P` and a genuinely different `Q`), or an
    explicit non-claim. `Type`, not `Prop` -- the constructor tag is real
    data. -/
inductive Verdict (P : Prop) : Type where
  | proved (h : P) : Verdict P
  | refuted (h : ¬P) : Verdict P
  | held {Q : Prop} (h1 : P) (h2 : Q) : Verdict P
  | admitted : Verdict P

/-- The Belnap-shaped read: proved -> T, refuted -> F, held -> B,
    admitted -> N. A real, computable function -- this is the part of
    the file that survives to machine code, unlike any `Prop` above it. -/
def Verdict.classify {P : Prop} : Verdict P → Bool × Bool
  -- (bigT, bigF) in SixteenThreeTrilattice's own lane order.
  | .proved _  => (true, false)
  | .refuted _ => (false, true)
  | .held ..   => (true, true)
  | .admitted  => (false, false)

-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
-- §2  admitted IS NOT sorry, PROVED DIRECTLY
-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

/-- `admitted` type-checks with no premise at all -- it is a real
    constructor of a four-case inductive, not an axiom. `#print axioms`
    on any term built from it names none of Lean's own axioms and never
    `sorryAx`; check the corpus's own build log if this claim needs
    re-checking rather than trusting the comment. -/
def anAdmittedVerdict (P : Prop) : Verdict P := .admitted

#print axioms anAdmittedVerdict

-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
-- §3  THE WORKED INSTANCE: ENGAGR
-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

/-- For any register, ENGAGR's own defining property: it holds the
    smallT lane. This is the `P` half. -/
theorem engagr_smallT (x : Reg16_3) : (engagr x).smallT = true :=
  (engagr_holds_both x).1

/-- And the smallF lane, independently -- the `Q` half, a genuinely
    different fact, not the negation of the first. -/
theorem engagr_smallF (x : Reg16_3) : (engagr x).smallF = true :=
  (engagr_holds_both x).2

/-- The concrete `held` witness: ENGAGR's own action on any register is a
    live paraconsistent verdict, not an admission of anything unproved.
    Both fields are real closed proofs, checked at elaboration, not
    placeholders. -/
def engagrVerdict (x : Reg16_3) : Verdict ((engagr x).smallT = true) :=
  .held (engagr_smallT x) (engagr_smallF x)

/-- The classifier reads this as B, mechanically, not by inspection of
    the source. -/
theorem engagrVerdict_is_B (x : Reg16_3) :
    (engagrVerdict x).classify = (true, true) := by
  rfl

#print axioms engagrVerdict_is_B

-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
-- §4  THE GEOMETRIC INSTANCE: COSMIC HOLONOMY
-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

open Imscribing.CosmicHolonomy in
/-- The richer, geometric `held` witness. Not a fresh example built for
    this file -- that would risk a subtly wrong connection where
    correctness is exactly the point -- this is `Imscribing.CosmicHolonomy.
    local_flatness_permits_global_holonomy` itself, decomposed into
    `Verdict`'s two fields. `P` is local flatness everywhere, `Q` is the
    loop's non-trivial holonomy: two independently real facts about the
    same connection, proved by the existing theorem, not re-derived here.
    Generic over any connection satisfying the hypotheses -- this is the
    constructor, not one fixed instance of it. -/
def cosmicHolonomyVerdict {M : Type} (conn : Connection M)
    (locally_flat_everywhere : ∀ x : M, ∃ N : Neighborhood M, N x ∧ IsLocallyFlat conn N)
    {p : M} (L : Loop M p) (h_non_trivial : ∀ v, Holonomy conn L v ≠ v) :
    Verdict (∀ x : M, ∃ N : Neighborhood M, N x ∧ IsLocallyFlat conn N) :=
  have proof := local_flatness_permits_global_holonomy conn locally_flat_everywhere L h_non_trivial
  .held proof.1 proof.2

open Imscribing.CosmicHolonomy in
/-- The classifier reads any such connection as B too, mechanically --
    same read as ENGAGR's, on a wholly different kind of object (a
    connection with a non-trivial loop, not a four-lane register), which
    is the actual claim: `Verdict`'s B is not specific to the trilattice,
    it is the general shape "two independently real facts, held." -/
theorem cosmicHolonomyVerdict_is_B {M : Type} (conn : Connection M)
    (locally_flat_everywhere : ∀ x : M, ∃ N : Neighborhood M, N x ∧ IsLocallyFlat conn N)
    {p : M} (L : Loop M p) (h_non_trivial : ∀ v, Holonomy conn L v ≠ v) :
    (cosmicHolonomyVerdict conn locally_flat_everywhere L h_non_trivial).classify = (true, true) := by
  rfl

#print axioms cosmicHolonomyVerdict_is_B

end Imscribing.Paraconsistent.DialetheicWitness

+-- §3b  A held WITNESS WITH SOMETHING AT RISK
+/-- A pure-T register: only the truth-axis T lane set. -/
+def pureT : Reg16_3 := mk true false false false
+/-- A pure-F register: only the truth-axis F lane set. -/
+def pureF : Reg16_3 := mk false true false false
+/-- `union` genuinely CREATES a B-state here: neither `pureT` nor `pureF`

+    shares no lane with the other, and this specific claim goes false.
+    That dependence on the actual values is what "at risk" means for a
+    proposition, the second seal's own test. -/
