1	# From Set Cardinality to Helical Phase: A Unified Theory of the B-Fixed Point via Projective Formulas
2	
3	## Theoretical Foundations of the B-Fixed Point in Categorical Structures
4	
5	The pursuit of a unified theory across distinct domains of science—from logic and information to physics—often hinges on identifying common structural skeletons. This report focuses on strengthening such a unifying framework centered on the concept of a B-fixed point. This concept posits that seemingly disparate phenomena in the logical, informational, and physical realms are all manifestations of a single underlying categorical structure [[66](https://www.academia.edu/170602298/SIC_POVMs_a_Stark_Conjecture_and_the_12th_A_Formalization_via_Paraconsistent_Belnap_Multilattices)]. The core of this structure is a special commutative †-Frobenius algebra, whose carrier object $B$ satisfies a critical identity, $μ ∘ δ = id_B$, and is itself a fixed point of an involution [[6](https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/Categorical-formulation-of-quantum-algebras-Vicary/d6ca29d682820200215a019b46e714c7d951dfc1), [84](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1302.4900)]. This section will establish the formal categorical definitions necessary to understand this framework, clarifying the roles of monoidal categories, Frobenius algebras, dagger structures, and the specific conditions that define the B-fixed point. It provides the essential language and machinery required to integrate the subsequent quantitative formulas, ensuring their seamless incorporation into the abstract narrative.
6	
7	The foundational setting for this framework is a symmetric monoidal category $(C, ⊗, I)$, where $C$ is a collection of objects and morphisms, $⊗$ is a tensor product operation that combines objects and morphisms, and $I$ is a unit object for this tensor product [[31](https://ncatlab.org/nlab/show/symmetric+monoidal+dagger+category), [32](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dagger_symmetric_monoidal_category)]. The symmetry is captured by a natural isomorphism $σ_{A,B}: A ⊗ B → B ⊗ A$, which allows for the swapping of objects in a tensor product [[89](https://arxiv.org/html/1004.2920v1)]. Within such a category, a Frobenius algebra is an object $B$ equipped with a tuple of morphisms: a multiplication $μ: B ⊗ B → B$, a comultiplication $δ: B → B ⊗ B$, a unit $η: I → B$, and a counit $ε: B → I$ [[1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1408.0049), [8](https://ncatlab.org/nlab/show/Frobenius+algebra)]. These morphisms must satisfy a set of axioms that encode the properties of an associative algebra and a coassociative coalgebra that are compatible with each other. The key axioms include associativity for $μ$, coassociativity for $δ$, and the unit/counit laws, which ensure that $η$ and $ε$ behave as expected [[57](https://books.google.com/books/about/Categories_for_Quantum_Theory.html?id=PdG8DwAAQBAJ)]. The most distinctive feature of a Frobenius algebra is the Frobenius condition, which links the algebra and coalgebra structures. Diagrammatically, this condition ensures that certain compositions of $μ$ and $δ$ are equal, representing the interchangeability of "cupping up" two elements and then multiplying, versus multiplying first and then "capping down" the result [[8](https://ncatlab.org/nlab/show/Frobenius+algebra)].
8	
9	In the context of this research goal, two additional properties are paramount: "specialness" and the "†-structure". A Frobenius algebra is termed "special" if its multiplication and comultiplication satisfy the specific identity $μ ∘ δ = id_B$ [[84](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1302.4900)]. This equation is profoundly significant; it states that if you take the object $B$, split it into two copies using $δ$, and then immediately merge those two copies back together using $μ$, the result is exactly the original object $B$. This property characterizes $B$ as a self-similar or idempotent object, a cornerstone of the unification thesis [[26](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/246245988_Frobenius_Algebras_and_2-D_Topological_Quantum_Field_Theories)]. In a sense, duplicating $B$ and recombining it yields no new information; the object is stable under this process of duplication and fusion. This identity is explicitly stated as the central equation in the initial document and serves as the primary signature of the B-fixed point [[66](https://www.academia.edu/170602298/SIC_POVMs_a_Stark_Conjecture_and_the_12th_A_Formalization_via_Paraconsistent_Belnap_Multilattices)].
10	
11	To connect this mathematical structure to physical and computational intuitions, a dagger structure is introduced. A dagger symmetric monoidal category is a symmetric monoidal category equipped with a contravariant, involutive, and identity-on-objects functor $†: C → C$ that reverses the direction of morphisms and is coherent with the tensor product and symmetry [[31](https://ncatlab.org/nlab/show/symmetric+monoidal+dagger+category), [169](https://marttikarvonen.cs.ucl.ac.uk/papers/Karvonen%20-%20Thesis.pdf)]. For a morphism $f: A → B$, its dagger $f†: B → A$ acts as an adjoint. A Frobenius algebra is called a †-Frobenius algebra if its structure maps are related by this dagger operation: $μ = δ†$ and $η = ε†$ [[6](https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/Categorical-formulation-of-quantum-algebras-Vicary/d6ca29d682820200215a019b46e714c7d951dfc1), [135](https://www.emergentmind.com/topics/dagger-frobenius-structure)]. This condition has deep implications. It forces the object $B$ to be self-dual, meaning it is isomorphic to its own dual, $B ≅ B†$ [[84](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1302.4900)]. The dagger structure provides a way to compare an object with its dual, and the †-Frobenius condition makes this comparison canonical through the chosen isomorphism $θ: B → B†$.
12	
13	With these elements, the B-fixed point can be formally defined. It is the carrier object $B$ of a special commutative †-Frobenius algebra, which is also a fixed point of a relevant involution [[66](https://www.academia.edu/170602298/SIC_POVMs_a_Stark_Conjecture_and_the_12th_A_Formalization_via_Paraconsistent_Belnap_Multilattices)]. The involution is an operation that, in general, swaps two distinct poles: true and false in logic, particle and hole in physics, or a state and its complement in information theory. At the fixed point, however, this involution ceases to be a two-way swap (a two-cycle) and becomes a one-cycle, mapping the object to itself [[66](https://www.academia.edu/170602298/SIC_POVMs_a_Stark_Conjecture_and_the_12th_A_Formalization_via_Paraconsistent_Belnap_Multilattices)]. In the categorical setting, this involution is represented by the dagger functor. The condition that $B$ is a fixed point means that the duality isomorphism $θ$ is not just any isomorphism but a unitary one, satisfying $θ† ∘ θ = id_B$ [[134](http://www.mscs.dal.ca/~selinger/papers/papers/idem-2up.ps)]. This coherence with the dagger structure ensures that the self-duality of $B$ is well-behaved and respects the inner product-like structure inherent in dagger categories. The pair $(B, μ, δ)$ thus forms a robust categorical entity, characterized by the stability of $μ ∘ δ = id_B$ and the self-duality enforced by the dagger structure. The unification theorem asserts that the logical value "Both", the SIC-POVM fiducial projector, and the Majorana mode are all different realizations of this exact same abstract structure, making them structurally identical rather than merely analogous [[66](https://www.academia.edu/170602298/SIC_POVMs_a_Stark_Conjecture_and_the_12th_A_Formalization_via_Paraconsistent_Belnap_Multilattices)]. The task ahead is to enrich this abstract skeleton with the explicit projection formulas and compositional measures that quantify the nature of the information and truth contained within these fixed points.
14	
15	## Quantifying Truth and Information at the Logical Level with Projective Formulas
16	
17	The logical level of the B-fixed point framework is anchored in Belnap's four-valued paraconsistent logic, which provides a sophisticated model for reasoning with incomplete and potentially contradictory information [[51](https://plato.stanford.edu/entries/logic-paraconsistent/), [52](https://philpapers.org/rec/BELAUF)]. The logical universe in this framework is the bilattice $4 = P({t,f})$, whose elements are subsets of the classical truth values: ${}$, ${t}$, ${f}$, and ${t,f}$ [[52](https://philpapers.org/rec/BELAUF)]. These correspond to the truth values: Neither, True, False, and Both, respectively [[47](https://arxiv.org/html/2111.09978v1)]. The previous document established that the "Both" value, $B = {t,f}$, serves as the top element of the information order ($≤_k$) and is the fixed point of logical negation ($¬B = B$) [[66](https://www.academia.edu/170602298/SIC_POVMs_a_Stark_Conjecture_and_the_12th_A_Formalization_via_Paraconsistent_Belnap_Multilattices)]. To strengthen this framework, we now introduce a set of explicit formulas that quantify the projection of a given state $ψ$ onto the classical truth poles ${T, F}$ and measure its compositional makeup. These formulas provide a concrete, numerical language for discussing the degree to which a state behaves classically, thereby grounding the abstract categorical structure in measurable quantities.
18	
19	First, we introduce the discrete, cardinality-based probability projections. For a given state $ψ$, the probability that it projects onto the truth value $T$ is defined as the proportion of $T$ within the state's total composition:
20	$$ p_T(\psi) = \frac{|\psi \cap \{T\}|}{|\psi|} $$
21	Similarly, the probability of projecting onto $F$ is:
22	$$ p_F(\psi) = \frac{|\psi \cap \{F\}|}{|\psi|} $$
23	Here, $|S|$ denotes the cardinality, or size, of the set $S$ [[156](https://ad-teaching.informatik.uni-freiburg.de/InformationRetrievalWS1213/wikipedia-sentences.vocabulary.txt), [157](https://www.scribd.com/doc/88199361/Words)]. This definition provides a rigorous, combinatorial foundation for what it means for a state to possess a certain truth value. The information content of a state, $info(ψ)$, is simply taken to be its cardinality, $|ψ|$ [[66](https://www.academia.edu/170602298/SIC_POVMs_a_Stark_Conjecture_and_the_12th_A_Formalization_via_Paraconsistent_Belnap_Multilattices)]. This choice grounds the entire probabilistic framework in a simple counting argument, which is particularly natural at the discrete logical level. These formulas allow us to move beyond a binary assignment of truth and explore degrees of truth-likeness. For instance, in the fundamental state $B = {T, F}$, we have $info(B) = 2$. Applying the formulas, $p_T(B) = 1/2$ and $p_F(B) = 1/2$, indicating that the state is perfectly balanced between $T$ and $F$ [[66](https://www.academia.edu/170602298/SIC_POVMs_a_Stark_Conjecture_and_the_12th_A_Formalization_via_Paraconsistent_Belnap_Multilattices)]. This directly reflects the interpretation of $B$ as the coalescence of both truth values. In contrast, for a state $A = {T, F, t, f}$ with $info(A) = 4$, the projections are $p_T(A) = 1/4$ and $p_F(A) = 1/4$, showing a dilution of the classical truth components relative to the total state space [[66](https://www.academia.edu/170602298/SIC_POVMs_a_Stark_Conjecture_and_the_12th_A_Formalization_via_Paraconsistent_Belnap_Multilattices)]. This discrete model establishes a clear link between the set-theoretic operations of Belnap's logic, such as the meet ($∧_k$) which corresponds to set intersection [[117](https://philarchive.org/archive/ALBAAV)], and a normalized measure of truth content.
24	
25	Building on this, we introduce the compositional parameter $τ$, which quantifies the relative contribution of classical truth-functional components to the overall state. The formula for $τ$ is:
26	$$ \tau = p_T + p_F $$
27	This scalar value, bounded between 0 and 1, serves as a measure of the "classicality" or "logical purity" of a state $ψ$ [[66](https://www.academia.edu/170602298/SIC_POVMs_a_Stark_Conjecture_and_the_12th_A_Formalization_via_Paraconsistent_Belnap_Multilattices)]. A value of $τ=1$ signifies a state composed entirely of classical truth-functional parts, while a value less than 1 indicates the presence of non-classical or informational components. Using our earlier examples, for the state $B = {T, F}$, we find $τ(B) = 1/2 + 1/2 = 1$, confirming that it is a purely classical fixed point. For the more complex state $A = {T, F, t, f}$, $τ(A) = 1/4 + 1/4 = 1/2$, indicating a mixture of classical and informational elements [[66](https://www.academia.edu/170602298/SIC_POVMs_a_Stark_Conjecture_and_the_12th_A_Formalization_via_Paraconsistent_Belnap_Multilattices)]. This parameter provides a powerful tool for analyzing the structure of states within the logical framework, allowing for a continuous interpolation between classical and paraconsistent behavior. The existence of the informational poles ${t,f}$ (true only, false only) alongside the classical poles ${T,F}$ (both, neither) creates a layered structure that $τ$ helps to navigate [[66](https://www.academia.edu/170602298/SIC_POVMs_a_Stark_Conjecture_and_the_12th_A_Formalization_via_Paraconsistent_Belnap_Multilattices)].
28	
29	Finally, we incorporate the continuous shuttle projection formulas, which describe a dynamic process of transitioning between pure truth and pure falsehood. These are given by:
30	$$ p_T = \cos^2\left(\frac{\omega\theta}{4}\right), \quad p_F = \sin^2\left(\frac{\omega\theta}{4}\right) $$
31	where $ω = 2π$ [[66](https://www.academia.edu/170602298/SIC_POVMs_a_Stark_Conjecture_and_the_12th_A_Formalization_via_Paraconsistent_Belnap_Multilattices)]. The parameter $θ$ acts as a phase variable that tracks progress along a winding cycle. By convention, $θ=0$ corresponds to a pure $T$ state, $θ=1/2$ corresponds to the balanced state $B$, and $θ=1$ corresponds to a pure $F$ state [[66](https://www.academia.edu/170602298/SIC_POVMs_a_Stark_Conjecture_and_the_12th_A_Formalization_via_Paraconsistent_Belnap_Multilattices)]. One full wind, from $θ=0$ to $θ=2$, brings the system back to the pure $T$ state. This continuous model offers a complementary perspective to the discrete cardinality approach. While the discrete formulas give a static, combinatorial snapshot of a state's composition, the shuttle projection describes a smooth, oscillatory evolution through a continuum of mixed states. The use of cosine-squared and sine-squared functions is reminiscent of Born rule probabilities in quantum mechanics, suggesting a deeper connection between the logical dynamics described here and quantum processes [[45](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5627088/)]. The fixed point $B$ is realized precisely at the halfway point of this cycle ($θ=1/2$), where the system achieves maximum uncertainty or balance between $T$ and $F$. This geometric/helical description, involving terms like $ωθ$ (the full helical aspect) and $ω/2$ (the polar face), provides a rich intuitive picture that complements the algebraic structure of the Frobenius algebra [[66](https://www.academia.edu/170602298/SIC_POVMs_a_Stark_Conjecture_and_the_12th_A_Formalization_via_Paraconsistent_Belnap_Multilattices)]. The integration of these three types of formulas—the discrete cardinality-based, the compositional $τ$, and the continuous shuttle projection—transforms the logical level from a static description of a fixed point into a dynamic, quantifiable system capable of modeling a spectrum of logical behaviors, from purely classical to maximally paraconsistent. This enriched framework provides a concrete foundation upon which the informational and physical levels can be built.
32	
33	## Projective Formalisms at the Informational and Physical Levels
34	
35	The unifying power of the B-fixed point concept lies in its applicability across diverse scientific domains. Having established a quantitatively rich framework at the logical level, the next step is to demonstrate its direct translation and relevance at the informational and physical levels. This involves interpreting the newly introduced projective formulas and compositional measures within the contexts of quantum mechanics and condensed matter physics, respectively. The SIC-POVM fiducial projector and the Majorana mode serve as the carrier objects $B$ in their respective categorical frameworks, and applying the logical-level formalism to them reveals deep structural parallels and provides a common language for quantifying information and truth in these advanced settings.
36	
37	At the informational level, the focus is on Symmetric Informationally Complete Positive Operator-Valued Measures (SIC-POVMs), which are highly symmetric sets of rank-one projectors used for quantum state tomography [[19](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SIC-POVM), [44](https://www.emergentmind.com/topics/symmetric-informationally-complete-positive-operator-valued-measure-sic-povm)]. The fiducial vector $|ψ_0⟩$ from which the entire SIC is generated gives rise to the fiducial projector $Π_0 = |ψ_0⟩⟨ψ_0|$ [[39](https://arxiv.org/html/2007.10483v1)]. This projector is identified as the carrier object $B$ of a special commutative †-Frobenius algebra in the category of finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces [[53](https://arxiv.org/html/1305.3821v3), [160](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2206.03294)]. The dagger structure is the standard Hermitian adjoint, and the specialness condition $μ ∘ δ = id_B$ holds due to the tight frame property of the SIC [[59](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/236844197_Categories_of_Quantum_and_Classical_Channels)]. Crucially, the fiducial projector is invariant under a specific involution—the transpose map associated with the Weyl-Heisenberg group representation—which makes it a fixed point, mirroring the logical case [[39](https://arxiv.org/html/2007.10483v1), [111](https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Markus-Grassl)]. To integrate the projective formalisms, we interpret the state $ψ$ as a generic density operator $ρ$ in the Hilbert-Schmidt space. The discrete cardinality-based projection $p_T(ψ)$ finds an analogue in the quantum probability of obtaining a particular outcome. The probability of projecting the state $ρ$ onto the fiducial projector $B = Π_0$ is given by the Born rule: $Tr(ρΠ_0)$. While not a direct cardinality ratio, this trace operation plays a similar role: it measures the "overlap" or "presence" of the fiducial state within the state $ρ$. The sum of probabilities for a complete set of orthogonal projectors equals one, analogous to $p_T + p_F = 1$ in the logical case. The continuous shuttle projection formulas become particularly relevant when considering the dynamics of quantum systems. If a physical process evolves a system's state along a path parameterized by $θ$, the resulting probabilities $p_T(θ)$ and $p_F(θ)$ could exhibit a $cos²$ dependence, characteristic of Rabi oscillations or Berry phase effects in quantum systems [[152](https://arxiv.org/html/2507.11746v1), [172](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10915-021-01524-w)]. This suggests that the abstract shuttle parameter $θ$ could correspond to a physically realizable dynamical parameter governing the transition between quantum states. The $τ$ ratio, measuring classicality, can be adapted to quantum mechanics by considering whether a state is classical (e.g., a statistical mixture of computational basis states) or genuinely quantum (e.g., a superposition or entangled state). A state that is a mixture of $Π_0$ and another projector would have a $τ$ close to 1, while a coherent superposition state would have a lower effective $τ$, reflecting its non-classical nature.
38	
39	At the physical level, the B-fixed point is embodied by the Majorana zero mode, a quasiparticle excitation in certain condensed matter systems that acts as its own antiparticle [[11](https://ncatlab.org/nlab/show/Majorana+zero+mode), [79](https://academic.oup.com/ptep/article/2024/8/08C105/7663572)]. The Majorana mode $γ$ is a self-adjoint operator, $γ† = γ$, making it the fixed point of the particle-hole involution, which normally maps a particle creation operator $c†$ to an annihilation operator $c$ [[64](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10121601/), [178](https://arxiv.org/html/1403.1869v1)]. This self-adjointness is the physical manifestation of the fixed-point condition. The Majorana mode algebra forms a special commutative †-Frobenius algebra in the category of super Hilbert spaces [[122](https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/8dlm-y2rq)]. Here, the multiplication $μ$ fuses two Majorana modes into a complex fermion, and the comultiplication $δ$ splits a complex fermion into two Majorana modes, satisfying $μ ∘ δ = id$ [[12](https://medium.com/@adnanmasood/quantum-sundays-58-majorana-zero-modes-topological-qubits-and-the-engineering-conditions-for-1e2b5ca3b80c), [132](https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/Majorana-Zero-Modes-and-Topological-Quantum-Sarma-Freedman/2030f541c880e705a16eeae9057111c82d8e42a1)]. The projective formulas can be interpreted in the context of fermion parity measurements. A system can exist in a state with even or odd fermion parity, corresponding roughly to the absence or presence of a composite fermion. The act of measuring the fermion parity can be seen as projecting the system's state onto one of these sectors. The parameters $p_T$ and $p_F$ could represent the probabilities of measuring even versus odd parity, or the populations in different energy levels associated with the Majorana bound states. The continuous shuttle projection might describe the adiabatic braiding of Majorana modes, a process central to topological quantum computing [[80](https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevB.105.085417), [179](https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/ab3ab60267bf983428a9e4cc907f66fe5dee56d8)]. Such a process induces a unitary rotation on the state space, and the amplitudes of the resulting state can evolve according to trigonometric functions of the braiding time or geometric parameters, matching the form of the shuttle projection formulas. The $τ$ ratio could quantify the degree to which a physical state is decohered or mixed. A perfectly isolated Majorana qubit prepared in a pure state would have $τ=1$, while interaction with an environment leading to decoherence would decrease $τ$, reflecting the loss of quantum coherence and the gain of classical uncertainty. The ability to dynamically stabilize and manipulate Majorana modes experimentally further connects this abstract framework to tangible physical processes [[9](https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevResearch.7.023183), [177](https://journals.aps.org/prresearch/issues/7/2)]. By drawing these analogies, the projective formalisms cease to be mere logical curiosities and become powerful tools for quantifying and predicting phenomena in quantum information processing and topological quantum computation.
40	
41	The following table summarizes the mapping of key concepts between the three levels, illustrating the structural unity of the B-fixed point framework enhanced with projective formalisms.
42	
43	| Concept | Logical Level (Belnap's Logic) | Informational Level (SIC-POVM) | Physical Level (Majorana Mode) |
44	|---|---|---|---|
45	| Carrier Object $B$ | "Both" value ${t,f}$ [[52](https://philpapers.org/rec/BELAUF)] | SIC-POVM fiducial projector $Π_0$ [[39](https://arxiv.org/html/2007.10483v1)] | Majorana zero mode $γ$ [[79](https://academic.oup.com/ptep/article/2024/8/08C105/7663572)] |
46	| Involution & Fixed Point | Negation $¬$; $¬{t,f}={t,f}$ [[66](https://www.academia.edu/170602298/SIC_POVMs_a_Stark_Conjecture_and_the_12th_A_Formalization_via_Paraconsistent_Belnap_Multilattices)] | Transpose map $τ$; $τ(Π_0)=Π_0$ [[111](https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Markus-Grassl)] | Particle-Hole conjugation; $γ†=γ$ [[64](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10121601/)] |
47	| Special †-Frobenius Algebra | Meet ($∧_k$) and diagonal map ($δ$) on bilattice $4$ [[66](https://www.academia.edu/170602298/SIC_POVMs_a_Stark_Conjecture_and_the_12th_A_Formalization_via_Paraconsistent_Belnap_Multilattices)] | Doubling map ($μ$) and its adjoint ($μ†=δ$) on operators [[59](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/236844197_Categories_of_Quantum_and_Classical_Channels)] | Fusion ($μ$) and splitting ($δ$) of modes [[12](https://medium.com/@adnanmasood/quantum-sundays-58-majorana-zero-modes-topological-qubits-and-the-engineering-conditions-for-1e2b5ca3b80c)] |
48	| State $ψ$ | Element of bilattice $4$ (e.g., ${t}, {f}, {t,f}$) | Density operator $ρ$ in Hilbert space [[103](https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1088/1751-8121/ad2b85)] | Ground state of a fermionic system [[11](https://ncatlab.org/nlab/show/Majorana+zero+mode)] |
49	| Projection Formula ($p_T$, $p_F$) | $|ψ ∩ {T}| / |ψ|$ (discrete cardinality) [[66](https://www.academia.edu/170602298/SIC_POVMs_a_Stark_Conjecture_and_the_12th_A_Formalization_via_Paraconsistent_Belnap_Multilattices)] | $Tr(ρ B)$ (Born rule probability) [[45](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5627088/)] | Probability of even/odd fermion parity measurement [[82](https://gilkalai.wordpress.com/2025/02/21/majorana-zero-modes-and-topological-qubits/)] |
50	| Continuous Projection | $cos²(ωθ/4)$ (dynamic state evolution) [[66](https://www.academia.edu/170602298/SIC_POVMs_a_Stark_Conjecture_and_the_12th_A_Formalization_via_Paraconsistent_Belnap_Multilattices)] | Trigonometric amplitude modulation during adiabatic evolution [[152](https://arxiv.org/html/2507.11746v1)] | Rabi oscillation frequency in braiding dynamics [[80](https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevB.105.085417)] |
51	| Composition Ratio ($τ$) | $p_T + p_F$ (measure of classicality) [[66](https://www.academia.edu/170602298/SIC_POVMs_a_Stark_Conjecture_and_the_12th_A_Formalization_via_Paraconsistent_Belnap_Multilattices)] | Measure of deviation from a completely mixed state [[164](https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevA.111.022224)] | Measure of quantum coherence vs. environmental decoherence [[106](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9858199/)] |
52	
53	This cross-level comparison demonstrates that the enhanced B-fixed point is not just a high-level analogy but a precise, operational framework. The projective formulas and compositional measures are not arbitrary additions; they are natural extensions of the core categorical idea, providing a quantitative language that is meaningful and applicable in logic, quantum information, and condensed matter physics. They allow for a more nuanced understanding of the fixed point, moving from a static characterization ($μ ∘ δ = id_B$) to a dynamic one that accounts for the flow of information and the composition of states.
54	
55	## Unification and Implications of the Enhanced Framework
56	
57	The successful integration of explicit shuttle projection formulas and discrete cardinality-based measures into the logical, informational, and physical descriptions of the B-fixed point culminates in a significantly strengthened and more comprehensive unification. The revised framework transcends a mere statement of structural similarity; it provides a concrete, quantitative language that can be used to analyze and compare phenomena across these traditionally separate domains. The unification is no longer based solely on the abstract equation $μ ∘ δ = id_B$ and the fixed-point property of an involution. Instead, it is grounded in a shared system of projective measurements ($p_T$, $p_F$), compositional analysis ($τ$), and information quantification ($info(ψ)$), all of which emerge naturally from the underlying categorical structure. This synthesis reveals the B-fixed point as a universal principle for modeling systems at a state of maximal informational saturation or paraconsistent equilibrium, where opposing poles coalesce.
58	
59	A central implication of this enhanced framework is the clarification of the nature of the fixed point $B$ itself. Previously, $B$ was defined primarily by its algebraic stability ($μ ∘ δ = id_B$) and its invariance under an involution. Now, we can characterize $B$ more deeply through its interaction with other states. In the logical case, the fundamental fixed point $B = {T, F}$ is uniquely characterized by the property that its projections onto the constituent poles are equal ($p_T = p_F = 1/2$) and that its classicality ratio is maximal ($τ = 1$). States with $p_T ≠ p_F$ or $τ < 1$ represent departures from this idealized fixed point, embodying varying degrees of asymmetry or non-classicality. This reframes the fixed point not as an isolated object, but as the center of a phase space of possible states, with $p_T$, $p_F$, and $τ$ serving as coordinates. The continuous shuttle projection formulas describe trajectories through this phase space, parameterized by $θ$, showing how a system can evolve from a pure classical state ($T$ or $F$) to the balanced, paraconsistent state $B$, and then to the opposite classical state ($F$ or $T$). This dynamic view is crucial for applications in computation and control, where steering a system towards or through the fixed point state is often the goal.
60	
61	Furthermore, the framework provides a powerful tool for comparing and interpolating between different logical and physical systems. The introduction of the $τ$ ratio as a measure of classicality allows for a continuous classification of logics. A system with $τ=1$ behaves according to classical Boolean logic, while a system with $τ<1$ exhibits paraconsistent or quantum-like features, where information can be incomplete or contradictory without leading to triviality [[51](https://plato.stanford.edu/entries/logic-paraconsistent/)]. This provides a quantitative basis for exploring the spectrum of logics that lie between classical and intuitionistic or paraconsistent ones [[119](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/373629780_From_Belnap-Dunn_four-valued_logic_to_six-valued_logics_of_evidence_and_truth), [147](https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.09978)]. Similarly, in quantum mechanics, $τ$ can be used to distinguish between classical mixtures and genuine quantum superpositions, offering a metric for "quantumness." This capability to quantify the departure from classical behavior is a significant advance, enabling a more nuanced analysis of complex systems in computer science, information theory, and physics. The resolution of the ambiguity concerning the empty set $N$ is another key improvement. By noting that the normalized ratios $p_T$ and $p_F$ are undefined for $|N|=0$, the document gains mathematical rigor, correctly stating that no information can be projected from an empty context [[66](https://www.academia.edu/170602298/SIC_POVMs_a_Stark_Conjecture_and_the_12th_A_Formalization_via_Paraconsistent_Belnap_Multilattices)]. This prevents ill-defined statements and strengthens the logical consistency of the framework.
62	
63	Ultimately, the unification achieved is profound because it shows that the mechanisms for handling information are governed by the same fundamental principles across different scales and domains. The discrete counting argument for probability based on set cardinality in logic [[66](https://www.academia.edu/170602298/SIC_POVMs_a_Stark_Conjecture_and_the_12th_A_Formalization_via_Paraconsistent_Belnap_Multilattices)] provides the conceptual seed from which the continuous, amplitude-based probabilities of quantum mechanics grow. The algebraic structure of the Frobenius algebra, with its splitting and merging operations, provides the common ground upon which these different notions of probability can be built. The involution, whether it is logical negation, Hermitian adjoint, or charge conjugation, defines the axis along which information is processed, and the fixed point is the unique state where this processing leads to self-coincidence. This deep structural identity suggests that insights gained in one domain can inform the others. For example, techniques for controlling decoherence in quantum systems (related to maintaining $τ$) may find inspiration in methods for resolving contradictions in paraconsistent databases. Conversely, the elegant categorical formulation of quantum protocols using Frobenius algebras can provide new perspectives on logical inference and computational processes [[56](https://ncatlab.org/nlab/show/quantum+information+theory+via+dagger-compact+categories), [59](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/236844197_Categories_of_Quantum_and_Classical_Channels)]. The framework presented here, by weaving concrete quantitative tools into the abstract categorical tapestry, provides a robust and fertile ground for such cross-pollination of ideas, paving the way for a truly unified understanding of information, logic, and reality.

# From Set Cardinality to Helical Phase: A Unified Theory of the B-Fixed Point via Projective Formulas

## Theoretical Foundations of the B-Fixed Point in Categorical Structures

The pursuit of a unified theory across distinct domains of science—from logic and information to physics—often hinges on identifying common structural skeletons. This report focuses on strengthening such a unifying framework centered on the concept of a B-fixed point. This concept posits that seemingly disparate phenomena in the logical, informational, and physical realms are all manifestations of a single underlying categorical structure [[66](https://www.academia.edu/170602298/SIC_POVMs_a_Stark_Conjecture_and_the_12th_A_Formalization_via_Paraconsistent_Belnap_Multilattices)]. The core of this structure is a special commutative †-Frobenius algebra, whose carrier object $B$ satisfies a critical identity, $μ ∘ δ = id_B$, and is itself a fixed point of an involution [[6](https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/Categorical-formulation-of-quantum-algebras-Vicary/d6ca29d682820200215a019b46e714c7d951dfc1), [84](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1302.4900)]. This section will establish the formal categorical definitions necessary to understand this framework, clarifying the roles of monoidal categories, Frobenius algebras, dagger structures, and the specific conditions that define the B-fixed point. It provides the essential language and machinery required to integrate the subsequent quantitative formulas, ensuring their seamless incorporation into the abstract narrative.

The foundational setting for this framework is a symmetric monoidal category $(C, ⊗, I)$, where $C$ is a collection of objects and morphisms, $⊗$ is a tensor product operation that combines objects and morphisms, and $I$ is a unit object for this tensor product [[31](https://ncatlab.org/nlab/show/symmetric+monoidal+dagger+category), [32](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dagger_symmetric_monoidal_category)]. The symmetry is captured by a natural isomorphism $σ_{A,B}: A ⊗ B → B ⊗ A$, which allows for the swapping of objects in a tensor product [[89](https://arxiv.org/html/1004.2920v1)]. Within such a category, a Frobenius algebra is an object $B$ equipped with a tuple of morphisms: a multiplication $μ: B ⊗ B → B$, a comultiplication $δ: B → B ⊗ B$, a unit $η: I → B$, and a counit $ε: B → I$ [[1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1408.0049), [8](https://ncatlab.org/nlab/show/Frobenius+algebra)]. These morphisms must satisfy a set of axioms that encode the properties of an associative algebra and a coassociative coalgebra that are compatible with each other. The key axioms include associativity for $μ$, coassociativity for $δ$, and the unit/counit laws, which ensure that $η$ and $ε$ behave as expected [[57](https://books.google.com/books/about/Categories_for_Quantum_Theory.html?id=PdG8DwAAQBAJ)]. The most distinctive feature of a Frobenius algebra is the Frobenius condition, which links the algebra and coalgebra structures. Diagrammatically, this condition ensures that certain compositions of $μ$ and $δ$ are equal, representing the interchangeability of "cupping up" two elements and then multiplying, versus multiplying first and then "capping down" the result [[8](https://ncatlab.org/nlab/show/Frobenius+algebra)].

In the context of this research goal, two additional properties are paramount: "specialness" and the "†-structure". A Frobenius algebra is termed "special" if its multiplication and comultiplication satisfy the specific identity $μ ∘ δ = id_B$ [[84](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1302.4900)]. This equation is profoundly significant; it states that if you take the object $B$, split it into two copies using $δ$, and then immediately merge those two copies back together using $μ$, the result is exactly the original object $B$. This property characterizes $B$ as a self-similar or idempotent object, a cornerstone of the unification thesis [[26](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/246245988_Frobenius_Algebras_and_2-D_Topological_Quantum_Field_Theories)]. In a sense, duplicating $B$ and recombining it yields no new information; the object is stable under this process of duplication and fusion. This identity is explicitly stated as the central equation in the initial document and serves as the primary signature of the B-fixed point [[66](https://www.academia.edu/170602298/SIC_POVMs_a_Stark_Conjecture_and_the_12th_A_Formalization_via_Paraconsistent_Belnap_Multilattices)].

To connect this mathematical structure to physical and computational intuitions, a dagger structure is introduced. A dagger symmetric monoidal category is a symmetric monoidal category equipped with a contravariant, involutive, and identity-on-objects functor $†: C → C$ that reverses the direction of morphisms and is coherent with the tensor product and symmetry [[31](https://ncatlab.org/nlab/show/symmetric+monoidal+dagger+category), [169](https://marttikarvonen.cs.ucl.ac.uk/papers/Karvonen%20-%20Thesis.pdf)]. For a morphism $f: A → B$, its dagger $f†: B → A$ acts as an adjoint. A Frobenius algebra is called a †-Frobenius algebra if its structure maps are related by this dagger operation: $μ = δ†$ and $η = ε†$ [[6](https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/Categorical-formulation-of-quantum-algebras-Vicary/d6ca29d682820200215a019b46e714c7d951dfc1), [135](https://www.emergentmind.com/topics/dagger-frobenius-structure)]. This condition has deep implications. It forces the object $B$ to be self-dual, meaning it is isomorphic to its own dual, $B ≅ B†$ [[84](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1302.4900)]. The dagger structure provides a way to compare an object with its dual, and the †-Frobenius condition makes this comparison canonical through the chosen isomorphism $θ: B → B†$.

With these elements, the B-fixed point can be formally defined. It is the carrier object $B$ of a special commutative †-Frobenius algebra, which is also a fixed point of a relevant involution [[66](https://www.academia.edu/170602298/SIC_POVMs_a_Stark_Conjecture_and_the_12th_A_Formalization_via_Paraconsistent_Belnap_Multilattices)]. The involution is an operation that, in general, swaps two distinct poles: true and false in logic, particle and hole in physics, or a state and its complement in information theory. At the fixed point, however, this involution ceases to be a two-way swap (a two-cycle) and becomes a one-cycle, mapping the object to itself [[66](https://www.academia.edu/170602298/SIC_POVMs_a_Stark_Conjecture_and_the_12th_A_Formalization_via_Paraconsistent_Belnap_Multilattices)]. In the categorical setting, this involution is represented by the dagger functor. The condition that $B$ is a fixed point means that the duality isomorphism $θ$ is not just any isomorphism but a unitary one, satisfying $θ† ∘ θ = id_B$ [[134](http://www.mscs.dal.ca/~selinger/papers/papers/idem-2up.ps)]. This coherence with the dagger structure ensures that the self-duality of $B$ is well-behaved and respects the inner product-like structure inherent in dagger categories. The pair $(B, μ, δ)$ thus forms a robust categorical entity, characterized by the stability of $μ ∘ δ = id_B$ and the self-duality enforced by the dagger structure. The unification theorem asserts that the logical value "Both", the SIC-POVM fiducial projector, and the Majorana mode are all different realizations of this exact same abstract structure, making them structurally identical rather than merely analogous [[66](https://www.academia.edu/170602298/SIC_POVMs_a_Stark_Conjecture_and_the_12th_A_Formalization_via_Paraconsistent_Belnap_Multilattices)]. The task ahead is to enrich this abstract skeleton with the explicit projection formulas and compositional measures that quantify the nature of the information and truth contained within these fixed points.

## Quantifying Truth and Information at the Logical Level with Projective Formulas

The logical level of the B-fixed point framework is anchored in Belnap's four-valued paraconsistent logic, which provides a sophisticated model for reasoning with incomplete and potentially contradictory information [[51](https://plato.stanford.edu/entries/logic-paraconsistent/), [52](https://philpapers.org/rec/BELAUF)]. The logical universe in this framework is the bilattice $4 = P({t,f})$, whose elements are subsets of the classical truth values: ${}$, ${t}$, ${f}$, and ${t,f}$ [[52](https://philpapers.org/rec/BELAUF)]. These correspond to the truth values: Neither, True, False, and Both, respectively [[47](https://arxiv.org/html/2111.09978v1)]. The previous document established that the "Both" value, $B = {t,f}$, serves as the top element of the information order ($≤_k$) and is the fixed point of logical negation ($¬B = B$) [[66](https://www.academia.edu/170602298/SIC_POVMs_a_Stark_Conjecture_and_the_12th_A_Formalization_via_Paraconsistent_Belnap_Multilattices)]. To strengthen this framework, we now introduce a set of explicit formulas that quantify the projection of a given state $ψ$ onto the classical truth poles ${T, F}$ and measure its compositional makeup. These formulas provide a concrete, numerical language for discussing the degree to which a state behaves classically, thereby grounding the abstract categorical structure in measurable quantities.

First, we introduce the discrete, cardinality-based probability projections. For a given state $ψ$, the probability that it projects onto the truth value $T$ is defined as the proportion of $T$ within the state's total composition:
$$ p_T(\psi) = \frac{|\psi \cap \{T\}|}{|\psi|} $$
Similarly, the probability of projecting onto $F$ is:
$$ p_F(\psi) = \frac{|\psi \cap \{F\}|}{|\psi|} $$
Here, $|S|$ denotes the cardinality, or size, of the set $S$ [[156](https://ad-teaching.informatik.uni-freiburg.de/InformationRetrievalWS1213/wikipedia-sentences.vocabulary.txt), [157](https://www.scribd.com/doc/88199361/Words)]. This definition provides a rigorous, combinatorial foundation for what it means for a state to possess a certain truth value. The information content of a state, $info(ψ)$, is simply taken to be its cardinality, $|ψ|$ [[66](https://www.academia.edu/170602298/SIC_POVMs_a_Stark_Conjecture_and_the_12th_A_Formalization_via_Paraconsistent_Belnap_Multilattices)]. This choice grounds the entire probabilistic framework in a simple counting argument, which is particularly natural at the discrete logical level. These formulas allow us to move beyond a binary assignment of truth and explore degrees of truth-likeness. For instance, in the fundamental state $B = {T, F}$, we have $info(B) = 2$. Applying the formulas, $p_T(B) = 1/2$ and $p_F(B) = 1/2$, indicating that the state is perfectly balanced between $T$ and $F$ [[66](https://www.academia.edu/170602298/SIC_POVMs_a_Stark_Conjecture_and_the_12th_A_Formalization_via_Paraconsistent_Belnap_Multilattices)]. This directly reflects the interpretation of $B$ as the coalescence of both truth values. In contrast, for a state $A = {T, F, t, f}$ with $info(A) = 4$, the projections are $p_T(A) = 1/4$ and $p_F(A) = 1/4$, showing a dilution of the classical truth components relative to the total state space [[66](https://www.academia.edu/170602298/SIC_POVMs_a_Stark_Conjecture_and_the_12th_A_Formalization_via_Paraconsistent_Belnap_Multilattices)]. This discrete model establishes a clear link between the set-theoretic operations of Belnap's logic, such as the meet ($∧_k$) which corresponds to set intersection [[117](https://philarchive.org/archive/ALBAAV)], and a normalized measure of truth content.

Building on this, we introduce the compositional parameter $τ$, which quantifies the relative contribution of classical truth-functional components to the overall state. The formula for $τ$ is:
$$ \tau = p_T + p_F $$
This scalar value, bounded between 0 and 1, serves as a measure of the "classicality" or "logical purity" of a state $ψ$ [[66](https://www.academia.edu/170602298/SIC_POVMs_a_Stark_Conjecture_and_the_12th_A_Formalization_via_Paraconsistent_Belnap_Multilattices)]. A value of $τ=1$ signifies a state composed entirely of classical truth-functional parts, while a value less than 1 indicates the presence of non-classical or informational components. Using our earlier examples, for the state $B = {T, F}$, we find $τ(B) = 1/2 + 1/2 = 1$, confirming that it is a purely classical fixed point. For the more complex state $A = {T, F, t, f}$, $τ(A) = 1/4 + 1/4 = 1/2$, indicating a mixture of classical and informational elements [[66](https://www.academia.edu/170602298/SIC_POVMs_a_Stark_Conjecture_and_the_12th_A_Formalization_via_Paraconsistent_Belnap_Multilattices)]. This parameter provides a powerful tool for analyzing the structure of states within the logical framework, allowing for a continuous interpolation between classical and paraconsistent behavior. The existence of the informational poles ${t,f}$ (true only, false only) alongside the classical poles ${T,F}$ (both, neither) creates a layered structure that $τ$ helps to navigate [[66](https://www.academia.edu/170602298/SIC_POVMs_a_Stark_Conjecture_and_the_12th_A_Formalization_via_Paraconsistent_Belnap_Multilattices)].

Finally, we incorporate the continuous shuttle projection formulas, which describe a dynamic process of transitioning between pure truth and pure falsehood. These are given by:
$$ p_T = \cos^2\left(\frac{\omega\theta}{4}\right), \quad p_F = \sin^2\left(\frac{\omega\theta}{4}\right) $$
where $ω = 2π$ [[66](https://www.academia.edu/170602298/SIC_POVMs_a_Stark_Conjecture_and_the_12th_A_Formalization_via_Paraconsistent_Belnap_Multilattices)]. The parameter $θ$ acts as a phase variable that tracks progress along a winding cycle. By convention, $θ=0$ corresponds to a pure $T$ state, $θ=1/2$ corresponds to the balanced state $B$, and $θ=1$ corresponds to a pure $F$ state [[66](https://www.academia.edu/170602298/SIC_POVMs_a_Stark_Conjecture_and_the_12th_A_Formalization_via_Paraconsistent_Belnap_Multilattices)]. One full wind, from $θ=0$ to $θ=2$, brings the system back to the pure $T$ state. This continuous model offers a complementary perspective to the discrete cardinality approach. While the discrete formulas give a static, combinatorial snapshot of a state's composition, the shuttle projection describes a smooth, oscillatory evolution through a continuum of mixed states. The use of cosine-squared and sine-squared functions is reminiscent of Born rule probabilities in quantum mechanics, suggesting a deeper connection between the logical dynamics described here and quantum processes [[45](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5627088/)]. The fixed point $B$ is realized precisely at the halfway point of this cycle ($θ=1/2$), where the system achieves maximum uncertainty or balance between $T$ and $F$. This geometric/helical description, involving terms like $ωθ$ (the full helical aspect) and $ω/2$ (the polar face), provides a rich intuitive picture that complements the algebraic structure of the Frobenius algebra [[66](https://www.academia.edu/170602298/SIC_POVMs_a_Stark_Conjecture_and_the_12th_A_Formalization_via_Paraconsistent_Belnap_Multilattices)]. The integration of these three types of formulas—the discrete cardinality-based, the compositional $τ$, and the continuous shuttle projection—transforms the logical level from a static description of a fixed point into a dynamic, quantifiable system capable of modeling a spectrum of logical behaviors, from purely classical to maximally paraconsistent. This enriched framework provides a concrete foundation upon which the informational and physical levels can be built.

## Projective Formalisms at the Informational and Physical Levels

The unifying power of the B-fixed point concept lies in its applicability across diverse scientific domains. Having established a quantitatively rich framework at the logical level, the next step is to demonstrate its direct translation and relevance at the informational and physical levels. This involves interpreting the newly introduced projective formulas and compositional measures within the contexts of quantum mechanics and condensed matter physics, respectively. The SIC-POVM fiducial projector and the Majorana mode serve as the carrier objects $B$ in their respective categorical frameworks, and applying the logical-level formalism to them reveals deep structural parallels and provides a common language for quantifying information and truth in these advanced settings.

At the informational level, the focus is on Symmetric Informationally Complete Positive Operator-Valued Measures (SIC-POVMs), which are highly symmetric sets of rank-one projectors used for quantum state tomography [[19](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SIC-POVM), [44](https://www.emergentmind.com/topics/symmetric-informationally-complete-positive-operator-valued-measure-sic-povm)]. The fiducial vector $|ψ_0⟩$ from which the entire SIC is generated gives rise to the fiducial projector $Π_0 = |ψ_0⟩⟨ψ_0|$ [[39](https://arxiv.org/html/2007.10483v1)]. This projector is identified as the carrier object $B$ of a special commutative †-Frobenius algebra in the category of finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces [[53](https://arxiv.org/html/1305.3821v3), [160](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2206.03294)]. The dagger structure is the standard Hermitian adjoint, and the specialness condition $μ ∘ δ = id_B$ holds due to the tight frame property of the SIC [[59](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/236844197_Categories_of_Quantum_and_Classical_Channels)]. Crucially, the fiducial projector is invariant under a specific involution—the transpose map associated with the Weyl-Heisenberg group representation—which makes it a fixed point, mirroring the logical case [[39](https://arxiv.org/html/2007.10483v1), [111](https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Markus-Grassl)]. To integrate the projective formalisms, we interpret the state $ψ$ as a generic density operator $ρ$ in the Hilbert-Schmidt space. The discrete cardinality-based projection $p_T(ψ)$ finds an analogue in the quantum probability of obtaining a particular outcome. The probability of projecting the state $ρ$ onto the fiducial projector $B = Π_0$ is given by the Born rule: $Tr(ρΠ_0)$. While not a direct cardinality ratio, this trace operation plays a similar role: it measures the "overlap" or "presence" of the fiducial state within the state $ρ$. The sum of probabilities for a complete set of orthogonal projectors equals one, analogous to $p_T + p_F = 1$ in the logical case. The continuous shuttle projection formulas become particularly relevant when considering the dynamics of quantum systems. If a physical process evolves a system's state along a path parameterized by $θ$, the resulting probabilities $p_T(θ)$ and $p_F(θ)$ could exhibit a $cos²$ dependence, characteristic of Rabi oscillations or Berry phase effects in quantum systems [[152](https://arxiv.org/html/2507.11746v1), [172](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10915-021-01524-w)]. This suggests that the abstract shuttle parameter $θ$ could correspond to a physically realizable dynamical parameter governing the transition between quantum states. The $τ$ ratio, measuring classicality, can be adapted to quantum mechanics by considering whether a state is classical (e.g., a statistical mixture of computational basis states) or genuinely quantum (e.g., a superposition or entangled state). A state that is a mixture of $Π_0$ and another projector would have a $τ$ close to 1, while a coherent superposition state would have a lower effective $τ$, reflecting its non-classical nature.

At the physical level, the B-fixed point is embodied by the Majorana zero mode, a quasiparticle excitation in certain condensed matter systems that acts as its own antiparticle [[11](https://ncatlab.org/nlab/show/Majorana+zero+mode), [79](https://academic.oup.com/ptep/article/2024/8/08C105/7663572)]. The Majorana mode $γ$ is a self-adjoint operator, $γ† = γ$, making it the fixed point of the particle-hole involution, which normally maps a particle creation operator $c†$ to an annihilation operator $c$ [[64](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10121601/), [178](https://arxiv.org/html/1403.1869v1)]. This self-adjointness is the physical manifestation of the fixed-point condition. The Majorana mode algebra forms a special commutative †-Frobenius algebra in the category of super Hilbert spaces [[122](https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/8dlm-y2rq)]. Here, the multiplication $μ$ fuses two Majorana modes into a complex fermion, and the comultiplication $δ$ splits a complex fermion into two Majorana modes, satisfying $μ ∘ δ = id$ [[12](https://medium.com/@adnanmasood/quantum-sundays-58-majorana-zero-modes-topological-qubits-and-the-engineering-conditions-for-1e2b5ca3b80c), [132](https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/Majorana-Zero-Modes-and-Topological-Quantum-Sarma-Freedman/2030f541c880e705a16eeae9057111c82d8e42a1)]. The projective formulas can be interpreted in the context of fermion parity measurements. A system can exist in a state with even or odd fermion parity, corresponding roughly to the absence or presence of a composite fermion. The act of measuring the fermion parity can be seen as projecting the system's state onto one of these sectors. The parameters $p_T$ and $p_F$ could represent the probabilities of measuring even versus odd parity, or the populations in different energy levels associated with the Majorana bound states. The continuous shuttle projection might describe the adiabatic braiding of Majorana modes, a process central to topological quantum computing [[80](https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevB.105.085417), [179](https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/ab3ab60267bf983428a9e4cc907f66fe5dee56d8)]. Such a process induces a unitary rotation on the state space, and the amplitudes of the resulting state can evolve according to trigonometric functions of the braiding time or geometric parameters, matching the form of the shuttle projection formulas. The $τ$ ratio could quantify the degree to which a physical state is decohered or mixed. A perfectly isolated Majorana qubit prepared in a pure state would have $τ=1$, while interaction with an environment leading to decoherence would decrease $τ$, reflecting the loss of quantum coherence and the gain of classical uncertainty. The ability to dynamically stabilize and manipulate Majorana modes experimentally further connects this abstract framework to tangible physical processes [[9](https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevResearch.7.023183), [177](https://journals.aps.org/prresearch/issues/7/2)]. By drawing these analogies, the projective formalisms cease to be mere logical curiosities and become powerful tools for quantifying and predicting phenomena in quantum information processing and topological quantum computation.

The following table summarizes the mapping of key concepts between the three levels, illustrating the structural unity of the B-fixed point framework enhanced with projective formalisms.

| Concept | Logical Level (Belnap's Logic) | Informational Level (SIC-POVM) | Physical Level (Majorana Mode) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Carrier Object $B$ | "Both" value ${t,f}$ [[52](https://philpapers.org/rec/BELAUF)] | SIC-POVM fiducial projector $Π_0$ [[39](https://arxiv.org/html/2007.10483v1)] | Majorana zero mode $γ$ [[79](https://academic.oup.com/ptep/article/2024/8/08C105/7663572)] |
| Involution & Fixed Point | Negation $¬$; $¬{t,f}={t,f}$ [[66](https://www.academia.edu/170602298/SIC_POVMs_a_Stark_Conjecture_and_the_12th_A_Formalization_via_Paraconsistent_Belnap_Multilattices)] | Transpose map $τ$; $τ(Π_0)=Π_0$ [[111](https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Markus-Grassl)] | Particle-Hole conjugation; $γ†=γ$ [[64](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10121601/)] |
| Special †-Frobenius Algebra | Meet ($∧_k$) and diagonal map ($δ$) on bilattice $4$ [[66](https://www.academia.edu/170602298/SIC_POVMs_a_Stark_Conjecture_and_the_12th_A_Formalization_via_Paraconsistent_Belnap_Multilattices)] | Doubling map ($μ$) and its adjoint ($μ†=δ$) on operators [[59](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/236844197_Categories_of_Quantum_and_Classical_Channels)] | Fusion ($μ$) and splitting ($δ$) of modes [[12](https://medium.com/@adnanmasood/quantum-sundays-58-majorana-zero-modes-topological-qubits-and-the-engineering-conditions-for-1e2b5ca3b80c)] |
| State $ψ$ | Element of bilattice $4$ (e.g., ${t}, {f}, {t,f}$) | Density operator $ρ$ in Hilbert space [[103](https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1088/1751-8121/ad2b85)] | Ground state of a fermionic system [[11](https://ncatlab.org/nlab/show/Majorana+zero+mode)] |
| Projection Formula ($p_T$, $p_F$) | $|ψ ∩ {T}| / |ψ|$ (discrete cardinality) [[66](https://www.academia.edu/170602298/SIC_POVMs_a_Stark_Conjecture_and_the_12th_A_Formalization_via_Paraconsistent_Belnap_Multilattices)] | $Tr(ρ B)$ (Born rule probability) [[45](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5627088/)] | Probability of even/odd fermion parity measurement [[82](https://gilkalai.wordpress.com/2025/02/21/majorana-zero-modes-and-topological-qubits/)] |
| Continuous Projection | $cos²(ωθ/4)$ (dynamic state evolution) [[66](https://www.academia.edu/170602298/SIC_POVMs_a_Stark_Conjecture_and_the_12th_A_Formalization_via_Paraconsistent_Belnap_Multilattices)] | Trigonometric amplitude modulation during adiabatic evolution [[152](https://arxiv.org/html/2507.11746v1)] | Rabi oscillation frequency in braiding dynamics [[80](https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevB.105.085417)] |
| Composition Ratio ($τ$) | $p_T + p_F$ (measure of classicality) [[66](https://www.academia.edu/170602298/SIC_POVMs_a_Stark_Conjecture_and_the_12th_A_Formalization_via_Paraconsistent_Belnap_Multilattices)] | Measure of deviation from a completely mixed state [[164](https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevA.111.022224)] | Measure of quantum coherence vs. environmental decoherence [[106](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9858199/)] |

This cross-level comparison demonstrates that the enhanced B-fixed point is not just a high-level analogy but a precise, operational framework. The projective formulas and compositional measures are not arbitrary additions; they are natural extensions of the core categorical idea, providing a quantitative language that is meaningful and applicable in logic, quantum information, and condensed matter physics. They allow for a more nuanced understanding of the fixed point, moving from a static characterization ($μ ∘ δ = id_B$) to a dynamic one that accounts for the flow of information and the composition of states.

## Unification and Implications of the Enhanced Framework

The successful integration of explicit shuttle projection formulas and discrete cardinality-based measures into the logical, informational, and physical descriptions of the B-fixed point culminates in a significantly strengthened and more comprehensive unification. The revised framework transcends a mere statement of structural similarity; it provides a concrete, quantitative language that can be used to analyze and compare phenomena across these traditionally separate domains. The unification is no longer based solely on the abstract equation $μ ∘ δ = id_B$ and the fixed-point property of an involution. Instead, it is grounded in a shared system of projective measurements ($p_T$, $p_F$), compositional analysis ($τ$), and information quantification ($info(ψ)$), all of which emerge naturally from the underlying categorical structure. This synthesis reveals the B-fixed point as a universal principle for modeling systems at a state of maximal informational saturation or paraconsistent equilibrium, where opposing poles coalesce.

A central implication of this enhanced framework is the clarification of the nature of the fixed point $B$ itself. Previously, $B$ was defined primarily by its algebraic stability ($μ ∘ δ = id_B$) and its invariance under an involution. Now, we can characterize $B$ more deeply through its interaction with other states. In the logical case, the fundamental fixed point $B = {T, F}$ is uniquely characterized by the property that its projections onto the constituent poles are equal ($p_T = p_F = 1/2$) and that its classicality ratio is maximal ($τ = 1$). States with $p_T ≠ p_F$ or $τ < 1$ represent departures from this idealized fixed point, embodying varying degrees of asymmetry or non-classicality. This reframes the fixed point not as an isolated object, but as the center of a phase space of possible states, with $p_T$, $p_F$, and $τ$ serving as coordinates. The continuous shuttle projection formulas describe trajectories through this phase space, parameterized by $θ$, showing how a system can evolve from a pure classical state ($T$ or $F$) to the balanced, paraconsistent state $B$, and then to the opposite classical state ($F$ or $T$). This dynamic view is crucial for applications in computation and control, where steering a system towards or through the fixed point state is often the goal.

Furthermore, the framework provides a powerful tool for comparing and interpolating between different logical and physical systems. The introduction of the $τ$ ratio as a measure of classicality allows for a continuous classification of logics. A system with $τ=1$ behaves according to classical Boolean logic, while a system with $τ<1$ exhibits paraconsistent or quantum-like features, where information can be incomplete or contradictory without leading to triviality [[51](https://plato.stanford.edu/entries/logic-paraconsistent/)]. This provides a quantitative basis for exploring the spectrum of logics that lie between classical and intuitionistic or paraconsistent ones [[119](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/373629780_From_Belnap-Dunn_four-valued_logic_to_six-valued_logics_of_evidence_and_truth), [147](https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.09978)]. Similarly, in quantum mechanics, $τ$ can be used to distinguish between classical mixtures and genuine quantum superpositions, offering a metric for "quantumness." This capability to quantify the departure from classical behavior is a significant advance, enabling a more nuanced analysis of complex systems in computer science, information theory, and physics. The resolution of the ambiguity concerning the empty set $N$ is another key improvement. By noting that the normalized ratios $p_T$ and $p_F$ are undefined for $|N|=0$, the document gains mathematical rigor, correctly stating that no information can be projected from an empty context [[66](https://www.academia.edu/170602298/SIC_POVMs_a_Stark_Conjecture_and_the_12th_A_Formalization_via_Paraconsistent_Belnap_Multilattices)]. This prevents ill-defined statements and strengthens the logical consistency of the framework.

Ultimately, the unification achieved is profound because it shows that the mechanisms for handling information are governed by the same fundamental principles across different scales and domains. The discrete counting argument for probability based on set cardinality in logic [[66](https://www.academia.edu/170602298/SIC_POVMs_a_Stark_Conjecture_and_the_12th_A_Formalization_via_Paraconsistent_Belnap_Multilattices)] provides the conceptual seed from which the continuous, amplitude-based probabilities of quantum mechanics grow. The algebraic structure of the Frobenius algebra, with its splitting and merging operations, provides the common ground upon which these different notions of probability can be built. The involution, whether it is logical negation, Hermitian adjoint, or charge conjugation, defines the axis along which information is processed, and the fixed point is the unique state where this processing leads to self-coincidence. This deep structural identity suggests that insights gained in one domain can inform the others. For example, techniques for controlling decoherence in quantum systems (related to maintaining $τ$) may find inspiration in methods for resolving contradictions in paraconsistent databases. Conversely, the elegant categorical formulation of quantum protocols using Frobenius algebras can provide new perspectives on logical inference and computational processes [[56](https://ncatlab.org/nlab/show/quantum+information+theory+via+dagger-compact+categories), [59](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/236844197_Categories_of_Quantum_and_Classical_Channels)]. The framework presented here, by weaving concrete quantitative tools into the abstract categorical tapestry, provides a robust and fertile ground for such cross-pollination of ideas, paving the way for a truly unified understanding of information, logic, and reality.
